General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD).

courses.title: The Ethnographic & Literary Imagination
courses.desc: The ethnographic and literary imagination. Relationship between fiction & anthropology, narrative form, modalities of ethnographic encounter, social & historical phenomena, aesthetics, poetics, language, and the question of representation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Language & Culture
courses.desc: Culture, cognition, meaning, and interpretation; language and the classification of experience; communication and learning in crosscultural perspective.
courses.prereqs: ANT 004 or LIN 001 recommended; ANT 002 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Special Topics in Medical Anthropology
courses.desc: Introduction to critical medical anthropology. Topics include anthropological analysis of bio-medicine, psychiatry, systems of knowledge and healing, the body, emotions, and clinical encounters in a cross-cultural perspective.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: STS 121.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Economic Anthropology
courses.desc: The varieties of production, exchange, and consumption behavior in precapitalist economies, their interaction with culture and social-political organization, and the theories that account for these phenomena. The effects of capitalism on precapitalist sectors.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 122. (Former ANT 122.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Capitalism & Power
courses.desc: Theorizations of economy and society. The rise of modern capitalism and new social and political formations. Relationships between value and violence, subjectivity, the unconscious, money, imperialism and different understandings of exchange and the political.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Resistance, Rebellion, & Popular Movements
courses.desc: Analysis of popular protest in Third World and indigenous societies ranging from covert resistance to national revolts. Comparative case studies and theories of peasant rebellions, millenarian movements, social bandits, Indian "wars", ethnic and regional conflicts, gender and class conflicts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 123B. (Former ANT 123B.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Religion in Society & Culture
courses.desc: Discussion of anthropological theories of religion with emphasis on non-literate societies. Survey of shamanism, magic and witchcraft, ritual and symbols, and religious movements. Extensive discussion of ethnographic examples and analysis of social functions of religious institutions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Postmodernism(s) & Culture
courses.desc: Crucial theories of modernity and post-modernity. How postmodernism is distinct from modernism, why it is related to the collapse of certainty about our collective reality and what it reveals about the status of reason, the self, and collective experience. Readings draw from various philosophical-theoretical, artistic and political literatures.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Anthropology of Development
courses.desc: Theories of development and current critiques. Colonial legacies and post-colonial realities. Roles of the state and NGOs, population migrations, changing gender identities, cash-earning strategies, and sustainability issues. Stresses importance of cultural understandings in development initiatives. Case studies emphasizing non-industrial societies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 126. (Former ANT 126.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Women & Development
courses.desc: Current Third World and Western development issues concerning women in agriculture, industry, international division of labor, political movements, revolutions, politics of health, education, family and reproduction. Impact of colonialism, capitalism, the world system, and international feminism on women and development.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): No credit if taken ANT 131.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Urban Anthropology
courses.desc: Survey of approaches to urban living: political structures, organization of labor, class relations, world views. The evolution of urban life and its contemporary dilemmas. Cross-cultural comparisons discussed through case studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Kinship & Social Organization: From Clans to Countries
courses.desc: Family, marriage, household and social organization from a cross-cultural and evolutionary perspective. Emphasis on case studies that illustrate human variation, theories that account for this variation, and recent advances in the treatment of this data.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 128. (Former ANT 128.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Health & Medicine in a Global Context
courses.desc: Recent works in medical anthropology and the science studies of medicine dealing with social and cultural aspects of global health issues such as AIDS, pandemics, clinical trials, cultural differences in illnesses, diabetes, organ trafficking, medical technologies, illness narratives, and others.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Cross Listing: STS 129.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Cultural Dimensions of Globalization
courses.desc: Cultural dimensions of recent economic and political developments frequently termed "globalization."
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Migration & the Politics of Place & Identity
courses.desc: Internal and international migration from an anthropological perspective, including causes, processes, and political, economic, and cultural effects of spatial mobility and displacement. Emphasizes the interplay of identity, place, and power in diverse cultural and historical contexts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 123D. (Former ANT 123D.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Ecology & Politics
courses.desc: Analysis of the complex interactions between ecological dynamics and political processes employing the emerging approach of political ecology. Case studies of environmental degradation (e.g., desertification, logging, mineral extraction, petroleum, water) from various cultural and geographic regions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Psychological Anthropology
courses.desc: History of the relationship between anthropology and psychoanalysis. Exploration of anthropology of emotions, colonial psychology, contemporary ethno-psychiatry, studies on personhood, possession, magic, altered states, subjectivity, and definitions of the normal and the pathological in different contexts and cultures.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Anthropology of Ocean Worlds
courses.desc: Exploration of various oceanic cultures and their engagement with the sea. Piracy, smuggling, exchange, maritime legal regimes, offshore policing, media infrastructures, and ocean ecologies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Buddhism in Global Culture
courses.desc: Buddhist meditation and ritual as a cultural system that adapts to global and local forces of change. Anthropological theory and method in understanding global culture transmission, including Buddhist reform movements in Asia and Buddhist practice in the West.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 50 students.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Media Anthropology
courses.desc: Examining human practices through their inscription in old and new media; evaluating the emergent fields of “cyber” and “digital” anthropology; and problematizing terms and concepts routinely deployed in studies of media worlds (platform, social media, hologram, algorithm, remediation, curation, animation).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Ethnographic Film
courses.desc: Overview of the use of film in anthropology and its advantages and limitations in comparison to written ethnographic descriptions. Essential features of ethnographic films. Film production in anthropological research and problems encountered in producing films in the field.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Meditation & Culture
courses.desc: Study and practice of the relation between meditation and cultural conditioning; comparison of Buddhist practice with other cultural constructions of mind, body, brain, thought, emotion, and self.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 50 students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnographic Research Methods in Anthropology
courses.desc: Basic concepts in and approaches to ethnographic field research. Problem formulation, research design, qualitative and quantitative data collection procedures, and techniques for organizing, retrieving, and analyzing information. Ethnographic description and constructed inference. Students will organize and conduct individual research projects.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Race, Class, Gender Systems
courses.desc: Comparative analysis of class/race/gender inequality, concentrating on the ways in which beliefs about descent, "blood," and biological difference interact with property and marital systems to affect the distribution of power in society.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 139. (Former ANT 139.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Gender & Sexuality
courses.desc: Gender and sexuality in foraging bands, horticultural and pastoral tribes, agricultural and industrial states. Debates on cultural evolution and distribution of gender hierarchies. Impact of politics, economics, religion, social practices, women's movements on gender and sexuality. Culture, nature and sexuality.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 130. (Former ANT 130.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Dispossession & Dynamism in Africa
courses.desc: Critical issues in the anthropology of Africa using history, ethnography, and literature. Representations of Africa, wealth in people, missionization, anti-colonial resistance, post/colonialism, resource extraction, and digital technologies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken ANT 140B.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Indigenous Peoples of the Arctic
courses.desc: Comparative history of Indigenous peoples across the circumpolar arctic. Arctic ecosystems, language, social structure, subsistence, gender, religion, art, health, colonialism, contemporary issues, climate change, and resilience.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): No credit if taken ANT 141C.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Peoples of the Middle East
courses.desc: Peoples of the Middle East (including North Africa). Discussions of class relations, kinship organization, sex/gender systems, religious beliefs and behavior, ethnic relations, political systems. Impact of world systems, political and religious movements and social change. (Former ANT 136.)
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Ethnology of Southeast Asia
courses.desc: Patterns of culture and social organization from prehistory to the present, in the context of historical, ecological, economic, and political settings. Emphasis on the relation of ethnic minorities to national states.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Contemporary Societies & Cultures of Latin America
courses.desc: Introduction to contemporary social structure of Latin America. Origins, maintenance and changes in inequality: economic responses to poverty, sociocultural responses to discrimination, and political responses to powerlessness.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Performance, Embodiment, & Space in South Asia
courses.desc: South Asian cultures and societies with a focus on performance, embodiment, and space from several disciplinary fields. Topics may include colonialism, nationalism, religious traditions, media, popular culture, cities, social movements, modernity, body-cultures, identity, gender, and diasporas.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Topics in the Anthropology of Europe
courses.desc: Recent ethnographies of different nation-states and socio-political spaces in Europe. Topics include the question of old and new boundaries, historical and contemporary constructions of Europe, migration and ethnicity, citizenship, belonging, multiculturalism, and post/socialisms.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Modern South Asia Cinema
courses.desc: South Asian cinema of last 100 years in the context of cultural, social, and political changes. South Asian history, Independence, Partition, urban life, class, migration, postcolonial identity, diaspora, gender, sexuality, religion, sport, performance, etc.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Film Viewing 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: MSA 131B, CTS 146B.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Culture & Political Economy in Contemporary China
courses.desc: Examining contemporary Chinese culture and political economy through reading ethnographic studies on recent transformations in rural and urban Chinese society. Special attention is given to state power, popular culture, spatial mobility, city space, and gender.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Evolution & Human Health
courses.desc: Potential health issues related to human anatomical and physiological features through the lens of human evolutionary history and recent changes (e.g., industrialization).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Primate Evolution
courses.desc: Origin and relationships of the prosimians, monkeys, and apes.
courses.prereqs: ANT 001 or BIS 002B or BIS 002C or EVE 010 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Human Evolution
courses.desc: Nature and results of the evolutionary processes involved in the formation and differentiation of humankind.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Human Genetics: Mutation & Migration
courses.desc: Introduction to human genetics. Principles of inheritance, the human genome, population genetics, mutation, genetic diversity, using DNA to study ancient human history, personal genomics. Human genetics as a tool to understand the patterns and processes of human migration. Introduction to the major concepts in human genetic and genomic research.
courses.prereqs: (BIO 001 C- or better, BIO 001L C- or better) or MCB 010 C- or better; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: The Evolution of Primate Behavior
courses.desc: Examines ecological diversity and evolution of social systems of prosimians, monkeys, and apes, placing the social behavior of the primates in the context of appropriate ecological and evolutionary theory.
courses.prereqs: ANT 001 or ANT 054 or EVE 010 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Primate Behavior: Methods & Experimental Design
courses.desc: Scientific methods of studying, describing and analyzing the behavior and ecology of primates.
courses.prereqs: (ANT 054 or ANT 154A or NPB 102); (STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 032 or STA 100 or SOC 046B); ANT 154CL (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to upper division ANT majors; concurrent enrollment in ANT 154CL required.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Laboratory in Primate Behavior
courses.desc: Design and conduct of scientific "field studies" of the behavior of group-living primates at the California National Primate Research Center.
courses.prereqs: (ANT 054 or ANT 154A or NPB 102); (STA 013 or STA 013V or  STA 013Y or STA 032 or STA 100 or SOC 046B); ANT 154C concurrent enrollment required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 6 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to upper division Anthropology majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Oral Skills (OL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Primate Conservation Biology
courses.desc: Study of the taxonomic, ecological and cultural diversity of Primates and how human activities impact tropical ecosystems. Emphasis on case studies and applied research methods. Includes discussion about career opportunities in conservation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Human Osteology
courses.desc: Human skeleton from archaeological, forensic, and paleontological perspectives, including anatomical nomenclature, variation with sex and age, function, evolution, growth, and development of bones and teeth. Hands-on study and identification of human skeletal remains.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Not open to students who have previously completed ANT 156.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Advanced Human Osteology
courses.desc: Human skeletons from archaeological, forensic, and paleontological contexts. Bone and tooth structure, growth, and development; measurement, statistics, and biomechanics; assessment of age, sex, weight, height, and ancestry; and indicators of illness, injuries, diet, and activities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Advanced Human Genetics
courses.desc: Advanced concepts in human genetics and genomics. Identification of genes underlying human health and disease. Use of genomic data in clinical settings and examination of biases associated with 'personalized medicine." Emphasis on current human genomic technology and critical reading of scientific papers.
courses.prereqs: ANT 153 or BIS 101 or BIS 101V or EVE 102 or EVE 131 or EVE 175 or MCB 162 or MCB 182.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Advanced Human Genetics Lab
courses.desc: Computer lab in human genetics and genomics. Emphasizes hands-on engagement with human genetic/genomic data. Ancestry analysis, pedigrees, de novo Mendelian disease.
courses.prereqs: ANT 153 or EVE 102 or EVE 131 or EVE 175 or MCB 162 or MCB 182; concurrent enrollment in ANT 157 encouraged.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion/Laboratory 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: The Evolution of Sex: A Biological Perspective
courses.desc: Current theoretical frameworks for explaining the evolution of sex differences and for understanding the interrelationship between biological processes and cultural construction of gender roles.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Disease Outbreaks in Humans and Other Primates
courses.desc: Impacts of infectious diseases on human and other primate populations, illustrated with past and present epidemiological studies from around the world. Theoretical concepts and applied questions, from local outbreaks to pandemics.
courses.prereqs: ANT 001 or ANT 001Y or BIS 002B; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Neandertals & Modern Human Origins
courses.desc: Origins, evolution, and disappearance of Neandertals. Emergence of humans like us in both anatomy and behavior. Interpretation of the fossil and archaeological records of Europe and Africa. Genetics of living and fossil humans.
courses.prereqs: ANT 001 or ANT 001Y or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Archeological Theory & Method
courses.desc: History of the philosophical propositions and conceptual foundations of archaeological theories from the 18th century to present, and their relationship to the research techniques, procedures, and strategies of archaeological methods.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Writing Experience (WE); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Ice-Age Settlement of the Americas
courses.desc: Critical evaluation of evidence related to human settlement of the Americas in the late Pleistocene/early Holocene (~40,000–8,000 years ago). Examines archaeological, genetic, biological, and paleoenvironmental data concerning early migrations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: European Archaeology: First Peopling to the Bronze Age
courses.desc: Survey of the archaeology of Europe from its earliest inhabitants, to the Neandertals and humans, and through early agricultural and complex societies. Analysis and interpretation of the record for understanding major processes and transitions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Andean Archaeology
courses.desc: Archaeology of the Andean region, especially Peru, from the earliest hunting and gathering societies through the Inca Empire. Use of archaeological data to reconstruct ancient human adaptations to the varied Andean environments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: California Archaeology
courses.desc: Discussion and analysis of archaeology and archaeological practice in California. Emphasis on precontact periods and earliest contact, from the late Pleistocene through to time of the Spanish Missions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s); Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: African Archaeology: From Australopithecines to Great Zimbabwe
courses.desc: African archaeological record from early human ancestors, through modern human origins, into early agricultural and complex societies, the Bantu expansion, and early state formation. Focus on major processes and transitions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Hunter-Gatherers
courses.desc: Study and interpretation of the ancient and modern lifeway in which peoples support themselves with primitive technologies and without benefit of domesticated plants and animals.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Zooarchaeology
courses.desc: Theories and methods for studying animal skeletal remains from archaeological sites. Identification and quantification of zooarchaeological material, cultural and natural processes affecting animal bones pre- and postburial, and use of faunal remains for determining past human diets and past environments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to junior or senior standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Archaeological Field Methods
courses.desc: Survey of archeological field methods and techniques. Strategies for survey and site location, mapping of artifacts and features, geophysical techniques, and hand excavation and analysis of stratigraphy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Field Course in Archeological Methods
courses.desc: On-site course using archaeological methods and techniques held at a field location in the western United States, generally California or Nevada. Incorporates basic methods of archaeological survey, mapping, and excavation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Fieldwork 18 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Archaeometry
courses.desc: Scientific techniques used to study the chemical and physical properties of archaeological materials. Types of anthropological questions that can be addressed with different methods. Preparation and analysis of archaeological materials.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Laboratory in Archeological Analysis
courses.desc: Museum preparation, advanced field investigation, and guidance in preparation of museum material for publication.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 4 hour(s), Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Evolution of Human Technology
courses.desc: Long-term evolutionary dynamics in human technology and technological systems as informed by the archaeological record, including lithics, ceramics, wood, basketry, and metallurgy. Emphasis on the significance of material resources in ancient human adaptation, economics, settlement patterns, and culture change. Lab experiments to demonstrate particular concepts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Lithic Analysis
courses.desc: Basic concepts of lithic analysis. General introduction on the place of stone tool technology in the archeological record. Physics, terminology and methodological concepts behind the study of stone tools. Review of the development of stone tool technology from its emergence.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Lab 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Cultural Resource Management in Archaeology
courses.desc: Examination of legal foundations and goals of cultural resource management in the United States, with a focus on archaeological resources. Review of state and federal regulations, guidelines for assessing eligibility for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, professional practices to preserve and mitigate damage to resources, and public outreach practices.
courses.prereqs: ANT 003; or consent of instructor; ANT 170 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Forensic Archaeology Field Course
courses.desc: Application of archaeological field methods to data recovery in forensic or medico-legal cases. Training in site survey, mapping, digitization, excavation, and evidence collection strategies. Field locations to be determined; international travel may be require
courses.prereqs: ANT 003; consent of instructor; ANT 056 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Fieldwork 9 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH).

courses.title: Topics in Anthropology
courses.desc: Intensive treatment of a special anthropological topic or problem.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Term Paper, Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Internship in Anthropology
courses.desc: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Anthropology under the supervision of a member of the faculty.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-36 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to Anthropology majors.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 12 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Special Study for Honors Students
courses.desc: Independent study of an anthropological problem involving the writing of an honors thesis.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; open only to majors of senior standing who qualify for honors program.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 3-15 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 12 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Tutoring in Anthropology
courses.desc: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing with major in Anthropology and consent of Department Chairperson.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Tutorial 1-5 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Directed reading and group discussion of selected anthropological problems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for advanced undergraduates.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: History of Anthropology
courses.desc: Historical development of socio-cultural theory within anthropology, from mid-19th to mid-20th centuries. Focus on original theory texts in context of historical developments in the field as a whole.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Critical Readings in Ethnography
courses.desc: Critical readings of selected ethnographies that examine a wide range of important topics and analytical issues in social and cultural anthropology. Emphasis on how and why ethnographic writing has changed over time and its relationship with contemporary theoretical explorations.
courses.prereqs: Graduate student in Anthropology or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: History & Theory of Biological Anthropology
courses.desc: History of thought in biological anthropology and analysis of major theoretical problems in the field. Suggested for all first-year graduate students lacking intensive preparation in biological anthropology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: History & Theory of Archaeology
courses.desc: History of archaeology and archaeological theory and analysis of archaeological research methodology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Generally restricted to graduate students; outstanding undergraduates with extensive training in archaeology with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Anthropological Theory
courses.desc: Advanced consideration of fundamental issues in anthropological theory. Emphasis on critical examination of major contemporary debates between proponents of competing theories.
courses.prereqs: ANT 002; ANT 137; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: History & Theory in Anthropological Linguistics
courses.desc: History of thought in anthropological linguistics. Consideration of the historical development of fundamental ideas in anthropological linguistics, of major theoretical issues, and of research methodology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research Design & Method in Social Anthropology
courses.desc: Formulation of research problems and preparation of research proposals; relationships between theory and method, funding, pre-fieldwork preparations, entering the community, field research techniques, and problems of ethics; intensive work on proposal writing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnographic Writing
courses.desc: Relationship between conducting participant observation of others and writing it up, emphasizing the processual rift between the reality of fieldwork and its written representation. Study of various literary genres and textual strategies used in cultural anthropology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Writing & Research Design in Evolutionary Anthropology
courses.desc: Guided preparation of a Ph.D. dissertation proposal or MA thesis/report. Discussion of literature review, hypothesis testing, research design and grant writing as relates to anthropology. Culminates in an oral capstone presentation to the department
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Aspects of Culture Structure
courses.desc: Analysis of various phases of culture, such as religion, economics, law, and folklore.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Political Ecology
courses.desc: Interdisciplinary seminar evaluating contributions from ecological anthropology, political economy, cultural constructivism, postmodernism, and feminism towards development of theories of political ecology. Historical relationships between local/global power structures, environmental degradation, and resistance movements. Case studies of desertification, deforestation, mining, conservation, development.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problems in Archeological Method
courses.desc: Techniques for analyzing archeological data; application to various prehistoric cultures.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quantitative Modeling in Archaeology
courses.desc: Examination of the nature of archaeological data with a focus on the quantitative and statistical techniques available to model, analyze, display, and make sense of such data.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Topics in New World Prehistory
courses.desc: Advanced study on current problems in New World Prehistory and archaeology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated only when material is unique for that student and with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Topics in Old World Prehistory
courses.desc: Advanced study on current problems in Old World prehistory and archaeology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated only when material is unique for that student and with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Field Course in Linguistics
courses.desc: Techniques of eliciting, recording, and analyzing; work with a native speaker.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Rural Transformation in Postcolonial Societies
courses.desc: Problems of rural transformation arising out of political and economic interaction between national elites and rural regional and local populations under varying conditions of induced change in postcolonial societies. Attention given to the implications of this interaction for rapid economic growth.
courses.prereqs: ANT 223; ANT 265; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cities & Citizenship
courses.desc: Explores the nature of modern cities, urban socioeconomic life, and urban culture and politics from an anthropological perspective.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Economic Anthropology
courses.desc: Selected current methodological and theoretical problems in the analysis of nonindustrial economic systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problems in Comparative Religion
courses.desc: Advanced study of current problems in the anthropological study of religion.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: State & Nation in the Modern World
courses.desc: A presentation of current anthropological theories of the origins and nature of the modern nation-state in both the First and Third Worlds, with special reference to state ideology (nationalism) and forms of control.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Consciousness & Resistance
courses.desc: Consideration of approaches to the study of social inequality, and responses of subordinated groups. Emphasis on situating approaches to contemporary social theory, concrete research problems, and political strategies. Topics: formation of consciousness and identity; collective action, accommodation to frontal resistance.
courses.prereqs: Completion of first-year graduate work or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Culture & Power
courses.desc: Exploration of one of the core paradigms within contemporary anthropological inquiry, "culture and power." Focus on how distinct theoretical perspectives–Marxism, post-Marxism, structuralism, post-structuralism, and feminism–have examined the mutually constitutive nature of culture and power.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Gender, Identity, & Self
courses.desc: Intersections of gender, identity, and selfhood cross-culturally and historically. How the self is feminized and masculinized, and interfaces with sexual, race, class, work, national, minority, and majority identities under different historical, cultural, and social structural conditions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Family Systems & Reproduction: Theory & Comparisons
courses.desc: Comparative examination of family systems in historical context and of reproductive behaviors and strategizing. A major theme is how family-system norms specify the relative desirability of differently configured offspring sets. Cases are drawn from Western Europe and South and East Asia.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing in one of the social sciences including History.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1.50 hour(s), Seminar 1.50 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Political Movements
courses.desc: Interdisciplinary approach to political movements of protest, reform, and revolution emphasizing historical comparison and evaluation of major theoretical approaches including world systems, resource mobilization, state & culture, rational choice, moral economy, social class and gender.
courses.prereqs: Completion of first-year graduate work recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problems in African Society & Culture
courses.desc: Diachronic analyses of traditional institutions in sub-Saharan Africa.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Topics in North American Ethnology
courses.desc: Advanced study on current problems in North American ethnography and culture history.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnology of Northern & Central Asia
courses.desc: Lectures on the culture aboriginally found north of the Caucasus-Korea line. Supervised study of the primary and secondary sources. Work with informants when available.
courses.prereqs: Reading knowledge of German, Russian, Chinese, or Japanese.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnology of Europe
courses.desc: Supervised study of the primary and secondary sources dealing with the ethnography and ethnology of the peoples of Europe. Emphasis upon folk, peasant, and minority groups.
courses.prereqs: Reading knowledge of a European language other than English.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Topics in Chinese Culture & Society
courses.desc: Selected topics in the anthropology of Chinese society. Focus on one or more of the following topics: state-society dynamics, family and gender, city formation and urban life, social movement, labor politics, and religion and ideology in Chinese society.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing in the social sciences, history, or the humanities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Behavioral Ecology of Primates
courses.desc: Concepts, issues, and hypotheses in primate behavioral ecology, with emphasis on the social and ecological determinants and consequences of variation in social organization for individuals.
courses.prereqs: ANT 154A (can be concurrent); or the equivalent, graduate standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Human Evolution Seminar
courses.desc: Study of selected topics in human evolutionary studies. Each year, focuses on one or more of the following: molecular evolution, primate evolutionary biology, Tertiary hominoids, Australopithecus, Homo erectus, archaic Homo sapiens, brain evolution.
courses.prereqs: ANT 152; and consent of instructor, or the equivalent of ANT 152.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Seminar in Human Genomics
courses.desc: In-depth study of current topics in human genomics including genetic diversity, migration, phenotypic evolution and genetic associations with disease. Focus on population genetic theory. Topic changes yearly.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to graduate students.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 3 time(s) when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Current Issues in Primate Sociobiology
courses.desc: Analysis of primate behavior, with particular emphasis on preparation for field studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Primate Conservation Biology
courses.desc: Application of understanding of primate biology to conservation of primates and their habitat. Topics include evolutionary anthropology, behavioral ecology, biogeography, macroecology, population biology, and socio-ecology of primates.
courses.prereqs: ANT 154; Graduate standing, or upper division undergraduates with consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 10 students.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) when term paper differs.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Modeling the evolution of social behavior
courses.desc: Tools and topics in modeling the evolution of social behavior in humans and other animals. Game theory, basic population genetics, animal conflict, altruism, reciprocity, signaling, and group selection.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Evolution & Human Behavior
courses.desc: Exploration of the links between behavioral ecological theory and human cultural variation, focusing on reproduction, marriage, parental investment and family structure; implications of evolutionary theory for social organization in human communities, historical and contemporary.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing, or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Human Applications of Foraging Theory
courses.desc: Foraging theory models and their use in ethnographic and archaeological analyses of human behavior, with a focus on hunter-gatherers and resource selection, patch use, population and habitat, central places, sharing, stochastic processes, population dynamics, and conservation behavior.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ANT 258.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Language, Performance, & Power
courses.desc: Exploration of the intersection between linguistic and social theories in the language-state relation and the performance of identity. Ideological sources of language differentiation; nation-building and linguistic difference. Political economic, sociolinguistic, and ethnographic approaches to understanding linguistic inequality.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing or consent of instructor.
Cross Listing: LIN 265.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Anthropology Colloquium Seminar
courses.desc: Reports and discussions of recent advances in the four subfields of anthropology. Presented by guest speakers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated up to a total of 6 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Human Behavioral Ecology
courses.desc: Topically focused, critical discussion of current and emerging research in the field of human behavioral ecology, giving special attention to theory, concepts, models, and methods for the evolutionary analysis of ethnographic and archaeological evidence.
courses.prereqs: ANT 261 or ANT 262 or ANT 263; and consent of instructor, or comparable experience in anthropology, or related disciplines.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) when topic differs & material covered is substantially different.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Seminar in Linguistic Anthropology
courses.desc: Selected topics in linguistic anthropology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Group Study
courses.desc: Group study.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Research
courses.desc: Research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.desc: Dissertation research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Teaching Anthropology
courses.desc: Intellectual and practical elements of college teaching in the field of Anthropology, from curriculum design and the syllabus through grading and course evaluations, including  classroom and information technology methods, and problems and rewards of teaching in higher education.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing in Anthropology or closely related discipline.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Practice 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.desc: Teaching assistant training practicum.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 3-36 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Metal Properties & Fabrication
courses.desc: Study of metal properties and of techniques for fabricating in metal. Physical principles, design considerations, effects of techniques on quality and appearance, and evaluation procedures. Experience in working with metal.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Field Equipment Operation
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Operation, adjustment, and troubleshooting of farm tractors and field equipment. Principles of operation, equipment terminology and uses of tilling, cultivating, thinning, and planting equipment. Typical sequences in cropping practices.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Field Equipment Welding
courses.desc: Intermediate welding to include hardfacing and inert gas welding. Class projects on repair and fabrication by welding. Troubleshooting and major repair of field equipment.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Introduction to Unmanned Aerial Systems for Agriculture & Environmental Science
courses.desc: Operation, use and impact of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) for applications in agriculture and environmental assessment. Principles of unmanned flight, vehicle systems, safety, and airspace regulations for communicating spatial relationships. UAS sensors, data acquisition, management, processing, visualization and analysis. Ethics and professional responsibilities in operations and public communication, and potential impacts for agricultural and environmental policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to College of Agricultural & Environmental Sciences students.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Engine Technology
courses.desc: Principles of 2-stroke cycle, 4-stroke cycle gasoline and 4-stroke cycle diesel engine construction and operation. Engine systems, performance, troubleshooting, and overhaul.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Irrigation Systems & Water Management
courses.desc: Soil and plant aspects of irrigation and drainage. Soil-water principles including water storage and movement, plant response to irrigation, water use by crops, irrigation systems (i.e., micro-irrigation, sprinkler irrigation and surface irrigation), and related salinity and water quality impacts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: ESM 110, HYD 110.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Animal Housing & Environment Management
courses.desc: Optimal structures and environments for animal growth and comfort; heat and moisture transfer principles; heating, cooling, ventilating principles and equipment; animal housing design; environmental regulations and waste management practices.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Equipment & Technology for Small Farms
courses.desc: Types and characteristics of agricultural equipment and technologies appropriate for small commercial farming. Adjustment and calibration of equipment. Selection of and budgeting for equipment.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: IAD 142.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
courses.desc: Basic concepts, principles, and methods of GIS are presented. Data structures, database design, GIS data creation, GPS, and spatial analysis. May be taught abroad.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to Landscape Architecture and Sustainable Environmental Design majors.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ABT 180/PLS 180, ABT 181N; LDA 150, LED 150, ABT 150.
Cross Listing: LDA 150.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Water Quality Management for Aquaculture
courses.desc: Basic principles of water chemistry and water treatment processes as they relate to aquacultural systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Aquaculture Systems Engineering
courses.desc: Design of aquacultural systems: design methodology, principles of fluid mechanics, site selection and facility planning, management operations, computer modeling.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Oral Skills (OL); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Irrigation Practices for an Urban Environment
courses.desc: Basic design, installation, and operation principles of irrigation systems for turf and landscape: golf courses, parks, highways, public buildings, etc. Emphasis on hardware association with sprinkler and drip/trickle systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Project.
Cross Listing: SAF 165.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Concepts & Methods in Geographic Information Systems
courses.desc: Data representation and analysis in geographic information systems (GIS). Creation of spatial data sets from analog and digital sources such as aerial photography and maps; data structures, data management, database design, georeferencing, georectification, surface models, analysis, and spatial data visualization.
courses.prereqs: LDA 150 or ABT 150; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Lab 8 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Environmental Analysis Using GIS
courses.desc: Ecosystem and landscape modeling with emphasis on hydrology and solute transport. Spatial analysis of environmental risk analysis including ecological risk assessment, natural resource management. Spatial database structures, scripting, data models, and error analysis in GIS.
courses.prereqs: ABT 150 or LDA 150; or equivalent GIS experience and skills; general biology and/or ecology courses recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: HYD 182.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Research Conference for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.desc: Research conferences for specialized study in applied biological systems technology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Tutoring in Applied Biological Systems Technology
courses.desc: Tutoring individual students, leading small voluntary discussion groups, or assisting the instructor in laboratories affiliated with one of the department's regular courses.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Tutorial.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Path to Zero Net Energy
courses.desc: Zero Net Energy concepts and social, technical, economic, and environmental considerations. Multidisciplinary research and analysis for clients.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Term Paper/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to upper division or graduate students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Pest Control Practices
courses.desc: Practical and theoretical considerations of pest control systems and techniques. Design, selection, and use of mechanical systems for field, orchard, greenhouse, and vector control use. Biological, legal, and environmental considerations in pest control and pesticide application.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Selected Topic in Applied Biological Systems Technology: Agricultural & Natural Resources
courses.desc: Special topic.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-5 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Selected Topics in Applied Biological Systems Technology: Biotechnology
courses.desc: Special topic.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-5 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Selected Topics in Applied Biological Systems Technology: Food Technology
courses.desc: Special topic.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-5 hour(s).

courses.desc: Introduction to the fundamentals of modern cosmology, humanity’s changing view of the Universe, and our current understanding of its origin and evolution.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed any quarter of the PHY 009 series or the PHY 009H series, or any upper-division physics course.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Introduction to Stars, Galaxies, & the Universe
courses.desc: Non-mathematical introduction to astrophysics of the Universe beyond our solar system using concepts of modern physics.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken AST 002, the former AST 010, any quarter of PHY 009 or PHY 009H, or any upper division physics course (other than PHY 137 or PHY 160).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Observational Astronomy Lab
courses.desc: Introduction to observations of the night sky using small telescopes in nighttime laboratory.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 2.50 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken AST 002 or AST 010.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Astronomy of the Solar System
courses.desc: Introduction to naked eye and telescopic observations of events in the night sky: positions of sun, moon, planets throughout the year. Historical perspective on how our understanding of the solar system evolved to current non-mathematical astrophysical interpretation of planetary systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken AST 002, any quarter of PHY 009 or PHY 009H, or any upper division PHY course (other than PHY 137 or PHY 160).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Introduction to Modern Astronomy & Astrophysics
courses.desc: Description and interpretation of astronomical phenomena using the laws of modern physics and observations by modern astronomical instruments. Gravity, relativity, electromagnetic radiation, atomic and nuclear processes in relation to the structure and evolution of stars, galaxies and the universe.
courses.prereqs: Good facility in high school physics and mathematics (algebra and trigonometry).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 2.50 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open to students who have received credit for AST 002, AST 010G, or AST 010L.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Global Climate Change
courses.desc: Scientific concepts needed to understand climate and climate change. Principles of regional variations in climate. Understanding observed seasonal, decadal and millennial changes. Analysis of the Antarctic ozone hole, El Nino and human-induced global warming.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Fundamentals of Atmospheric Pollution
courses.desc: Effects of human emissions on the atmosphere: smog, ozone pollution, and ozone depletion; indoor air pollution; global warming; acid rain. Impacts of these problems on the earth, ecosystems, and humans. Strategies to reduce atmospheric pollution.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Severe & Unusual Weather
courses.desc: Introduction to physical principles of severe and unusual weather: flood, blizzards, thunderstorms, lightning, tornadoes, and hurricanes. Emphasis on scientific perspective and human context. Not open to students who have received credit for ATM 100. (Former ATM 100.)
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Introduction to Atmospheric Science
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Fundamental principles of the physics, chemistry, and fluid dynamics underlying weather and climate. Solar radiation, the greenhouse effect, and the thermal budget of the Earth. Clouds and their formation, convection, precipitation, mid-latitude storm systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL).
