courses.desc: Probability theory; stochastic processes/random fields (time/frequency domain description, stationarity, mean square calculus, multivariate processes); response of linear systems under stochastic excitations (single-/multi-DOF systems, time/frequency domain, state space approach); reliability-based structural design (first-excursion and fatigue failures); applications to earthquake and wind engineering.
courses.prereqs: Graduate level course in (deterministic) Structural Dynamics such as ECI 213 required (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Concrete Structures
courses.desc: Ductility of reinforced concrete; strength of two-way slabs; modified compression field theory.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Design of Steel Structures
courses.desc: Review of Load and Resistance Factor Design (LRFD); design of indeterminate systems; moment frames and bracing systems; connection design; seismic design of steel structures; direct analysis method for stability design; and performance assessment of steel structures.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Prestressed Concrete
courses.desc: Survey of methods and applications; prestressing materials and systems; prestress losses; flexural design; design for shear and torsion; deflection computation and control; continuous beams and indeterminate structures; floor systems; partial prestressing; design of compression members; strut-and-tie models.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cement Composites
courses.desc: Applications of cement composites; materials selection and proportioning; component and composite properties; hydration reactions and microstructure development; mechanisms of failure; nondestructive test methods; fiber reinforcement; concrete durability; novel reinforcing materials; ferrocement; repair and retrofit technologies; applications to structural design.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Design of Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composite Structures
courses.desc: Basics of mechanics and design of polymer matrix composites: composite classification, manufacturing process, micromechanical property determination, classical lamination theory, strength theories, first-ply-failure, test methods, design practice, strengthening and retrofitting of existing reinforced concrete structures.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Bridge Design
courses.desc: Bridge types, behavior and construction characteristics; design philosophy, details according to Caltrans and American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials codes, principles; seismic design and retrofit of concrete bridges; modern bridges using advanced fiber reinforced polymer composites; fieldtrip required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Performance-Based Seismic Engineering
courses.desc: Modern seismic design; performance-based seismic design; seismic hazard; seismic demands: linear and nonlinear procedures; performance assessment: deterministic and probabilistic procedure; review of FEMA-350, FEMA-356, ATC-40 and other performance-based guidelines.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Design of Materials & Systems for Sustainability
courses.desc: Effects on environmental impacts from materials selection and design in the built environment. Material mechanics, design constraints, and life cycle assessment in the development of “greener” materials and systems. Design of engineered materials through selecting constituents & processing techniques and the influence on mechanical properties, microstructure, and environmental impacts. Role of materials in the environmental impacts of buildings, infrastructure, and other systems.
courses.prereqs: ENG 104 C or ENG 104V C or better; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to Graduate Students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Water Quality
courses.desc: Quality requirements for beneficial uses of water. Hydrologic cycle of quality. Hydromechanics in relation to quality of surface and groundwaters; transport and fate of waterborne pollutants. Heat budget for surface waters; predictive methods; introduction to water quality modeling.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Environmental Reactive Chemical Transport Modeling
courses.desc: Modeling of reactive chemical transport in air and water including kinetic reactions, equilibrium reactions, and phase partitioning. Emphasis on numerical solution schemes and programming techniques to provide deeper insight into model performance and limitations.
courses.prereqs: (CHE 002A or CHE 002B or ECI 149N); or equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Air Quality
courses.desc: Factors determining air quality. Effects of air pollutants. Physical and chemical fundamentals of atmospheric transport and reaction. Introduction to dispersion modeling.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Water & Waste Treatment
courses.desc: Characteristics of water and airborne wastes; treatment processes and process kinetics; treatment system design.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Biological Treatment of Wastewater
courses.desc: Regulations; microbiology and kinetics of engineered biological processes; aeration; and activated sludge.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Biological Treatment of Wastewater
courses.desc: Biological treatment of wastewater using fixed film, hybrid, digestion, and biological nutrient removal processes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Pilot Plant Laboratory
courses.desc: Laboratory investigation of physical, chemical, and biological processes for water and wastewater treatment.
courses.prereqs: ECI 243A; ECI 243B (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor. Graduate standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Life Cycle Assessment for Sustainable Engineering
courses.desc: Life cycle assessment methodology. Emphasis on applications to infrastructure and energy systems. Life cycle design, life cycle cost methods, other tools from industrial ecology, and links to policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Enrollment restricted to graduate students.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open to students who have taken ECI 244.
Cross Listing: EGG 201.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Methods in Industrial Ecology
courses.desc: Implementation, interpretation, and methodological issues and advances in life cycle assessment and other complementary methods from the field of Industrial Ecology with a focus on use in research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Applied Environmental Chemistry: Inorganic
courses.desc: Chemistry of natural and polluted waters. Topics include chemical, kinetic and equilibrium principles, redox reactions, gas solution and solid-solution equilibria, thermodynamics, carbonate systems, coordination chemistry, interfacial phenomena.
courses.prereqs: ENG 105; ECI 140; CHE 002B; or the equivalent of CHE 002B; CHE 002C or CHE 107A recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Applied Environmental Chemistry: Organic
courses.desc: Transport and transformation of organic chemicals in the environment. Topics include application of thermodynamics to predict solubility and activity coefficients; distribution of organic chemicals between the aqueous phase and air, solvent, or solid phases; chemical, photochemical and biological transformation reactions.
courses.prereqs: CHE 128A; CHE 128B; CHE 128C; or the equivalent; CHE 002C or CHE 107A recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Aerosols
courses.desc: Behavior of airborne particles including particle formation, modification, and removal processes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Aerosols Laboratory
courses.desc: Methods of generation and characterization of aerosols. Detailed topics may include flow rate measurement, aerosol generation, aerosol collection, ions measurement, metals measurement, and carbon measurement.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Environmental Health Engineering
courses.desc: Principles and practices of environmental health engineering. Identification, evaluation, and management of environmental factors that impact public health with an emphasis on viruses and waterborne pathogens. Wastewater-based epidemiology, quantitative microbial and chemical risk assessment, and the removal and inactivation of pathogens in water and wastewater treatment.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to graduate students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Probabilistic Design & Optimization
courses.desc: Design by optimization for probabilistic systems, decision theory, the value of information, probabilistic linear programming, probabilistic dynamic programming, nonlinear probabilistic optimization. Applications in civil engineering design, project evaluation, and risk management.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Transportation Demand Analysis
courses.desc: Procedures used in urban travel demand forecasting. Principles and assumptions of model components (trip generation, trip distribution, model split). New methods of estimating travel demand. Computer exercises using empirical data to calibrate models and forecast travel demand.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sustainable Transportation Systems
courses.desc: Freight transportation systems, with optimization model applications beyond freight including mobility, autonomous vehicles, electrification, and planning. Evaluation of freight improvement strategies including operations, infrastructure, management, and vehicle technologies.  Analysis of private and system impacts and environmental and social issues of freight activity such as traffic, behaviors, logistics, and e-commerce.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Dynamic Programming & Multistage Decision Processes
courses.desc: Operations research. Optimization techniques with a focus on dynamic programming in treating deterministic, stochastic, and adaptive multistage decision processes. Brief review of linear programming and non-linear programming. Applications in transportation networks and other civil infrastructure systems.
courses.prereqs: MAT 021C; MAT 022A; programming course; EAD 115 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Applied Data Analysis
courses.desc: Data exploration and integrity; data collection and cleaning techniques; examination of data types, handling missing data and outliers. Coverage of analytical regression techniques encompasses parametric (OLS), semi-parametric (logistic), and non-parametric (GLM, kernel regressions) models. Application of techniques on diverse real-world datasets using various software tools.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: TTP 201.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Transit System Planning & Design
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Transit agency and transit service operations and planning, including scheduling. Street design for transit priority. Bus and rail transit capacity and modal differences. Data used to measure transit performance.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Urban Traffic Management & Control
courses.desc: Basic concepts, models, and methods related to the branch of traffic science that deals with the movement of vehicles on a road network, including travel speed, travel time, congestion concepts, car-following and hydrodynamic traffic models.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Flow in Transportation Networks
courses.desc: Elements of graph theory, a survey of pertinent optimization techniques, extremal principles in network flow problems, deterministic equilibrium assignment, stochastic equilibrium assignment, extensions of equilibrium assignments and dynamic transportation network assignment.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Asphalt & Asphalt Mixes
courses.desc: Asphalts and asphalt mix types and their use in civil engineering structures, with primary emphasis on pavements. Asphalt, aggregate properties and effects on mix properties. Design, construction, recycling. Recent developments and research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sediment Transport
courses.desc: Sediment transport in hydrologic systems. Process-oriented course which will emphasize how sediment moves and the physical processes that affect sediment transport. Field trip.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Colloids in Soil & Water
courses.desc: Colloid occurrence, properties, behavior in different environments, and transport mechanisms in water and soils. Emphasis on their role in water contamination.
courses.prereqs: CHE 002B; (ENG 103 or ECI 100); upper division or graduate standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to graduate standing; Pass Two restricted to upper division standing or graduate standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Turbulent Land-Water-Atmosphere Interactions in the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
courses.desc: Atmospheric boundary layer and the associated thermodynamics, surface energy balance partitioning, equations of motion for the atmospheric boundary layer, turbulent scalar (e.g., heat, water vapor, pollution, etc.) transport equations for stratified flow, atmospheric stability, land-water-atmosphere interactions, similarity relations, modeling parameterizations, and field data analysis.
courses.prereqs: MAT 022B; ECI 100; ECI 141; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Evolutionary Algorithms
courses.desc: Engineering systems design via approximate optimization of simulation models. Local vs. global search. Genetic algorithms, evolutionary strategies, genetic programming. Multi-objective methods. Parameter sensitivity and convergence assessment. Surrogate modeling.
courses.prereqs: ECI 153 C or better; or consent of instructor. Computer programming experience required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Transport, Mixing & Water Quality in River & Lakes
courses.desc: Principal causes of mixing and transport in rivers, lakes and reservoirs, and their impacts on water quality. Case studies of specific lakes and rivers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Transport, Mixing & Water Quality in Estuaries & Wetlands
courses.desc: Principal causes of mixing and transport in estuaries and wetlands, and their impacts on water quality. Topics include advection/diffusion; tides; transverse mixing; longitudinal dispersion; sediment transport; nutrient cycling; computer modeling of estuaries. Case studies of specific systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Stochastic Hydrology & Hydraulics
courses.desc: Physics-based stochastic methods in modeling hydrologic and hydraulic processes; theory for modeling hydrologic-hydraulic governing equations as stochastic partial differential equations applied to various hydrologic-hydraulic processes under uncertainty, including transport, open channel flow, overland flow, soil water flow, and groundwater.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Applied Stochastic Methods in Engineering
courses.desc: Stochastic processes classification; Gaussian random fields; stochastic calculus in mean square; Ito and Stratonovich stochastic differential equations; Fokker-Planck equation; stochastic differential equations with random coefficients.
courses.prereqs: ECI 114 or MAT 131 or STA 130A or STA 131A or MAT 118A (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Water Resource Management
courses.desc: Engineering, institutional, economic, and social basis for managing local and regional water resources. Examples in the context of California's water development and management. Uses of computer modeling to improve water management.
courses.prereqs: ECI 114; ECI 142; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Cross Listing: GEO 212.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Infrastructure Economics
courses.desc: Economics applied to infrastructure engineering  planning, operations, maintenance, and management problems; microeconomic and macroeconomic theories; benefit-cost analysis; effect of uncertainty; optimization economics; non-classical economics; public finance.
courses.prereqs: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); ENG 106; or the equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Transportation-Air Quality: Theory & Practice
courses.desc: Health and regulatory aspects of airborne pollutants. Principles of modeling vehicle emissions. Conformity issues and the regulatory framework. Regional and micro-scale modeling.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Water Resources Management
courses.desc: Discussion of technical papers related to planning theory, system maintenance, regionalization, multi-objective methods, risk analysis, institutional issues, pricing model application, economic development, forecasting, operations, and other topics.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Contaminant Fate & Transport in Porous Media
courses.desc: Solute and colloid mass transport processes in porous media. Characterizing and quantifying physical processes of advection, diffusion/dispersion, sorption, as well as basic biogeochemical reactions. Colloid-facilitated transport in porous media. Analytical and numerical solutions to the reactive advection-dispersion equation in Eulerian and Lagrangian forms with an introduction to advanced random walk models.
courses.prereqs: ECI 144; MAT 021A; MAT 021B; MAT 021C; MAT 022A; MAT 022B; Ability to program.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to upper division and graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Water Resources Systems Engineering
courses.desc: Planning and management of water resource systems. Deterministic and stochastic simulation and optimization techniques. Capacity design and operation of reservoir systems for water supply, hydropower, flood control, and environmental objectives.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Turbulence
courses.desc: Fundamental theory, statistics, analysis tools and models for turbulence and turbulent flows. Practical skills related to the analysis and study of turbulence.
courses.prereqs: MAT 022B; ECI 100; ECI 141; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Hydrologic Time-Series Analysis
courses.desc: Application of statistical methods for analysis and modeling of hydrologic series. Statistical simulation and prediction of hydrologic sequences using time series methodology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Watershed Hydrology
courses.desc: Analysis and mathematical modeling of hydrologic processes taking place in a watershed. Precipitation analysis and modeling. Theory of overland flow and its kinematic wave approximation. Analysis and modeling of saturated and unsaturated subsurface flow processes taking place on a hill slope.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computational River Mechanics I
courses.desc: Unsteady open channel flows, computation of water surface profiles, shallow water equations, St. Venant equations, method of characteristics, finite difference methods, stability and accuracy of explicit and implicit schemes, flood routing in simple and compound channels, advection of plumes.
courses.prereqs: EAD 115 (can be concurrent); ECI 141 (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken ECI 277.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computational River Mechanics II
courses.desc: Open channel flows, physical aspects of river mechanics, formulation of depth-averaged equations, boundary conditions, coordinates transformation and grid generation, finite-difference solution techniques, applications to two-dimensional momentum and pollutant transport in rivers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Hydrodynamics
courses.desc: Perturbation methods. Basic water waves. Governing equations for fluid motion on a rotating earth. Rotation effects, vorticity dynamics, Ekman layer. Stratification effects, internal waves and turbulent mixing. Combined effects.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Mechanics of Fluids
courses.desc: Rotational flows. Navier-Stokes equations and solutions for laminar flow; boundary layer equations and solution techniques. Nature of turbulence. Reynolds equations. Introduction to turbulence modeling.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nonlinear Finite Elements for Elastic-Plastic Problems
courses.desc: State of the art finite element methods and tools for elasticplastic problems, including computational techniques based on the finite element method and the theory of elastoplasticity.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nonlinear Dynamic Finite Elements
courses.desc: State of the art computational methods and tools for analyzing linear and nonlinear dynamics problems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
courses.desc: Consolidation and secondary compression. Preloading and wick drains. Seepage and seepage pressures. Filtration, drainage, and dewatering. Shear strength: friction, cohesion, dilatancy and critical states.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Engineering Geology
courses.desc: Principles of geology in engineering design, construction, and natural hazards. Study of geologic setting, geologic processes, properties of geologic materials and influence on safety, constructability, economic feasibility, environmental impact, and performance.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Integrated Site Characterization
courses.desc: Integrated site characterization using field and laboratory techniques. Applied within context of slope stability analysis as a representative design problem.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only or consent of instructor.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken  ECI 281B.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Pavement Design & Rehabilitation
courses.desc: Advanced pavement design and structural/functional condition evaluation for concrete and asphalt pavements. Highways, airfields, port facilities; new facilities, rehabilitation, reconstruction. Mechanistic-empirical procedures, materials, climate and traffic characterization. Use of current design methods; recent developments and research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physico-Chemical Aspects of Soil Behavior
courses.desc: Study of the geotechnical behavior of soils considering formation, transport, mineralogy, soil-fluid-electrolyte systems, surface tension, particle mechanics, shape, fabric, and structure. Laboratories demonstrate effects of fundamental interparticle forces (contact, Van Der Waals, capillarity and chemical).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Theoretical Geomechanics
courses.desc: Elasticity, plasticity, micromechanics, coupled behavior and large deformations for geomaterials. Prediction of stress-strain-volume change behavior of geomaterials. Monotonic and cyclic loading, anisotropy, bifurcation of deformation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Concrete Pavement Engineering & Materials
courses.desc: Advances in concrete pavements engineering and materials, current and future needs. Strategies to reduce global warming potential through optimizing structural design and enhancing the durability of concrete pavements. Topics include structural design optimization strategies, mixture design optimization, implementation of performance-based specifications for concrete pavements, use of supplementary cementitious materials, fibers, nanomaterials, admixtures.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Foundation Design
courses.desc: Design and analysis of pile and pier foundations, including seismic effects; deep excavation systems; tie-back, nailing, and anchor systems; coffer dams; loads on buried conduits; ground modification techniques; and other related topics.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering
courses.desc: Characteristics and estimation of earthquake ground motions; wave propagation and local site response; liquefaction potential and remediation; residual strength and stability considerations; ground deformations; dynamic soil-structure interaction.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Earth & Rockfill Dams
courses.desc: Site selection; design considerations; layout; seismic effects including considerations of fault movements; construction; environmental considerations, instrumentation; maintenance remediation and retrofit of existing dams.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Discussion of current graduate research, and guest lectures on recent advances. Oral presentation of individual study. Required of graduate degree candidates.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Graduate Research Group Conference
courses.desc: Research problems, progress, and techniques in civil engineering.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.

courses.title: Projects for Environmental & Water Resources
courses.desc: Capstone independent literature-based research project. Project development, reading and mining the literature, strategies and best-practices for writing and oral communication.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Project 2 hour(s)
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students only.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.desc: Geotechnical practice issues that affect the delivery of technical solutions for geotechnical projects, including business and management practices, contract documents, legal constraints, public policy and societal concerns, ethics, and professional development. Part 1 of three part series that includes a capstone project.

Part 3 of three part series that includes a capstone project.

courses.desc: Overview of the discipline of engineering education. One course in a three-course series.

courses.title: Engineering Education II - DEI
courses.desc: Diversity, equity, inclusion and justice in engineering education. One course in a three-course series.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).

courses.desc: Designing engineering lessons and modules for an academic or professional audience. One course in a three-course series.

courses.prereqs: CMN 201; CMN 202; PSC 204A; PSC 204B; or equivalents.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Biological Foundations of Communication
courses.desc: Communibiological, evolutionary, neuroscience, and neurophysiological perspectives on communication. Methodologies for examining human physiological responses to messages, such as heart rate, skin conductance, electromyography, and cortical activity.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Experimental Methods & Analysis in Communication
courses.desc: Experimental designs in communication. Topics include: causation; threats to validity; conceptualization, operationalization, and measurement; hypothesis testing; ethics; data analysis software focusing on the analysis of variance and planned contrasts; and the practical and effective implementation and writing of experiments.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing; one course in inferential statistics.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Survey Research Methods in Communication
courses.desc: Methods for designing personal interview, phone, mail, and web-based surveys in communication. Topics include: sampling strategies, sources of error and bias in survey designs, questionnaire construction, cognitive interviewing, interviewer behavior, and analysis of complex survey data using standard software packages.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor. Graduate standing; one course in inferential statistics.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Web Science Research Methods
courses.desc: Applications of data science to web-based communication research. Design, implementation, analysis, and reporting of studies using online data. Use of Python to scrape, organize, analyze, and visualize web data.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Simulation Methods in Communication Research
courses.desc: Simulation methods for modeling human communication. Single and multiple agent approaches to developing process theories of cooperation, coordination, strategic behavior, information and innovation diffusion, and other aspects of sociality.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Analysis of Communication Networks
courses.desc: Theoretical and analytic issues pertaining to network perspectives on communicating and organizing. Consideration of structural and dynamic features of communication networks. Introduction to network analysis software and various analysis techniques.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Persuasion Theories & Message Design
courses.desc: Major social scientific theories and perspectives on attitude change and persuasion. Application of persuasion theories and principles to persuasive message design in applied contexts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Communication & Cognition
courses.desc: Explores the cognitive structures and processes that enable the production, comprehension and interpretation of messages in face-to-face and mediated communication contexts. Explores the communication outcomes associated with these processes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Risk Communication
courses.desc: Theories and models of individual risk information processing. Media depictions of threats and risk-related information and their potential effects on audiences. Implications for the design and implementation of messages concerning threat and risk.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Social Interaction Theory & Research
courses.desc: Survey of theories and research on social interaction and interpersonal communication. Covers communication codes, individual differences in communication, communication and relationship development, family communication, conflict, cognitive and emotional processes underlying social interaction, social influence, intercultural communication, and nonverbal behavior.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Tactics of Interpersonal Influence
courses.desc: Achievement of interpersonal goals in social interaction. Topics include message production; tactics, strategies and planning; anticipating potential obstacles; resisting and thwarting goals; plan recognition; and goal detection. Examined goals include compliance gaining, attitude change, ingratiation, information seeking, comforting, and deception.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Health Communication
courses.desc: Health communication theories and research traditions. Topics include consumer health information seeking; physician-patient interaction; information, social marketing, “edutainment,” and media advocacy campaigns; social networks and coping; media influences on health; and new communication technologies in health promotion and healthcare delivery.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Cross Listing: SPH 232.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Persuasive Technologies for Health
courses.desc: Theorizing, designing and evaluating ethical technology-based health communication interventions. Uses of social media, mobile communication apps, wearable devices, computer-generated tailored messages, educational games, and computational approaches in health promotion and healthcare delivery.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Cross Listing: SPH 233.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Intercultural Communication
courses.desc: Theories and research on intercultural communication. Topics include national, racial, and ethnic similarities and differences in communication  practices; cultural beliefs and values; identity and conflict; and technological influences on intercultural communication. Methodological issues in intercultural communication research are also examined.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Health Communication Campaigns
courses.desc: Principles of health communication campaign planning, implementation and evaluation. Strategies for changing health behaviors, shaping policy, and improving healthcare organizations’ relations with stakeholders.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate students.
Cross Listing: SPH 235.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Media & Health
courses.desc: Survey of research on media and health. Topics include health news coverage; depictions of health, illness and disability in entertainment; health campaigns; advertising of health products and services; and the influence of gaming and other new media on health behaviors.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Organizational Communication
courses.desc: Theory and research on communication processes in organizations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Mediated Communication Theory & Research
courses.desc: Survey of major theories on the intended and unintended effects of mediated communication. Topics include media's effects on learning, political behavior, interpersonal violence, sexual socialization, consumer behavior, race relations, gender socialization, and cultural processes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Digital Technology & Social Change
courses.desc: Conceptual, theoretical, and international consideration of how digital communication technologies transform social organization and development. Topics include social media, big data, political revolutions, e-democracy, digital divide, e-education, e-health, entrepreneurship, public policies, poverty reduction, technological innovations, microfinance, and entertainment.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open to students who have taken CMN 251Y.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Digital Technology & Social Change
courses.desc: Discussion and research on how digital technologies transform our lives through social media, mobility, big data, global connectivity, and artificial intelligence; changing business, health, democracy, globalization, families, dating, and education.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 2 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open to students who have taken CMN 251.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computer-Mediated Communication
courses.desc: Effects of computer-mediated communication on the ways in which people express themselves, form impressions about strangers, develop and maintain relationships, collaborate on group work, and expand social network, especially in comparison to face-to-face communication.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Children, Adolescents, & the Media
courses.desc: Theory and research on the uses and effects of traditional and new media on children and adolescents, emphasizing social, emotional, cognitive, and physical development. Methodological approaches and ethical issues in studies of underage populations. Parent and family mediation of effects.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Communication Campaigns
courses.desc: Strategic uses of media and interpersonal channels to promote social change through social marketing, information, and media advocacy campaigns. Focus on theory-based interventions in a variety of applied contexts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Social Media
courses.desc: Theoretical, conceptual and analytic issues pertaining to social media research. Topics include motivation, participation, virality, and social-technical capital. Examination of social media in various contexts. Introduction to online behavioral data collection and analysis methods.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Communication Perspective on Video Games
courses.desc: Review of theory and research on the uses and effects of video games and virtual environments developed for entertainment and education. Study of the research methods available for documenting and measuring game use and effects on behavior.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cognitive Approaches to Media
courses.desc: Interdisciplinary examination of cognitive approaches to mediated communication. Application of studies on mediated message processing, cognitive and emotional information processing, psychophysiology, and neuroscience to mass communication. Review of media research and methods on attention, memory, motivation, and limited capacity.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Political Communication
courses.desc: Theories and research on the connections between media, politics, and citizens in the digital age. Critical framework for understanding the nature of mediated politics by assessing inter-relationships between production of news, political elites’ campaign strategies, and behaviors of citizens.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Diffusion of Innovations
courses.desc: Communication processes by which information and innovations spread through social systems. Models of diffusion, including spatial, network, time dependent, semantic and cognitive frameworks. Impact of communication technologies on diffusion. Practical application of diffusion models in a variety of contexts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computational Social Science
courses.desc: Survey of modern computational research methods. Big data, social network analysis, machine learning, Agent-based computer simulations. Online lectures are taught by faculty from all 10 UC campuses. Local face-to-face discussion section.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 1.50 hour(s), Discussion 2 hour(s), Term Paper.
Credit Limitation(s): Only 2 units of credit to students who have taken CMN 150V.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.

courses.desc: Reading, discussion, research and writing on a focused topic in health communication.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Special Topics in Organizational Communication
courses.desc: Reading, discussion, research, and writing on a selected topic in the specialty of organizational communication.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topics differ.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Special Topics in Political Communication
courses.desc: Reading, discussion, research, and writing on a selected topic in the specialty of political communication.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 4 time(s) when topic differs.

courses.desc: Basic concepts of community analysis and planned social change. The dynamics of community change through case studies of communities including peasant, urban ghetto, suburban mainline, and California farm workers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Food Systems
courses.desc: Social aspects of agri-food systems. Social science perspectives applied to food and agricultural sustainability in relation to ecology, knowledge, technology, power, governance, labor, social difference, and social movements. Social and environmental effects of commodity chains in comparative global context.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Industrial cluster formation and institutions. Technology, labor relations and interfirm linkages in global value chains. California and other regions are used as case studies.

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Extensive Writing, Term Paper, Project.

courses.title: Organization of Economic Space
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Globalization and technological restructuring of economic activity focusing on new spatial patterns of production and circulation and their implications for workers, communities and societies, both in the U.S. and around the globe.
courses.prereqs: CRD 001 or CRD 002 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or ANT 002.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Rural Change in the Industrialized World
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Geography of rural environment with emphasis on rural restructuring. Demographics, community, economy, governance, agriculture, and environmental conservation in rural areas of industrialized world. Case studies from and comparisons drawn between North America, Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Japan.
courses.prereqs: SOC 001 or SOC 001V or CRD 001 or CRD 002 or ANT 002.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Extensive Writing, Term Paper.

General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Community Youth Development
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Community influences on youth well-being, youth as agents of community change, and policies to support healthy communities for young people. Special emphasis on disparities in youth well-being related to race, class, immigration status, gender, sexual-orientation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Project, Extensive Writing/Discussion, Term Paper  hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Oral Skills (OL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Community Development Perspectives on Environmental Justice
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Environmental justice social movements; inequitable distribution of pollution on low-income communities of color; histories, policies, and innovations associated environmental justice movements in the United States and around the world.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Extensive Writing/Discussion, Project, Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Oral Skills (OL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Community Research
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Introduction to statistical analysis of social data relevant to community research, planning and assessment, emphasizing data sources and acquisition, descriptive and inferential analysis techniques, and data interpretation and presentation. Emphasis on spatial data and methods, focusing on the sources, processing, analysis, and presentation of spatial data in a community assessment context.
courses.prereqs: SOC 046B or STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 032; consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Community Field Research: Theory & Analysis
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Design and analysis of community research considering the relationship between theory and practice. Community research methods, including elite interviewing, ethnographic approaches, and statistical methods, descriptive statistics and OLS regression. Requires design and completion of field research project.
courses.prereqs: CRD 001; (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or SOC 046B); any upper division Community  Regional Development (CRD) course recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Community Development
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Principles and strategies of community organizing and development. Social change from the grassroots organizing perspective to the formalized public participation process involved in general plan revisions. Practical experience in conducting charrettes, visioning and community needs assessments.
courses.prereqs: CRD 001 or CRD 151 or SOC 002 or SOC 002V  or ANT 002 or ASA 100 or CHI 132 or AAS 101.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: International Community Development: Asia
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Examination and analysis of community development efforts in a range of Asian countries and the impact of global forces in different settings. Includes classroom lectures, workshops, field trips, and collaborative action research projects. May be taught abroad.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor. 2.000 GPA; good academic standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Project 3 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): For summer and quarter abroad versions, limited to 30 students; for the Seminar Abroad version, limited to 15 students; this allows for the small group learning methodology as well as the active collaboration with in-country university students; available for undergraduate and graduate students; applications through UC Davis Study Aboard accepted on a first-come, first-reserved basis for qualified applicants.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: International Community Development: Europe
courses.desc: Examination and analysis of community development efforts in Europe and the impact of global forces in different settings. Alternative strategies with emphasis on self-reliance and locally controlled development. Based in Freiburg, Germany, including field trips to France and Switzerland; taught abroad.
courses.prereqs: ANT 002 or IAD 010 or CRD 001 or CRD 002 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or SOC 002 or SOC 002V or POL 001 or POL 001Y.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: International Community Development: Africa
courses.desc: Examination and analysis of community development efforts in Africa and the impact of global forces in urban and rural settings. Focus on strategies that promote self-reliance and locally controlled development. Based in South Africa; includes field trips.
courses.prereqs: CRD 001 or CRD 002 or ANT 002 or IAD 010 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or SOC 002 or SOC 002V or POL 001 or  POL 001Y.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Fieldwork 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Social Theory & Community Change
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Comparative overview of the dominant social science paradigms for the study of community development and change. Among the paradigms discussed are functionalism, conflict theory/Marxism, structuralism, community capitals, social exchange, post-positivism, feminist theories and social constructivism.
courses.prereqs: CRD 001 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or ANT 002; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).

General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Community Economic Development
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.How government and community organizations help firms grow and create jobs through local economic development corporations, small business centers, revolving loan funds, incubators, and other programs. Techniques to analyze community economic potential and identification of appropriate intervention tools. Group project.
courses.prereqs: CRD 152 or PLS 021 or PLS 021V or ECS 015; and consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Politics & Community Development
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Analyzes political, economic and sociocultural forces shaping the form and function of local communities in the U.S. Considers theories of the state, the community and social change and case studies of actual community development in comparative historical perspective.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Community Governance
courses.desc: Governing institutions and political processes at the local level. Local government organization, community autonomy, leadership, political change, policy development, and select policy issues including public finance. Topics change depending on student interest. Field research on coalition building or policy issues in select communities.
courses.prereqs: CRD 001 or SOC 001 or SOC 001V or POL 001 or POL 001Y.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: People, Work & Technology
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Analysis of the relationship between work, technology, and the human experience. General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Oral Skills (OL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Housing & Social Policy
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Social impact, economics, and politics of housing in the United States. Special attention given to federal, state, and local policy and program strategies to produce and preserve affordable housing and inclusive neighborhoods.

Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Focus on the dimensions, causes, and means of alleviating social inequality in the U.S. Examination and analysis of major theories and forms (class, race/ethnicity, gender, and citizenship status) of inequality. Policy-based and grassroots approaches to change.

courses.details:

courses.desc: Fundamental concepts. Planar graphs: Kuratowski's theorem. Packings and coverings. Menger's theorem, representation of cuts, Hamilton graphs, rigid graphs, chordal graphs, graph coloring, graph isomorphism, applications and some algorithms.
courses.prereqs: graduate standing in electrical engineering or computer science or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Mathematics of unstructured data. Algorithms for data structures such as Voronoi diagrams, oct-trees, and arrangements. Applications in computer graphics, concentrating on problems in three-dimensions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Modern cryptography as a discipline emphasizing formal definitions and proofs of security. One-way functions, pseudo-randomness, encryption, digital signatures, zero-knowledge, secure protocols.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cryptography for E-Commerce
courses.desc: Cryptographic primitives and protocols of importance to e-commerce, present and future, including content distribution mechanisms, payment mechanisms, pricing mechanisms, anonymity and privacy mechanisms, fair exchange mechanisms.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Computational Structural Bioinformatics
courses.desc: Algorithmic problems in structural biology; protein structure classification; protein structure prediction (including comparative modeling and ab initio protein structure prediction); molecular simulations (molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Applied Numerical Linear Algebra
courses.desc: Numerical linear algebra (NLA) with emphasis on applications in engineered systems; matrix factorizations; perturbation and rounding error analyses of fundamental NLA algorithms.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion/Laboratory 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One open to Ph.D. students in Computer Science only and Pass Two open to graduate students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Large-Scale Scientific Computation
courses.desc: Algorithms and techniques for large-scale scientific computation, including basics for high performance computing, iterative methods, discrete approximation, fast Fourier transform, Poisson solvers, particle methods, spectral graph partition and its applications.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Theory of Molecular Computation
courses.desc: Theory of chemical reaction networks, molecular circuits, DNA self-assembly, DNA sequence design and thermodynamic energy models, and connections to the field of distributed computing.
courses.prereqs: ECS 120 or ECS 220 recommended; probability course recommended, for example ECS 132 or MAT 135A or STA 012 or STA 131A or MAT 131A; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to graduate students in Computer Science; Pass Two restricted to graduate students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computational Functional Genomics
courses.desc: Bioinformatics methods for analysis and inference of functional relationships among genes using large-scale genomic data, including methods for integration of gene expression, promoter sequence, TF-DNA binding and other data, and approaches in modeling of biological networks.
courses.prereqs: ECS 124; graduate standing in Computer Science or Life Sciences.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computer & Information Security
courses.desc: Modern topics in computer security, including: protection, access control, operating systems security, network security, applied cryptography, cryptographic protocols, secure programming practices, safe languages, mobile code, malware, privacy and anonymity, and case studies from real-world systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 235.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Foundations of Computer & Information Security
courses.desc: Theoretical foundations of methods used to protect data in computer and communication systems. Access control matrix and undecidability of security; policies; Bell-LaPadula, Biba, Chinese Wall models; non-interference and non-deducibility; information flow and the confinement problem.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken ECS 235.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Concepts of intrusion detection, anomaly detection based on machine learning, signature-based detection using pattern matching, automated response to attacks using artificial intelligence planning, tracing intruders based on principal component analysis, security policy languages.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.desc: Advanced topics in programming languages, including formal syntax and semantics, the relation between formal semantics and verification, an introduction to the lambda calculus. Additional topics will include language design principles, alternative programming languages, in-depth semantic theory and models of language implementation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One open to Ph.D. students in Computer Science only and Pass Two open to graduate students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Translation of Programming Languages
courses.desc: Lexical analysis, parsing, storage management, symbol table design, semantic analysis and code generation. LR, LALR grammars. Compilercompilers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Code Generation & Optimization
courses.desc: Compiler optimizations for performance, code size and power reduction. Topics include control- and data-flow analysis, redundancy elimination, loop and cache optimizations, register allocation, local and global instruction scheduling, and modulo scheduling.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Principles of Concurrent Programming
courses.desc: Fundamental concepts and applications of concurrent programs; concurrent program verification and derivation; synchronization mechanisms in programming languages; distributed programming techniques; case studies of languages.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Analysis of Software Artifacts
courses.desc: Techniques for the analysis of software artifacts, including source code, build processes, test suites, bug reports and documentation with a special emphasis on software correctness and performance in real-world settings.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to PhD students in Computer Science; Pass Two restricted to Graduate Students in Computer Science.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Concurrent Programming Languages
courses.desc: Language design parameters. Models of parallel machines. Load balancing. Scalability. Portability. Efficiency measures. Design and implementation techniques for several classes of concurrent programming languages (such as object-oriented, functional, logic, and constraint programming languages).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.desc: Models, design, implementation, performance evaluation in operating systems. Algorithms, internal architectures for single processor OS and distributed systems. Concurrency control, recovery, security. OS kernel-level programming. Special topics embedded systems, real-time system, device driver, NPU (Network Processor Unit).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.desc: Internet protocol based computer networks applications, transport, network layer protocols. High speed LAN technologies: Ethernet, Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM). Delay models in data networks: analysis of multiaccess techniques in polling, ring, random access networks. Multimedia applications requirements and design.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Develops the mathematical theory underlying growth, structure and function of networks with applications to physical, social, biological and engineered systems. Topics include network growth, resilience, epidemiology, phase transitions, software and algorithms, routing and search control, cascading failures.

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: MAE 253.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Resource Management in Wireless Communication Networks
courses.desc: Advanced research issues in wireless communication networks, including multi-user diversity and cross-layer optimization, basic network information theory, MIMO systems and the impact on networks, and dynamics spectrum management.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Probabilistic and statistical models useful in computer/data science. Applications to networks, bioinformatics, database management, machine learning, software engineering and image processing.
courses.prereqs: A calculus-based course in probability, such as ECS132, STA 131A, or EEC 161; programming skills and familiarity with matrix algebra.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project, Extensive Problem Solving.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ECS 256A.

courses.title: Mobile & Wireless Networks
courses.desc: Fundamental techniques in design of second generation wireless networks: cellular network and protocols, medium access techniques, handoff control, signaling and mobility management, wireless data works, Internet mobility and Personal Communication Services (PCS). Third generation wideband systems, novel technologies, adhoc networks.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Independent Study 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Optical Networks
courses.desc: Optical networks. Enabling technologies. Multiplexing techniques. WDM. Broadcast networks. Wavelength-routed networks. Network architectures. Protocols. Network algorithms. Device-network interface. Optimization problems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Independent Study 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.desc: Advanced techniques for domain-specific software reuse.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One open to Ph.D. students in Computer Science only and Pass Two open to graduate students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Methods of proving correctness of programs with respect to formal specifications, with attention to those suited for employing automated deduction. Logic background, symbolic execution, techniques suited to iterative programming, methods from denotational semantics, termination, dynamic logic and proofs of concurrent programs.

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.

courses.desc: Formal specification of modules, and its relationship to topdown programming development and verification. Abstract data types, together with methods for specifying them. Implementations and proofs of implementation. Using specifications to reason about programs. Parameterized types. Constructing good formal specifications.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Distributed Database Systems
courses.desc: Concepts of distributed database systems and architectures, distributed database design, distributed query processing and optimization, transaction management and concurrency control, heterogeneous and multidatabase systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Spatial Databases
courses.desc: Concepts, models, and architectures for spatial databases, spatial access methods, query processing, spatio-temporal data management, moving objects, spatial data mining.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Students in Computer Science only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Wide-Area Distributed Information Systems
courses.desc: Wide-area distributed information systems, data broadcast, multicast, publish/subscribe, service differentiation, information retrieval, Web caching.
courses.details:

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One open to PhD students in Computer Science only and Pass Two open to graduate students in Computer Science only.

courses.desc: Generative modeling techniques and architectures for large-scale AI systems, focusing on large language models (LLMs) and multimodal generative models. courses.title: Public Economics
