courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Fieldwork.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 40 students per section.
Cross Listing: GEL 183.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Oral Skills (OL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Learning in a Digital Age
courses.desc: Critical analysis and history of social media, ubiquitous connectivity, digital communication, educational games, and media literacy as related to fundamental shifts in information, schooling, and society.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: Internship as a tutor, teacher's aide, or peer counselor in a school or educational counseling setting under the supervision of a faculty member. May be taught abroad.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 2-8 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Tutoring in Education
courses.desc: Leading of small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with the School's upper division courses under the supervision of, and at the option of, the course instructor, who will submit a written evaluation of the student's work.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Tutorial 1-2 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) up to 4 units.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Directed group study.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 3-15 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Educational Research
courses.desc: Defining educational research questions, reviewing relevant literature, developing research designs, developing research instruments, selecting appropriate data analysis procedures, and writing research projects. A case problem will provide practice in designing and reporting research.
courses.prereqs: Introductory statistics or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Qualitative Research in Education
courses.desc: Examines the design and conduct of educational research using non-numerical data (e.g., text, discourse, imagery and artifacts). Focuses on issues (e.g., validity, reliability, generalizability, ethics) and reporting genres (e.g., narrative accounts, case studies, and arguments).
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s), Lecture 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Educational & Psychological Measurement
courses.desc: Theory and practice of measurement with educational and psychological variables. Common applications of standardized tests and debates surrounding their interpretation and use. Procedures for test development and scoring as well as statistical methods for evaluating reliability, validity, dimensionality, and test fairness.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Educational Research:  Analysis of Correlational Designs
courses.desc: Methods for analysis of correlational data in educational research. Topics include multiple correlation and regression, discriminant analysis, logistic regression, and canonical correlation. Emphasis on conceptual understanding of the techniques and use of statistical software.
courses.prereqs: Introductory statistics or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Educational Research:  Experimental Designs
courses.desc: Methods for analysis of experimental data in educational research. Topics include ANOVA, fixed v. random effects models, repeated measures ANOVA, analysis of co-variance, MANOVA, chi square tests, small sample solutions to t and ANOVA.
courses.prereqs: Introductory statistics or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnographic Research in Schools I: Current Theory & Practice
courses.desc: Current literature from anthropology and society related to schools. Emphasis on the organizational structure of institutions, and the analysis of face-to-face interaction. Explore the relationship between field-based research and theory development on the acquisition of knowledge in specific social and cultural contexts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnographic Research in Schools II: Field-Based Research Projects
courses.desc: Research projects in specific schools with cooperative critical analysis of the design, data collection, and inferencing by researchers. Continue to meet with instructors as a group throughout the quarter to discuss specific projects.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry into Classroom Practice: Traditions & Approaches
courses.desc: Introduction to traditions and approaches of teachers conducting research in their own classrooms: purposes, focal areas, methods of data collection and analysis, and written genre conventions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Fieldwork.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry into Classroom Practice: Application of Teacher Research Approaches
courses.desc: Analysis and application of teacher research through the development, implementation and evaluation of a short-term classroom research-based intervention. Particular attention to research that enhances learning of English language learners and under-performing students.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate Teaching Credential students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry into Classroom Practice: Study Design
courses.desc: Proposal development for classroom-based inquiry designed to address student learning needs. Mixed methods research design and preliminary data collection approaches. Design and application of baseline student assessment for proposal development. Literature review. Data collection in K-12 classrooms required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate MA Credential students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry into Classroom Practice: Data Analysis & Research Reporting
courses.desc: Support of the inquiry in EDU 206C through continuous collaborative critique and feedback resulting in the writing and presentation of a research study.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s), Extensive Writing/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate MA Credential students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Psychological Perspectives on School Learning
courses.desc: Study of human learning theory and research related to learning of academic content. Review of contemporary issues of constructivism, problem solving, expertise, conceptual change, transfer, and metacognition.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sociocultural & Situative Perspectives on Learning & Cognition
courses.desc: Sociocultural and situative theories of cognition and learning. Major ideas of L.S. Vygotsky, followed by modern perspectives: situated cognition, cognitive apprenticeship, situated learning, communities of practice, cultural-historical activity theory, and distributed cognition. Implications of each theoretical perspective for educational practice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Individual Assessment
courses.desc: Theories of intellectual functioning and the measurement of cognitive abilities in school-aged children. Supervised practice in administration and scoring of contemporary tests for children including the WISC-R, the WAIS-R, the Stanford Binet, the McCarthy Scales of Children's Ability.
courses.prereqs: Introductory statistics or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research on Achievement Motivation in Education
courses.desc: Analysis and critique of recent research on cognitive processes related to achievement motivation in school settings. Topics include self-determination theory, attribution theory, goal theory, intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, learned helplessness. psychological reactance, gender and culture, and research design.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Concepts & Methods of Policy Analysis
courses.desc: Introduction to concepts and methods of policy analysis. Emphasis on the relationship between educational issues and problems; policy development; constructing persuasive policy analyses; issues related to policy process.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Fieldwork, Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Culture & Social Organization of Schools
courses.desc: Culture and social organization of schools. Examines perspectives of social researchers, educational policy-makers, and school members and their implications for educational research, policy and practice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: School Change & Educational Reform
courses.desc: Analysis of models, processes, and case studies of school change and educational reform with respect to variable characteristics of schools and schooling, planned and unplanned change, the moral evaluation of school change, and the role of educational research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Education & Social Policy
courses.desc: Focuses on understanding the social and political context of education in the U.S. and California and how education policy is formed in the broader public arena. Develops skills in educational policy analysis. (Former EDU 237.)
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Education Policy & Law
courses.desc: Examination of law as an instrument of social policy. Specific focus on the legalization of education decision making, its causes, dimensions, and effects on administrative and teacher authority.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Culture & Social Organization of Higher Education
courses.desc: Critical study of culture and social organization of higher education institutions policies and functions in the U.S., with some attention to other countries.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Politics & Governance of Education
courses.desc: Examination of political power, representation, influence, decision-making and inter-governmental relations in the public schools.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Education Finance Policy
courses.desc: Examination of (1) United States financing public education, (2) the relationship between school finance and education policy, and (3) the relationship between education finance and education practice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Special Topics in Education Policy
courses.desc: Selected topics in education policy. Designed to facilitate preparation for the qualifying examination or dissertation. Critically analyze scholarly work including their own works in progress.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quasi-Experimental Methods in Educational Research
courses.desc: Introduction to experimental and quasi-experimental statistical methods to evaluate the effectiveness of educational policies and practices. Analytic approaches include randomized control trials, regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences methods, instrumental variables, and fixed and random effects.
courses.prereqs: EDU 204A; or equivalent course covering multivariate regression.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing, Extensive Problem Solving.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Humanizing Research Methods
courses.desc: Methodological approaches that humanize the qualitative inquiry process for researchers and the non-dominant communities they serve with a focus on ethnography, historiography, and social design experiments. Strategies for leveraging and disseminating findings to engage in transformational problem solving in education both in schools and in out-of-school settings.
courses.prereqs: EDU 201 or similar introductory qualitative methods course.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Critical Pedagogy
courses.desc: A socio-cultural critique, from an interdisciplinary perspective, of educational reform and change. The critique will include an analysis of the influence of text content on the perpetuation of social power differences.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Application of Hierarchical Linear Models in Education Research
courses.desc: Application of hierarchical linear models in education research across multiple areas, such as policy, curriculum, and assessment. Develop working knowledge of hierarchical linear modeling and an understanding of its use in existing research as well as student's work.
courses.prereqs: EDU 204A; or similar course with permission of the instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Survey Research Methods
courses.desc: Theories, principles and application of survey research methodology. Students develop, validate, and administer survey instruments; select representative samples; conduct focus groups; and collect, organize, and analyze survey data. Familiarity with introductory concepts in descriptive and inferential statistics is assumed.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Participatory Action Research (PAR)
courses.desc: Principles and strategies of PAR and related methodologies that emphasize collaborating with those affected by the issue being researched in order to educate, take action or effect social change. Conduct interviews with potential collaborators, case analyses and research proposals.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Interview Methods
courses.desc: Introduction to qualitative interviewing, focused in particular on narrative and self-story as both practical method and theoretical stance. Complete a case-focused interview project during the course: designing an interview protocol, conducting the interview, transcribing, analyzing, and presenting their research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Digital Literacies
courses.desc: The changing nature of literacy and learning as people participate with digital tools across local and global contexts. Young people’s digital literacies. Research and theories on culturally and socially situated meaning-making practices as mediated by digital tools. Varied digital literacies practices.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Topical Seminar in Language, Literacy & Culture
courses.desc: Critical study of selected issues of language, literacy, and culture as they relate to education.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topics differ.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Theory & Research in Early Literacy
courses.desc: Analysis of children's initial processes in learning to read extending from the preschool years into second grade. Topics include emergent literacy, phonological awareness, word recognition, decoding, spelling, vocabulary, comprehension, second language reading, assessment, intervention, and instruction.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Reading as a Social & Cultural Process
courses.desc: Recent theoretical and empirical work on reading in social contexts. Topics include reading as an individual interactive process; reading as a social and cultural process; critical perspectives on reading; implications of contrastive theoretical perspectives for curriculum and instruction in reading.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research on Response to Culturally Diverse Literature, K-12
courses.desc: Research on response to culturally diverse literature in classrooms and other K-12 settings. Topics include reader response theories, values in expanding the literary canon, problems of cultural authenticity, resistance to multicultural literature, and instruction for diverse texts and learners.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Academic Language & Literacies
courses.desc: Exploration of theories and research on academic language and literacies for the schooling of first and second language learners. Students use basic qualitative methods to collect and analyze classroom language and literacy data.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Discourse Analysis in Educational Settings
courses.desc: Examines form and type in discourse (e.g., narration, conversation, routines), approaches to discourse analysis, and research on classroom discourse (lessons, teaching/learning interactional sequences). Final term paper is an analysis of discourse data tape-recorded by student in a field setting.
courses.prereqs: An introductory linguistics or sociolinguistics course or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research in Bilingual & Second Language Education
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Discussion and analysis of recent research in bilingual and second language education. Topics include: language acquisition in second language learners and bilinguals, second language teaching methods, language-use models in bilingual education, interaction analysis in bilingual/cross-cultural classrooms, use of the vernacular in classrooms.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry into Classroom Practice: Bilingual Methods
courses.desc: Analysis and application of teacher research through the development, implementation and evaluation of a short-term research-based classroom intervention. Research that enhances learning of multilingual language learners.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Curriculum Development & Evaluation in Mathematics
courses.desc: Analysis of curricular issues and goals in mathematics education, including long-term trends, current status and influences, proposed changes, and evaluation issues. Selected curriculum projects examined.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research in Mathematics Education
courses.desc: Examination of research process in mathematics education; review of critical productive problems identified by researchers; evolution of trends, issues, theories and hypotheses in various areas of mathematics education research. Emphasizes foundations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research in Mathematics Education
courses.desc: Current research issues and activities in mathematics education: status, trends, theories and hypotheses. Formulation of research questions and design of studies. Projection of future directions for research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: The Modern History of Science Education
courses.desc: History of curricular issues and goals in science education from the late-19th century forward, including long-term trends, current status and influences, proposed changes, and evaluation issues. National science standards and curriculum projects.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research Topics in Science Education I
courses.desc: Research process and product in science education; review of critical science education issues; evolution of trends, theories and hypotheses in various areas of science education research. Survey of current major research in science education.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research Topics in Science Education II
courses.desc: Current research issues and activities in science education: status, trends, theories and hypotheses. Formulation of research questions, design of studies and critical, in-depth review of literature related to the student's research interests.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Scientific Literacy & Science Education Reform
courses.desc: Current trends in science education reform locally, regionally, and nationally focusing on scientific literacy. Equity, access and "science for all."
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research on Teacher Education & Development
courses.desc: Research on teacher preparation in university credential programs and on professional development of in-service teachers, with special attention to teacher preparation for work with culturally and linguistically diverse youth.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Supervision of Student Teachers: Research, Theory & Practice
courses.desc: Research, theory and practice in the preparation and supervision of teachers. Practice in the supervision of candidates in university teaching credential programs during the student teaching field placement and the mentoring of novice teachers by expert teachers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Effective Instruction: Curriculum & Assessment-Theory, Research, & Practice
courses.desc: Examination of contemporary theories of curriculum development, research about the relationship among instructional planning, classroom assessment, and student learning to guide teaching practice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to Teaching Credential majors.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Effective Instruction: English Language Development & Instructing English Language Learners
courses.desc: Analysis and application of English language acquisition and development research to teaching practice. Particular attention to research that enhances learning of English language learners and under-performing students.
courses.prereqs: Acceptance in the Teaching Credential Program.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry & Practice: Qualitative Research for Educational Leaders
courses.desc: Prepares students to understand the nature/assumptions/logic of qualitative methodology as applied to educational settings, focusing on issues of design/conceptualization/ interpretation/application of qualitative research procedures. Use these methods in conducting studies in their educational settings.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry & Practice: Quantitative Research for Educational Leaders
courses.desc: Focus is on field-based and general quantitative research methods in education. Acquire skills and knowledge to collect, organize, analyze, and interpret univariate and multivariate quantitative data in educational research, dissertation projects, and field-based projects.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Inquiry & Practice: Research Design & Application for Educational Leaders
courses.desc: Educational leaders are introduced to qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods educational research methods and learn to frame research questions, identify data/data sources, use descriptive statistics, critically examine research studies, make sense of educational research/policy, and conduct independent studies.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problem-Based Learning Courses: Part 1
courses.desc: Students identify problems from their educational settings, engage in data collection/analysis, write-up the process/results, and present to class. Work may become a dissertation proposal, if the problem or its extension is of sufficient interest and value.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Extensive Writing/Discussion, Fieldwork.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problem-Based Learning Courses: Part 2
courses.desc: Continuation of part one.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Extensive Writing/Discussion, Fieldwork.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problem-Based Learning Courses: Part 3
courses.desc: Continuation of part two.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Extensive Writing/Discussion, Fieldwork.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problem-Based Learning Courses: Part 4
courses.desc: Continues problem-based series. Support preparing dissertation proposals for qualifying exams (QE), and for IRB submission. Includes extensive writing: writing assignments and writing support for dissertation proposal and synthesis of learning. Includes preparation for QE presentations, including mock-QEs with exams scheduled. Short preview of concepts of data analysis and writing of findings, but more in-depth instruction provided on those topics in EDU 281E.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3.2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to CANDEL EdD program only.
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Problem-Based Learning Courses: Part 5
courses.desc: Concludes the problem-based series. Provides support to enter the post-qualifying exam phase, including instruction on data analysis, and extensive writing assignments. Writing tasks include reporting findings and synthesizing dissertation findings with existing literature, as well as finalizing and formatting dissertations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3.2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to CANDEL EdD program only.
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Beginning Issues & Practices: Contemporary Educational Leadership
courses.desc: Explore the history and emergent relationships among leadership theories/practice and their application to current educational settings. Reflect on and refine their personal theory of leadership.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Beginning Issues & Practices: Diversity Issues for Educational Leaders
courses.desc: Diversity of stakeholders and community issues in California schools and colleges will be explored. Emphasis will be placed on the interaction between underrepresented segments of society and educational institutions. Best Practices in leading diverse schools will be explored.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Issues & Practices: Leadership Across Communities
courses.desc: Examine the theory/practice/process of leadership in community-building and collaboration in/across communities, while addressing the utilization of human and material resources and the creation of partnerships, community linkages, and collaborative efforts.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Issues & Practices: Leadership & Student Services
courses.desc: Practical and theoretical perspectives for building a sense of vision to lead the profession of student affairs and to meet the needs of the whole student.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Policy: History & Theory of Educational Policy
courses.desc: Learn/analyze the history/theory of educational policy. Explore how education leaders have/can positively influence the  process and implement effective policies in their local institutions. Policy issues covered: educational opportunity, equity, access, regulation, testing, tenure, accountability.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Policy: Formulating & Influencing Policy
courses.desc: Conduct critical analyses of policy at the federal, judicial, state, regional and local levels. Specific California and federal policy environment structures, processes and people will be examined for intended consequences, ethical dilemmas, social justice and equity issues.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Policy: Possibilities & Limitations of Educational Policy in a Democracy
courses.desc: Critically examine the democratic purposes of education in light of existing National, State, and local policy reform efforts. Questions include, "In what ways are these reforms and policies guided by democratic ideas and challenged by those ideals."
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Educational Finance, Human Resources, & Law; Human & Financial Assets; Allocations & Budgets
courses.desc: Topics include: education finance theory, contemporary finance policy issues, intergovernmental relations, effective resource management, budget analysis and preparation.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Educational Finance, Human Resources, & Law: Ethical & Legal Issues in Education
courses.desc: Human resource and legal concepts and activities governing decisions of school leaders in public education. Attention to theory, application, and practice of personnel and risk management, curriculum, student services, teacher rights, torts, student rights.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Organizational Structures & Change: Data-Driven Decision-Making for Change
courses.desc: Use and examine multiple sources of information and data and trends found in making quality decisions to improve P-12/community college settings and addressing problems at sites. Learn limitations of these data sources.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: CANDEL Dissertation Seminars
courses.desc: Third-year seminars encourage students to complete dissertations within the year. Cohort members meet together in every three-week meetings with faculty members and share their writing, data collection, analysis, discussion of results, development of conclusions/implications.
courses.prereqs: Admission into the CANDEL EdD program or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 18-36 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 9 time(s) until dissertation is completed.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: CANDEL Dissertation
courses.desc: Cohort members continue to meet with faculty and share their writing, data collection, analysis, development of conclusions/implications.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; passing of qualifying exams in CANDEL program and advancement to candidacy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 18-36 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 9 time(s) until dissertation is completed.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Inquiry & Practice: Academic Writing for Educational Leaders
courses.desc: Rigorous practice in the types of writing required of educational doctorate (CANDEL) students. courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 6 hour(s).

courses.title: Signal Analysis & Communications
courses.desc: Signal analysis based on Fourier methods. Fourier series and transforms; time-sampling, convolution, and filtering; spectral density; modulation: carrier-amplitude, carrier-frequency, and pulse-amplitude.

courses.desc: Introduces basic aspects of computer architecture, including computer performance measurement, instruction set design, computer arithmetic, pipelined/non-pipelined implementation, and memory hierarchies (cache and virtual memory). courses.title: RF Integrated Circuits for Wireless Communications
courses.desc: Integrated RF front end circuit design of receivers and synthesizers for wireless communications, such as LNA, mixers, PLL; noise and linearity analysis and specifications; theory and working mechanism of synthesizers and phase noise analysis.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Terahertz & mm-Wave Integrated Circuit Design
courses.desc: Fundamental theory of RF transmitter and receiver, including noise analysis, transceiver architectures, and antenna arrays. Fundamental limitations, theory and design of amplifiers, oscillators and signal sources at THz and mm-wave frequencies.
courses.prereqs: EEC 132A; EEC 112; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Microwave Circuit & Device Design Techniques
courses.desc: Theory, design, fabrication, analysis of advanced microwave circuits and devices. Wideband transformers, stripline/microstripline broadband couplers. Lumped and distributed filter synthesis. Broadband matching theory applied to microwave devices. Wideband and low noise FET/HEMT amplifiers. Advanced microwave oscillator theory. Phase noise analysis.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: RF-MEMS & Adaptive Wireless Frontends
courses.desc: Focuses on the modeling, design, fabrication, and characterization of RF-MEMS while providing a thorough introduction to the technology with an emphasis on how it will benefit the design of adaptive RF/microwave wireless systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Electromagnetics
courses.desc: Maxwell's equations, plane waves, reflection and refraction, complex waves, waveguides, resonant cavities, and basic antennas.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Plasma Physics & Controlled Fusion I
courses.desc: Equilibrium plasma properties; single particle motion; fluid equations; waves & instabilities in a fluid plasma; plasma kinetic theory & transport coefficients; linear & nonlinear Vlasov theory; fluctuations, correlations & radiation; inertial & magnetic confinement systems in controlled fusion.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Graduate Standing in Engineering or Consent of Instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Plasma Physics & Controlled Fusion II
courses.desc: Equilibrium plasma properties; single particle motion; fluid equations; waves & instabilities in a fluid plasma; plasma kinetic theory & transport coefficients; linear & nonlinear Vlasov theory; fluctuations, correlations & radiation; inertial & magnetic confinement systems in controlled fusion.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Plasma Physics & Controlled Fusion III
courses.desc: Equilibrium plasma properties; single particle motion; fluid equations; waves & instabilities in a fluid plasma; plasma kinetic theory & transport coefficients; linear & nonlinear Vlasov theory; fluctuations, correlations & radiation; inertial & magnetic confinement systems in controlled fusion.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Electromagnetics I
courses.desc: The exact formulation of applied electromagnetic problems using Green's functions. Applications of these techniques to transmission circuits.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Electromagnetics II
courses.desc: An advanced treatment of electromagnetics with applications to passive microwave devices and antennas.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physics & Technology of Microwave Vacuum Electron Beam Devices I
courses.desc: Physics & technology of electron beam emission, flow and transport, electron gun design, space charge waves & klystrons with applications to accelerator systems, RF power sources for radar & communication systems, thermionic energy conversion, and electric space propulsion. Recent advances in materials & manufacturing technologies are also reviewed.
courses.prereqs: B.S. degree in physics or engineering or the equivalent background or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physics & Technology of Microwave Vacuum Electron Beam Devices I
courses.desc: Physics & technology of electron beam emission, flow and transport, electron gun design, space charge waves & klystrons with applications to accelerator systems, RF power sources for radar & communication systems, thermionic energy conversion, and electric space propulsion. Recent advances in materials & manufacturing technologies also reviewed.
courses.prereqs: B.S. degree in physics or engineering or the equivalent background or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physics & Technology of Microwave Vacuum Electron Beam Devices II
courses.desc: Theory, modeling, & experimental design of traveling wave tubes, backward wave oscillators, and extended interaction oscillators employed in satellite commutations, plasma imaging, and underground imaging systems.
courses.prereqs: EEC 234A or EEC 324AV; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physics & Technology of Microwave Vacuum Electron Beam Devices II
courses.desc: Theory, modeling, & experimental design of traveling wave tubes, backward wave oscillators, and extended interaction oscillators employed in satellite commutations, plasma imaging, and underground imaging systems.
courses.prereqs: EEC 234A or EEC 234AV recommended; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physics & Technology of Microwave Vacuum Electron Beam Devices III
courses.desc: Physics & technology of gyrotrons, gyro-amplifiers, free electron lasers, magnetrons, cross-field amplifiers, and relativistic devices employed in plasma fusion reactors, microwave heating, and high power microwave applications.
courses.prereqs: EEC 234B or EEC 234BV; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physics and Technology of Microwave Vacuum Electron Beam Devices III
courses.desc: Physics & technology of gyrotrons, gyro-amplifiers, free electron lasers, magnetrons, cross-field amplifiers, and relativistic devices employed in plasma fusion reactors, microwave heating, and high power microwave applications.
courses.prereqs: EEC 234B or EEC 234BV; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Photonics
courses.desc: Optical propagation of electromagnetic waves and beams in photonic components and the design of such devices using numerical techniques.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nonlinear Optical Applications
courses.desc: Nonlinear optical interactions in optical communication, optical information processing and integrated optics. Basic concepts underlying optical nonlinear interactions in materials and guided media.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed EEC 233.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Lasers
courses.desc: Theoretical and practical description of lasers. Theory of population inversion, amplification and oscillation using semiclassical oscillator model and rate equations. Description and design of real laser system.
courses.prereqs: EEC 235; EEC 130B; or the equivalent of EEC 130B.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed EEC 226A.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Laser Physics II
courses.desc: Oscillation threshold. Coupled cavity/atomic rate equations, Linear pulse propagation; dispersion, broadening, compression. Nonlinear pulse propagation. Energy extraction. Optical beams, resonators, eigenmodes, axial/transverse modes. Paraxial ray optics, resonator stability, ABCD matrices. Laser dynamics; transients, spiking, Q-switching, active and passive modelocking.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed EEC 226B.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Semiconductor Lasers & Photonic Integration
courses.desc: Understanding of fundamental optical transitions in semiconductors and quantum-confined systems are applied to diode & unipolar lasers and selected photonic devices. The importance of radiative and non-radiative recombination, simulated emission, excitons in quantum wells, and strained quantum layers are considered. Photonic integrated circuits based on active (with optical gain) and passive (without optical gain).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Optical Communication Technologies  for High-Speed Data Networking
courses.desc: Enabling technologies for optical fiber communication and data center networks. Physical layer issues for component and system technologies in high-speed data optical communications. High-capacity data multiplexing technologies including wavelength-division-multiplexing, time-division-multiplexing, and advanced coherent modulation. Optical signal transmission, optical amplification, and optical switching for telecom and data center networks.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: High-Capacity Optical Data Systems & Networks
courses.desc: High-capacity optical data systems and networks, built-on modern optical communication technologies. Technologies behind data center networking, software defined networking, and RF-optical networking. Physical layer issues in light of networking architectures and protocols. Optical communications systems design and integration. Systems technologies and higher-level network architecture, case studies. WDM, TDM, and EON networking, optical and wireless access technologies based on PON and ROF.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Semiconductor Device Physics
courses.desc: Physical principles, characteristics and models of various semiconductor materials and devices, including: P-N junction, metal- semiconductor diodes, junction, and insulated-gate field effect transistors.  Elements of basic design exercises to explore circuit design, RF phenomenon, optoelectronics, solid-state devices, materials, and large-scale integration.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s); Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quantum Information Technologies
courses.desc: Qubits, quantum gates, quantum circuits, quantum programming, the No Cloning Theorem, quantum teleportation, Bell inequalities, quantum cryptography, quantum sensing, photonic, superconducting and trapped ion implementations of quantum hardware.
courses.prereqs: MAT 022A B- or better; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
This course version is effective from, and including: Fall Quarter 2026.

courses.title: Advanced Nanostructured Devices
courses.desc: Physics of nano-structured materials and device operation. Overview of new devices enabled by nanotechnology; fabrication and characterization methods; applications of nano-structures and devices.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s); Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Optical Imaging & Microscopy
courses.desc: Theory and techniques of optical imaging & microscopy. Fourier optics; light propagation & light detection; imaging contrast mechanisms; optical & microscopy techniques.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Neuroengineering
courses.desc: Survey of neuroengineering field from engineering and biological perspectives; micro-/nano-fabrication technology; optical and electrical techniques to monitor and modulate neural activity; computational tools and control systems; prosthetics and human machine interfaces; human performance and rehabilitation; cognitive neuroengineering; neuroethics; extensive proposal development to merge aforementioned themes into a multidisciplinary project.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s); Discussion 1 hour(s); Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Micro- & Nano-Technology in Life Sciences
courses.desc: Survey of biodevice design from engineering and biological perspectives; micro-/nano-fabrication techniques; surface science and mass transport; essential biological processes and models; proposal development skills on merging aforementioned themes.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: ECH 245, EMS 245, MAE 245.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Projects in IC Fabrication
courses.desc: Individualized projects in the fabrication of analog or digital integrated electronic or optoelectronic circuits.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s), Laboratory 9 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Photovoltaics & Solar Cells
courses.desc: Physics and application of photovoltaics and solar cells, including design, fabrication technology, and grid incorporation. Mono and microcrystalline silicon devices; thin-film technologies, heterojunction and organic-semiconductor technologies. Collectors, electrical inverters and infrastructure issues. Challenges and concerns.
courses.prereqs: EEC 140B; or consent of instructor, or equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: EMS 246.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nanofabrication
courses.desc: Theory and practice of nanofabrication (top-down and bottom-up approaches), used for producing integrated circuits, electronic devices, sensors, and microstructures. Process development and characterization.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Linear Systems & Signals
courses.desc: Mathematical description of systems. Selected topics in linear algebra. Solution of the state equations and an analysis of stability, controllability, observability, realizations, state feedback and state estimation. Discrete-time signals and systems, and the Z-transform.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nonlinear Systems
courses.desc: Nonlinear differential equations, second-order systems, approximation methods, bifurcations, Lyapunov stability, absolute stability, Popov criterion, circle criterion, sliding-mode control, feedback linearization techniques.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Multivariable Control System Design
courses.desc: Review of single-loop feedback design. Stability, performance and robustness of multi-input multi-output control systems. H-infinity design. Frequency response methods. Optimization-based design. Algebraic design methods for uncertain systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Optimization
courses.desc: Understanding, analyzing, and solving constrained convex optimization problems arising in cutting-edge engineering and science fields, including machine learning, signal processing, networks, control, transportation, and circuit design. Convexity theory and the algorithmic approaches for convex optimization problem.
courses.prereqs: MAT 022A; or consent of instructor; working knowledge in Linear Algebra and Multivariate Calculus, knowledge of Python or MATLAB.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion/Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Robotic Systems
courses.desc: Introduction to robotic systems. Mechanical manipulators, kinematics, manipulator positioning and path planning. Dynamics of manipulators. Robot motion programming and control algorithm design.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Reinforcement Learning
courses.desc: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is the subset of machine learning, the core of artificial intelligence. Topics include fundamentals of RL, bandit problems, Markov decision processes, and dynamic programming.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Random Signals & Noise
courses.desc: Random processes as probabilistic models for signals and noise. Probability and random variables, Convergence and limit theorems, Specification of random processes, Markov Chains, Wiener process and white Gaussian noise, Poisson process and shot noise, Processing and frequency analysis of random signals.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Signal Processing for Communications
courses.desc: Signal processing in wireless and wireline communication systems. Characterization and distortion of wireless and wireline channels. Channel equalization and maximum likelihood sequence estimation. Channel precoding and pre-equalization. OFDM and transmit diversity. Array processing.
courses.prereqs: EEC 165; EEC 260; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Multi-access Communications Theory
courses.desc: Maximum stable throughput of Poisson collision channels. Classic collision resolution algorithms. Carrier sensing multiple access and its performance analysis. System stability analysis. Joint design of the physical/medium access control layers. Capacity region of multi-access channels. Multi-access with correlated sources.
courses.prereqs: (EEC 173A or ECS 152A); STA 120; or equivalent of STA 120.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Optimal & Adaptive Filtering
courses.desc: Geometric formulation of least-squares estimation problems. Theory and applications of optimum Wiener and Kalman filtering. MAP and maximum likelihood estimation of hidden Markov models, Viterbi algorithm. Adaptive filtering algorithms, properties and applications.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Estimation & Detection of Signals in Noise
courses.desc: Introduction to parameter estimation and detections of signals in noise. Bayes and Neyman-Pearson likelihood-ratio tests for signal detection. Maximum-likelihood parameter estimation. Detection of known and Gaussian signals in white or colored noise. Applications to communications, radar, signal processing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Principles of Digital Communications
courses.desc: Introduction to digital communications. Coding for analog sources. Characterization of signals and systems. Modulation and demodulation for the additive Gaussian channel. Digital signaling over bandwidth-constrained linear filter channels and over fading multipath channels. Spread spectrum signals.
courses.prereqs: EEC 165; EEC 260; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Information Theory & Coding
courses.desc: Topics include Entropy, Relatively Entropy, Mutual Information; Asymptotic Equipartition Property; Entropy Rates of Stochastic Process; Data Compression; Channel Capacity; Differential Entropy; Gaussian Channel; Rate Distortion Theory; Network Information Theory.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Mobile Communications
courses.desc: Time-varying multi-path fading channel models and receiver performance in fading channels; multiple access techniques and multiple access receivers design and performance; optimum design and the capacity of wireless channels.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Lab 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Error Correcting Codes: Algebraic Approach
courses.desc: Introduction to theory and practice of block codes, linear block codes, cyclic codes, decoding algorithms, and coding techniques.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Error Correcting Codes: Probabilistic Approach
courses.desc: Probabilistic approach to construct and decode error-correcting codes, coded communication systems, low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, polar codes, fountain codes, decoding algorithms.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.desc: Introduction to modern techniques for high-performance single and multiple processor systems. Topics include advanced pipeline design, advanced memory hierarchy design, optimizing pipeline and memory use, and memory sharing among multiprocessors. Case studies of recent single and multiple processor systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: High-Performance Computer Architecture
courses.desc: Designing and analysis of high performance computer architecture with emphasis on vector processing, on-chip interconnect networks, chip-level multiprocessors, memory and storage subsystem design and impact of technological advances on computer architecture.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Networking Architecture & Resource Management
courses.desc: Design & implementation principles of networking architecture and protocols. Internet, data center, and telephony case studies. Topics: Internet data & control planes; application & services; resource management; Quality of Service (QoS) provisioning; traffic engineering; performance evaluation, software-defined networks, & future research issues.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One and Pass Two only open to Graduate Students in Computer Science and Electrical & Computer Engineering.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Hardware Security
courses.desc: Hardware Security. Cryptographic processing and the analysis of its overhead, physical attacks, side-channel attacks and counter measures, physically unclonable functions, hardware-based random number generators, watermarking of Intellectual Property blocks, field-programmable gate array security, printed circuit board security, passive and active metering for prevention of piracy, and access control.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Modern Parallel Computing
courses.desc: Exploration of the architecture of modern parallel computers, their programming models, and their programming systems.
courses.prereqs: Prior experience in C/C++ required; experience with other computer architecture, computer graphics, algorithms, and data structures are also useful; all assignments use C/C++.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: VLSI Digital Signal Processing
courses.desc: Digital signal processors, building blocks, and algorithms. Design and implementation of processor algorithms, architectures, control, functional units, and circuit topologies for increased performance and reduced circuit size and power dissipation.
courses.prereqs: EEC 150B; EEC 170; (EEC 180 or EEC 180B); or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Machine Learning Systems & Hardware
courses.desc: Hardware architectures and systems for executing machine-learning workloads, with emphasis on dataflows, memory hierarchy, accelerator microarchitecture, hardware quantization,  hardware with support for model sparsity, and hardware–software co-design.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Design Verification of Digital Systems
courses.desc: Design verification techniques for digital systems; simulation-based design verification techniques; formal verification techniques, including equivalence checking, model checking, and theorem proving; timing analysis and verification; application of design certification techniques to microprocessors.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Design & Optimization of Embedded Computing Systems
courses.desc: Introduction to design and optimization of digital computing systems for embedded applications. Topics include combinatorial optimization techniques, performance and energy optimization in embedded systems, compilation and architecture-specific mapping, programmable and reconfigurable platforms; design automation and algorithmic improvements to design process.
courses.prereqs: EEC 170; (EEC 180 or EEC 180B); or consent of instructor. ECS 122A recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital System Testing
courses.desc: Review of several current techniques used to detect physical faults in both combinational and sequential circuits. Topics include fault modeling, fault simulation, test generation, compression techniques, and testing architectures.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Project.
