courses.title: Environmental Analysis
courses.desc: Analysis of the physical, biological, and social interactions which constitute environmental problems. Emphasis on analysis of environmental problems, the consequences of proposed solutions, and the interaction of environmental science and public policy in creating solutions.
courses.prereqs: UWP 001 (can be concurrent) or UWP 001Y (can be concurrent) or UWP 001V (can be concurrent) or ENL 003 (can be concurrent) or ENL 003V (can be concurrent); or equivalent; sophomore standing; ECN 001A and BIS 002B recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Current Issues in the Environment
courses.desc: Science behind environmental issues, and policies affecting our ability to solve domestic and international environmental problems. Resources, environmental quality, regulation, environmental perception and conservation. Integrative case studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ESP 001.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS); Scientific Literacy (SL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Careers in Environmental Science & Policy: Alumni Seminar
courses.desc: Environmentally focused career paths through presentations and discussions with alumni of the Environmental Science and Management and Environmental Policy Analysis and Planning majors. Each offering will feature a unique set of alumni speakers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated for credit.
Grade Mode: P/NP only.

courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the College of Agricultural & Environmental Sciences. Internship supervised by member of the faculty.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Primarily for lower division students.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: General Ecology
courses.desc: Theoretical & experimental analysis of the distribution, growth & regulation of species populations; predator-prey & competitive interactions; and the organization of natural communities. Application of evolutionary & ecological principles to selected environmental problems.
courses.prereqs: (BIS 002A,  BIS 002B,  BIS 002C); (MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 021A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B); STA 013 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken EVE 101.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Ecology, Nature, & Society
courses.desc: Interdisciplinary study of diversity and change in human societies, using frameworks from anthropology, evolutionary ecology, history, archaeology, psychology, and other fields. Topics include population dynamics, subsistence transitions, family organization, disease, economics, warfare, politics, and resource conservation.
courses.prereqs: ANT 001 or ANT 002 or ESP 030 or EVE 100 or BIS 101 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Cross Listing: ANT 101.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Community Ecology
courses.desc: Population growth and density dependence; predation; exploitative, interference and apparent competition; mutualism and facilitation; coexistence mechanisms; niches, spatial and temporal variation etc. Emphasis on quantitative understanding through models, concepts, and empirical evidence.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s); Discussion 1 hour(s).
Cross Listing: EVE 104.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Environmental Data Science
courses.desc: Programming with environmental data using R. Understanding data types, loops, branching and functions. Reproducible workflows and version control to import, organize, explore, analyze and visualize environmental data. Data science terminology and approaches. Common data sources used in environmental science and policy.
courses.prereqs: STA 013 (can be concurrent) or STA 013V (can be concurrent) or STA 013 (can be concurrent) or STA 032 (can be concurrent) or STA 100 (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Principles of Environmental Science
courses.desc: Application of physical and chemical principles, ecological concepts, and systems approach to policy analysis of atmospheric environments, freshwater and marine environments, land use, energy supplies and technology, and other resources.
courses.prereqs: (PHY 001A or PHY 007A); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B); BIS 002A or BIS 010 recommended; upper division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Marine Environmental Issues
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Examination of critical environmental issues occurring in coastal waters including the effects of climate change, overfishing, and other human impacts. Through readings and group discussions, students will develop an integrative understanding of the oceanographic and ecological processes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 2 time(s) when topic differs.
Cross Listing: EVE 111.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Oceanography
courses.desc: Advanced oceanographic topics: Chemical, physical, geological, and biological processes; research methods and data analysis; marine resources, anthropogenic impacts, and climate change; integrated earth/ocean/atmosphere systems; weekly lab and one weekend field trip.
courses.prereqs: GEL 001 or GEL 002 or GEL 016 or GEL 016V or GEL 050.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Fieldwork.
Cross Listing: GEL 116N.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Population Ecology
courses.desc: Development of exponential and logistic growth models for plant and animal populations, analysis of age structure, analysis of competition and predator-prey systems, and analysis of disease dynamics. Developing mathematical models and using them to make predictions and solve problems.
courses.prereqs: BIS 002B; (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 019C or MAT 021B or MAT 021BH).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 2.5 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Introduction to Field & Laboratory Methods in Ecology
courses.desc: Introduction to methods used for collecting ecological data in field and laboratory situations. Methods used by population ecologists and community ecologists; emphasis on experimental design, scientific writing and data analysis.
courses.prereqs: (ESP 100 or EVE 101); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100); or equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s), Fieldwork 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Marine & Coastal Field Ecology
courses.desc: Ecology of marine populations and communities living in diverse habitats along the California coast. Hands-on learning using scientific process and tools of the biological trade to address ecological questions arising during field trips. Critical thinking through discussing scientific literature.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing or consent of instructor; residence at or near Bodega Marine Lab required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 1 hour(s), Fieldwork 5 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Enrollment restricted to application at http://www.bml.ucdavis.edu.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Plant Conservation Biology
courses.desc: Principles governing the conservation of plant species and plant communities, including the roles of fire, exotic species, grazing, pollination, soils, and population genetics; analytic and practical techniques for plant conservation; and introduction to relevant legal, ethical, and policy issues.
courses.prereqs: ESP 100 or EVE 101; or equivalent upper division general ecology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Physical & Chemical Oceanography
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Physical and chemical properties of seawater, fluid dynamics, air-sea interaction, currents, waves, tides, mixing, major oceanic geochemical cycles.
courses.prereqs: (ESP 116N or GEL 116N); (PHY 007B or PHY 009B); (MAT 016C or MAT 017C or MAT 019C or MAT 021C); (CHE 002C or GEL 055); and consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Cross Listing: GEL 150A.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: Geological Oceanography
courses.desc: Introduction to the origin and geologic evolution of ocean basins. Composition and structure of oceanic crust; marine volcanism; and deposition of marine sediments. Interpretation of geologic history of the ocean floor in terms of sea-floor spreading theory.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: GEL 150B.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Biological Oceanography
courses.desc: Ecology of major marine habitats, including intertidal, shelf benthic, deep-sea and plankton communities. Existing knowledge and contemporary issues in research. Segment devoted to human use. One weekend field trip required.
courses.prereqs: BIS 002A; consent of instructor; a course in general ecology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Fieldwork.
Cross Listing: GEL 150C.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Limnology
courses.desc: Biology and productivity of inland waters with emphasis on the physical and chemical environment.
courses.prereqs: BIS 002A; BIS 002B; (BIS 002C and ESP 100 or EVE 101 recommended.)
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Limnology Laboratory
courses.desc: Limnological studies of lakes, streams, and reservoirs with interpretation of aquatic ecology.
courses.prereqs: ESP 151 (can be concurrent); junior, senior, or graduate standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Coastal Oceanography
courses.desc: Oceanography of coastal waters, including bays, river plumes, nearshore and estuaries; focus on transport patterns, how they are forced and implications for ecological and environmental problems. Pertinent for students in oceanography, ecology, environmental engineering, geology and hydrology.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing or consent of the instructor; physics (PHY 009B), calculus (MAT 021B) and exposure to physical and chemical oceanography (GEL 150A and ESP 150A) are recommended; residence at or near Bodega Marine Laboratory required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Fieldwork 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Enrollment restricted to application at http://www.bml.ucdavis.edu.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: The Policy Process
courses.desc: Alternative models of public policymaking and application to case studies in the U.S. and California.
courses.prereqs: POL 001 or POL 001Y; ECN 001A and STA 013 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Environmental Law
courses.desc: Introduction for non-Law School students to some of the principal issues in environmental law and the judicial interpretation of some important environmental statutes, e.g., NEPA.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing; one course in environmental science or political science recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Environmental Policy
courses.desc: Compares economic with socio-cultural approaches to understanding the causes of environmental problems and strategies for addressing them. Includes different approaches to the policy process, policy instruments, and environmental behavior. Applies these principles to several problems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Energy & Environmental Aspects of Transportation
courses.desc: Engineering, economic, and systems planning concepts. Analysis and evaluation of energy, air quality and selected environmental attributes of transportation technologies. Strategies for reducing pollution and petroleum consumption in light of institutional and political constraints. Evaluation of vehicle emission models.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing in engineering or economics or environmental studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to Civil Engineering, Environmental Science & Management, Environmental Policy Analysis & Planning majors.
Cross Listing: ECI 163.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Climate Policy
courses.desc: Models, data and assumptions behind competing arguments regarding societal response to the prospect of climate change at the state, national and international level from economic, ethical and policy science perspectives.
courses.prereqs: ESP 001 or ECN 001A  or ESP 001AY or ECN 001AV; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Ocean & Coastal Policy
courses.desc: Overview of U.S. and International ocean and coastal policy, including energy, coastal land-use and water quality, protected areas and species.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Energy Policy
courses.desc: Survey of primary energy resources (fossil, renewable, nuclear), energy conversion methods, future energy demand scenarios, and environmental impacts of energy. Overview of energy policy in the U.S. Analysis of policy alternatives for addressing energy-related environmental and national security issues.
courses.prereqs: (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); (MAT 016B or MAT 017B or MAT 021B); or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Methods of Environmental Policy Analysis
courses.desc: Evaluation of alternatives for solution of complex environmental problems; impact analysis, benefit cost analysis, distributional analysis, decision making under uncertainty, and multi-objective evaluation.
courses.prereqs: (ESP 001 or ESP 010); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100); (ECN 001A or ECN 001AY or ECN 001AV); ECN 100 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Methods of Environmental Policy Evaluation
courses.desc: Continuation of ESP 168A. Emphasis on examination of the literature for applications of research & evaluation techniques to problems of transportation, air & water pollution, land use, and energy policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Water Policy & Politics
courses.desc: Governance of water, including issues of water pollution/quality and water supply. Politics of water decision-making and effectiveness of water policy. Broad focus on federal water policy, with case examples from nationally significant U.S. watersheds.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Conservation Biology Policy
courses.desc: Analysis of policies designed to conserve species and their habitats. Emphasis on how individual incentives affect the success of conservation policies. Valuation of endangered species and biodiversity. Criteria for deciding conservation priorities.
courses.prereqs: One course in environmental science (e.g., ESP 001), conservation (e.g., WFC 011 or WFC 154), or government (e.g., POL 001) recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Urban & Regional Planning
courses.desc: How cities plan for growth in ways that minimize environmental harm. Standard city planning tools (general plan, zoning ordinance) and innovative new approaches. Focus on planning requirements and practices in California. Relationships between local, regional, state, and federal policy.
courses.prereqs: ESP 001 or ESP 161 or ESP 179 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Public Lands Management
courses.desc: Investigation of alternative approaches to public lands management by Federal and state agencies. Role each agency's legislation plays in determining the range of resource allocations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH).

courses.title: Land Use & Growth Controls
courses.desc: Exposes students to the economic, political, and legal factors affecting land use and growth controls, and helps students critically evaluate written materials in terms of their arguments and supporting data. May be taught abroad.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing; one course in environmental policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Environmental Justice Policy & Practice
courses.desc: History and frameworks of environmental justice; environmental justice policy; methods of spatial analysis. Emphasis on California and the United States.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Natural Resource Economics
courses.desc: Economic concepts and policy issues associated with natural resources, renewable resources (ground water, forests, fisheries, and wildlife populations) and non-renewable resources (minerals and energy resources, soil).
courses.prereqs: ARE 100A C- or better or ECN 100A C- or better or ECN 100AV C- or better or ECN 100 C- or better.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One open to Managerial Economics (AMGE), Environmental Policy Analysis & Planning (AEPP) Majors, Agricultural & Resource Economics (GARE) Graduate Majors.
Cross Listing: ARE 175.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Community Analysis for Environmental Justice
courses.desc: Community-engaged research on a local or regional environmental justice issue. Emphasis on skill development for applied projects.
courses.prereqs: ESP 001 or equivalent recommended; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Workshop 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Applied Research Methods
courses.desc: Research methods for analysis of urban and regional land use, transportation, and environmental problems. Survey research and other data collection techniques; demographic analysis; basic forecasting, air quality, and transportation models. Collection, interpretation, and critical evaluation of data.
courses.prereqs: STA 103 or STA 100 or STA 108 or SOC 106 or ARE 106; or the equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
courses.desc: Introduction to the information resources and methods typically used in environmental impact analysis. Emphasis on how environmental information is applied to planning, environmental regulation, and public policymaking, with case studies from California land use and natural resource policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Environmental Impact Reporting Using Geographic Information
courses.desc: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) by using ArcView for assessment and environmental planning.
courses.prereqs: ESP 179 (can be concurrent); ESP 179 required concurrently.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s), Laboratory 4 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ABT 180, ABT 181, or ASE 132.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Workshops on Environmental Problems
courses.desc: Workshops featuring empirical analyses of contemporary environmental problems by multidisciplinary student teams. Guided by faculty and lay professionals, the teams seek to develop an integrated view of a problem and outline a series of alternative solutions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 2-16 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to all upper division and graduate students on application.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; completion of 84 units.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-36 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Tutoring in Environmental Science & Policy
courses.desc: Experience in teaching under guidance of faculty member.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Tutorial 2-6 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Directed group study.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Environmental Policy Process
courses.desc: Introduction to selected theories of the policy process and applications to the field of environmental policy. Develops critical reading skills, understanding of policy theory, and an ability to apply multiple theories to the same phenomena.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing.
Cross Listing: ECL 212A.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Tropical Ecology
courses.desc: Overview of present status of knowledge on structure and processes of major tropical ecosystems. Differences and similarities among tropical and temperate systems stressed.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate and undergraduate students who meet requirement subject to consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Simulation Modeling
courses.desc: Advanced techniques in simulation modeling; optimization and simulation, dynamic parameter estimation, linear models, error propagation, and sensitivity testing. Latter half of course introduces model evaluation in ecological and social system models.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Economic Analysis of Resource & Environmental Policies
courses.desc: Development of externality theory, market failure concepts, welfare economics, theory of renewable and non-renewable resource use, and political economic models. Applications to policy issues regarding the agricultural/environment interface and managing resources in the public domain.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: ARE 275.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research Methods in Environmental Policy
courses.desc: Introduction to scientific research in environmental policy. Major issues in the philosophy of the social sciences. How to design research that acknowledges theoretical assumptions and that is likely to produce evidence in an intersubjectively reliable fashion with explicit recognition of its uncertainties.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Directed group study.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research
courses.desc: Research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.desc: Teaching assistant training practicum.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 3-12 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Toxicology
courses.desc: Hazardous substances, their effects on humans and their actions and movement in the environment. Emphasis on substances of current concern.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Introduction to Forensic Science
courses.desc: Basic principles of forensic science, types of information on which investigations focus, how information is obtained and used in criminal investigations, types of scientific skills required to practice forensic science, guidance on training. Real cases discussed; demonstrations of methods provided.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Chemical & Drug Use & Abuse
courses.desc: Overview of chemical use and abuse in our society. Effects of chemicals (therapeutic drugs, pesticides, food additives, herbal remedies, environmental contaminants, and recreational drugs) on humans and other living systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Contaminants in Our Environment
courses.desc: Contaminants in the environment (air, water, and soil) that influence the health of the environment, wildlife, and humans. An emphasis on contaminant properties, sources, and movement, public policy, and applying quantitative reasoning.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the College of Agricultural & Environmental Sciences. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-36 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Group study on focused topics in Environmental Toxicology. Topic varies according to instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: P/NP only.

courses.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for undergraduates.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Principles of Environmental Toxicology
courses.desc: Principles of toxicology with a focus on environmental, industrial, and natural chemicals. Topics include fate and effects of chemicals in organisms and the environment, air pollutants, insecticides, aquatic toxicology, endocrine disruptors, biomarkers and bioassays, and risk assessment.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Environmental Fate of Toxicants
courses.desc: Properties of toxic chemicals influencing their distribution and transformations; action of environmental forces affecting toxicant breakdown, movement, and accumulation; sources and occurrence of major classes of environmental toxicants.
courses.prereqs: CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 128B; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ETX 112A.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis of Environmental Toxicants
courses.desc: Sample preparation methods for trace analysis of environmental toxicants. Concept and techniques of advanced analytical instrumentation. Interpretation and use of analytical data.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed ETX 112B.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Biological Effects of Toxicants
courses.desc: Biological effects of toxic substances in living organisms. Metabolism, cellular and tissue targets, mechanisms of action, and pathological effects.
courses.prereqs: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; NPB 101  ETX 101 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken ETX 114A.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Biological Effects of Toxicants: Experimental Approaches
courses.desc: Experimental approaches for assessing the biological effects of toxicants.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken ETX 114B.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Environmental & Nutritional Factors in Cellular Regulation & Nutritional Toxicants
courses.desc: Cellular regulation from nutritional/toxicological perspective. Emphasis: role of biofactors on modulation of signal transduction pathways, role of specific organelles in organization/regulation of metabolic transformations, major cofactor functions, principles of pharmacology/toxicology important to understanding nutrient/toxicant metabolism.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Cross Listing: NUT 104.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Oral Skills (OL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Toxic Tragedies & Their Impact on Society
courses.desc: Examination of toxic tragedies, their origins, consequences, and effects on toxic regulation.
courses.prereqs: Upper division status or consent of instructor required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Introduction to Mass Spectrometry
courses.desc: Introduction to mass spectrometry, including ionization techniques, mass analyzers, interpretation of mass spectra, and applications of mass spectrometry. Emphasis on fundamental concepts of mass spectrometry necessary to identify and quantify organic molecules.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Perspectives in Aquatic Toxicology
courses.desc: Toxic substances, their fate in marine and freshwater systems, and their effects on aquatic organisms, populations, and ecosystems. Emphasis on substances and issues of current concern.
courses.prereqs: BIS 002A; CHE 002C; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Oral Skills (OL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Environmental Stress & Development in Marine Organisms
courses.desc: Taught at Bodega Marine Laboratory. Effects of environmental and nutritional stress, including pollutants, on development and function in embryos and larvae of marine organisms. Emphasis on advanced experimental methods.
courses.prereqs: ETX 101 or BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 104; and consent of instructor, or the equivalent; ETX 114A or NUT 114 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Laboratory 12 hour(s), Discussion 2 hour(s).
Cross Listing: NUT 127.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Oral Skills (OL); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Food Toxicology
courses.desc: Chemistry and biochemistry of toxins occurring in foods, including plant and animal toxins, intentional and unintentional food additives. The assessment of food safety and toxic hazards.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: FST 128.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Role & Applications of Toxicology in Modern Industry
courses.desc: Role of toxicology in industry research and development, human health and environmental protection, hazard and risk evaluations, risk management and communications, product stewardship, and regulatory compliance. Scientific principles and methods of toxicology in chemical, energy, pharmaceutical, pesticide, biotechnology industries.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Environmental Toxicology of Air Pollutants
courses.desc: Field trip required. Toxicology of air pollutants in the ambient, indoor, and occupational environments. Health effects, sources, environmental fates, pulmonary responses, sampling and analyses, and air-quality criteria and standards. Field trip required.
courses.prereqs: CHE 008B (can be concurrent); or the equivalent; BIS 102 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Health Risk Assessment of Toxicants
courses.desc: Current practices of health risk assessment of environmental chemicals using toxicological principles and their application to regulatory control of these chemicals.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Environmental Toxicology
courses.desc: Federal and California legislation concerning air and water pollution, pesticide use, food and feed additives, consumer protection, and occupational exposure to toxic substances; roles of federal regulatory agencies; alternatives to government control.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor. ETX 010 or ETX 101 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Genes & the Environment
courses.desc: Evaluation of evidence that human health and disease susceptibility result from complex interactions between genes and the environment. Critical thinking through problem solving using the scientific method with examples of cancer, metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurological health outcomes related to environmental and genetic risk factors and mechanisms.
courses.prereqs: BIS 002A (can be concurrent) or MCB 010 (can be concurrent) or BIS 101 (can be concurrent) or BIS 101V (can be concurrent); college-level coursework in environmental toxicology recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Exposure & Dose Assessment
courses.desc: Exposure component of risk assessment; specifically, the presence and/or formation of toxic substances in environmental media, their movement within and between contaminated media, and the contacts of human populations with those media.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Evolution in Human-Altered Environments
courses.desc: Effects of recent human alterations to the natural environment on the evolutionary trajectories of diverse species, including our own.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to upper division students.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Chemistry & Toxicology of Metals
courses.desc: Metal contaminants in the environment (air, water, and soil) and their effects on the health of the environment and humans. How the chemistry of metals ultimately controls their environmental fate and toxicity, application of numerical models, and discussion of case studies.
courses.prereqs: ETX 102A or CHE 008B or CHE 118B or CHE 128B; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: Selected topics presented by students, faculty, or outside speakers covering current research and instructional activities within environmental toxicology. Reports and discussion concerning oral and written presentations, literature sources, and career opportunities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 1 hour(s).

courses.title: Research Group Conference

courses.desc: Careers in environmental toxicology; discussions with graduates from the Department of Environmental Toxicology and other experts in the field.

Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Environmental Toxicants
courses.desc: Toxic chemicals: selected topics illustrating their occurrence, structure, and the reactions underlying detection, toxicity, fate, and ecological importance.
courses.prereqs: CHE 008B or CHE 128C; and consent of instructor, or the equivalent of CHE 128C.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Mechanisms of Toxic Action
courses.desc: Chemical, biochemical, and molecular mechanisms underlying the adverse effects of toxic chemicals. Students are required to write a grant proposal and participate in a grant review panel.
courses.prereqs: BIS 102 or BIS 102V; BIS 103; and consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Analysis of Toxicants
courses.desc: Principles of microanalysis of toxicants. Theoretical considerations regarding separation, detection and quantitative determination of toxicants using chemical and instrumental techniques.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: FOR 220.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Analysis of Toxicants Laboratory
courses.desc: Laboratory techniques for microanalysis of toxicants. Separation, detection, and quantitative determination of toxicants using chemical and instrumental methods.
courses.prereqs: ETX 220 (can be concurrent); consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Current Topics in Neurotoxicology
courses.desc: General principles of neurotoxicology, the cell and molecular mechanisms and health impacts of specific neurotoxicants and the contribution of neurotoxic compounds to complex eurodevelopmental disorders and neurodegenerative diseases.
courses.prereqs: Core courses in one of the following graduate programs: Pharmacology  Toxicology (PTX), Agricultural  Environmental Chemistry (AGC), Biochemistry  Molecular Biology (BMB), Cell  Developmental Biology (CDB), Immunology (IMM), Molecular Cellular  Integrative Physiology (MCP) or Neuroscience (NSC).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to upper level undergraduate students must obtain permission from the course coordinator.
Cross Listing: MCP 234, VMB 234.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ecotoxicology
courses.desc: Principles of toxicology as applied to chemical action on natural populations, communities, and ecosystems. Physical, chemical, and biological characteristics which influence ecotoxic effects, modeling, and field research. Selected case histories are analyzed and presented in class.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; elementary course in toxicology and ecology or the equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Reproductive Toxicology
courses.desc: Application of toxicological principles in reproductive studies. Effects of toxicants on the male, female, and developing embryo/fetus. Critical evaluation of reproductive toxicity studies and development of mechanistic approaches to understanding how chemical exposure can adversely affect reproduction.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1.50 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 1.50 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Immunotoxicology
courses.desc: Provides students with skills and knowledge for evaluating and applying research on the impact of environmental toxicants on immunological function in human and wildlife populations.
courses.prereqs: Undergraduate or graduate introduction to immunology coursework recommended but not required; graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Toxicology of Pesticides
courses.desc: Classification and chemical properties of pesticides, their mode of action, metabolism and disposition, pesticide resistance, effects on human health and ecological health and methods of risk benefit analyses.
courses.prereqs: ETX 101; one course each in (a) Organic Chemistry, (b) Biochemistry, (c) Toxicology (ETX 101 or equivalent), or with consent of instructor; graduate standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Molecular Techniques
courses.desc: Recombinant DNA technology and its applications.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: FOR 278.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Forensic DNA Analysis
courses.desc: Foundation in theory and practice of forensic DNA analysis; past, present, and emerging technologies; legal and quality assurance issues. DNA extraction, DNA quantitation, multiplex amplification of STR loci, capillary electrophoresis of amplified products, and analysis of STR typing data.
courses.prereqs: Coursework in genetics and molecular biology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Graduate standing; consent of instructor required for all students not enrolled in the MS Forensics program.
Cross Listing: FOR 280.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Principles & Practice of Forensic Serology & DNA Analysis
courses.desc: Comprehensive overview of forensic serology and DNA typing techniques and technologies. Strong emphasis on real-world applications, including preservation and tracking of biological evidence, detection and identification of bodily fluids, and methods to extract, quantify, and type human DNA.
courses.prereqs: (FOR 278 or ETX 278) or (FOR 280 or ETX 280); or equivalent; consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to students enrolled in the M.S. in Forensic Science Program or by consent of Forensic Science Program Director.
Cross Listing: FOR 281.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Non-Human Forensic DNA; Theory & Casework Application
courses.desc: Provides a comprehensive understanding of plant and animal forensic biology in terms of sample collection, preservation, analytical methods, and of the invaluable lines of inquiry these forensic evidence may permit.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor required for all students not enrolled in the MS Forensics program; upper division Molecular Biology and Genetics or its equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing.
Cross Listing: FOR 284.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quantitative Epidemiology I: Probability
courses.desc: Foundations in probability for epidemiologists. Emphasis on properties of and relationships between distributions and application of probability concepts to epidemiology. Includes a mathematical skills laboratory to assist in solution of epidemiologic problems.
courses.prereqs: ((MAT 016A,  MAT 016B) or (MAT 017A,  MAT 017B) or (MAT 021A,  MAT 021B)); STA 100; STA 108 (can be concurrent); or equivalent of any listed course with consent of instructor; concurrent or previous enrollment in a basic epidemiology course (e.g., EPI 205).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quantitative Epidemiology II: Statistical Inference
courses.desc: Provides the mathematical statistics foundation for statistical models, methods, and data analysis.
courses.prereqs: STA 108; (EPI 202 or STA 130A or STA 131A); (EPI 205 or MPM 205 or MPM 205V); ((MAT 017A B or better, MAT 017B B or better) or (MAT 021A B or better, MAT 021B B or better)); MAT 017C or MAT 021C or MAT 167 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Epidemiology graduate students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Quantitative Epidemiology III: Statistical Models
courses.desc: Introduces statistical models, methods, and data analysis in the areas of generalized linear model and survival analysis methodology.
courses.prereqs: STA 108; (EPI 203 or STA 130B or STA 131B); EPI 205.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Principles of Epidemiology
courses.desc: Basic epidemiologic concepts and approaches to epidemiologic research, with examples from veterinary and human medicine, including outbreak investigation, infectious disease epidemiology, properties of tests, and an introduction to epidemiologic study design and surveillance.
courses.prereqs: MPM 202; or consent of instructor; an introductory statistics course.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: MPM 205.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Epidemiologic Study Design
courses.desc: Builds on concepts presented in EPI 205. Concepts of epidemiologic study design (clinical trials, observational cohort studies, case control studies) introduced in EPI 205A are covered in more depth, using a problem-based format. Discussion of published epidemiologic studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 30 hour(s), Discussion 9 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Cross Listing: MPM 206.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methodology
courses.desc: In-depth integration of advanced epidemiological concepts. Theory, methods, and applications for observational studies including random and systematic error, confounding, counterfactuals, causal inference, effect modification, internal and external validity, estimability, and interpretation of effect measures, and advanced study designs.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Cross Listing: SPH 207.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Analysis & Interpretation of Epidemiologic Data
courses.desc: Application of theory and concepts of statistics and epidemiology to analysis and interpretation of data typically found in veterinary and human epidemiologic research.
courses.prereqs: EPI 204 (can be concurrent); EPI 207; (STA 144 or PHR 202); and entry level skill in standard statistical software; e.g., SPSS, BMDP, SAS, Stata, MinTab, S-Plus.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 16 hour(s), Laboratory 21 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: History of Epidemiology in Public Health
courses.desc: Introduction to the history of epidemiology in solving major public health problems. Original historical articles will be read/discussed. Topics may include: infectious disease, accidents/adverse events, nutritional deficiencies, community vaccination trials, occupational exposures, cancer, birth defects, cardiovascular disease, and smoking.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 0.50 hour(s), Discussion 1.50 hour(s).
Cross Listing: SPH 209.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Implementation Research in Health
courses.desc: Introduction to concepts and methods in implementation science, including theories, models and frameworks, qualitative and mixed methods, adaptations, and common study designs in implementation research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
courses.desc: Basic and advanced level of conceptual and methodological foundations in infectious disease epidemiology necessary for veterinarians to develop and evaluate programs for detection, prevention, and control of infectious diseases in animal populations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Cross Listing: MPM 212.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Problems in Epidemiologic Study Design
courses.desc: Design and development of research protocols and funding applications for peer review. Application of research methods data collection and management and statistical analysis in research proposals. Methods of evaluating research proposals, mechanisms of funding, specifying human subjects considerations.
courses.prereqs: MPM 405; STA 102; STA 106; or the equivalent; MPM 406 or the equivalent; PHR 207 required concurrently.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Spatial Epidemiology
courses.desc: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and spatial statistics. Students are expected to complete a term project based on their graduate research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Health & Ecological Risk Analysis
courses.desc: Methodological approach to risk analysis for human and animal-related health and ecological issues. Basic principles of risk analysis, including perception, communication, assessment and management. Emphasis on the assessment of risk.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Epidemiology Methods
courses.desc: In-depth study of topics in epidemiology theory and methods, selected from: causal inference, confounding, study design, or other related areas, with year to year variation. Readings are assigned and students are expected to lead discussions on the readings.
courses.prereqs: EPI 205; EPI 206; EPI 207; or equivalents, with consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Methods for Longitudinal & Repeated Measurement Data
courses.desc: Mixed models for longitudinal data (LD)/repeated measurements; Mean and covariance models; General linear LD models; Random coefficients models; Linear mixed effects models for continuous outcome; Generalized linear mixed effects model for discrete outcome including binary, ordinal and count data.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Meta Analysis
courses.desc: Systematic review, standard and advanced statistical methods for meta-analysis and syntheses of knowledge and evidence. Quantitative analysis of published data, primarily in aggregate form. Students demonstrate skills in study design, protocol, analysis, and results reporting through presentation of drafted first author paper.
courses.prereqs: A course in basic statistics or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Geographic Information Systems for Health Professionals
courses.desc: Emphasis on basic geographic and data management principles. Focus on software proficiency in application to analyzing/solving health-related problems. For graduate and professional students in epidemiology, public health, preventive veterinary medicine, health informatics with interest in spatial techniques in research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Molecular Epidemiology
courses.desc: Overview of the modern field of molecular epidemiology. Integrates molecular biology into traditional epidemiologic research by identifying pathways, molecules and genes that influence the risk of developing disease.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Infectious Disease Epidemiology
courses.desc: Infectious disease epidemiology and prevention, with emphasis on human and veterinary diseases of global health importance. Major global health epidemics and challenges of infectious diseases, by mode of transmission.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Data Analysis with SAS
courses.desc: Provide an overview of common advanced statistical methods as well as a treatment of how to use SAS to implement them. Learn the ideas of reproducible research and reporting of statistical analyses.
courses.prereqs: EPI 202; EPI 203; EPI 204; or the equivalent, or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Principles of Injury Epidemiology
courses.desc: Overview of the epidemiology of human injury, including general principles, surveillance methods, behavioral factors, environmental factors, treatment issues and engineering and legal interventions related to vehicular injuries, drownings, falls, fires and burns, poisonings, firearm injuries, and other intentional injuries.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Critical Thinking in Epidemiology
courses.desc: Critical thinking in Epidemiology.
courses.prereqs: EPI 205 B or better; EPI 206 B or better; EPI 207 (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Epidemiology Graduate Group students or advanced medical students only; limited to 15 students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Environmental Epidemiology
courses.desc: Examination of the human health effects and the risk of disease from community, occupational, and personal exposure to toxic substances.
courses.prereqs: MPM 405 (can be concurrent); upper division undergraduates who have completed EST 126; or the equivalent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Epidemiology of Chronic Diseases & Aging
courses.desc: Overview of the epidemiology of chronic disease in old age. Topics include biology of aging, epidemiology of cardiovascular disease, neoplasms, osteoporosis and fractures, psychosocial factors and health in old age, dementias, functional status and prevention of disease.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research Methods in Occupational Epidemiology
courses.desc: Methods used in epidemiologic research on occupational hazards. Topics include design and analysis of cohort and case-control studies, sample size, measuring dose, choosing a control group, validation of employment and health data, interpreting negative studies, and analysis software.
courses.prereqs: (EPI 205 or MPM 205 or MPM 205V); (MPM 202 or STA 100).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cancer Epidemiology
courses.desc: Covers the underlying concepts essential to understanding cancer epidemiology, such as trends in incidence and survival, epidemiologic methods used to assess cancer etiology, prevention and control, and an introduction to the cancer initiation and progression multi-stage model.
courses.prereqs: EPI 205; EPI 206 (can be concurrent); STA 100; must have basic understanding of epidemiologic and statistical concepts covered in the listed courses.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Recitation 1 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Mathematical Models in Epidemiology
courses.desc: Theory of epidemics and mathematical modeling concepts for infectious diseases to include discrete and continuous time models, their use to explore disease dynamics and investigate prevention and control strategies for human and veterinary infectious diseases.
courses.prereqs: MPM 403; MPM 405; consent of instructor; although not required, students encouraged to refresh their knowledge of high school calculus and differential equations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 30 students.
Cross Listing: PHR 277.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to SAS Programming
courses.desc: Introduction to SAS, an integrated software system for data retrieval and management, data manipulation and programming.
courses.prereqs: Introductory statistics course; e.g., MPM 402, STA 102.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Cross Listing: SPH 280.

courses.title: Food Chemistry & Biochemistry
courses.desc: Advanced topics in food chemistry and biochemistry, emphasizing the application of the basic principles of chemistry and biochemistry to food composition, properties, preservation and processing. Chemical structures, interactions, reaction mechanisms and experimental methods are stressed.
courses.prereqs: Undergraduate courses in organic chemistry and biochemistry; undergraduate course in food chemistry is recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to Food Science graduate level standing or consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Foods
courses.desc: Fundamental principles of chemistry and physics are applied to a study of changes in water binding properties and activity, changes in proteins, nutrients, toxic constituents, and other compounds during storage, heating, freezing, dehydrating, and concentrating of food materials.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Food Processing
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Principles of food engineering applied to food processing. Relationship of Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluid properties to heat and momentum transfer. Application of mass transfer in controlling kinetics and quality changes of foods.
courses.prereqs: FST 110A; PHY 007C); CHE 107B; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Food Microbiology
courses.desc: Principles and recent developments in food microbiology. Mechanisms of foodborne disease, pathogen detection, parameters of microbial growth and control in foods, intestinal microbiology including probiotics and prebiotics, and the microbiology of food and beverage fermentations.
courses.prereqs: Undergraduate level coursework in microbiology, or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Industrial Microbiology
courses.desc: Use of microorganisms for producing substances such as amino acids, peptides, enzymes, antibiotics and organic acids. Emphasis on metabolic regulation of pathways leading to fermentation products, on yeast fermentations, and on genetic manipulations (including recombinant DNA techniques) of industrial microorganisms.
courses.prereqs: BIS 001A; BIS 102 or BIS 102V; BIS 103; MIC 130A and MIC 130B or BIS 101 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Sensory-Instrumental Analyses
courses.desc: Basic principles of measurement of color, texture, and flavor of foods by sensory and instrumental methods. Advanced statistical analysis of relation of colorimetry, texturometry, and chemistry of volatile compounds to perception of appearance, texture, flavor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Proteins: Functional Activities & Interactions
courses.desc: Relationships of structure of proteins to their biological functions. Structural proteins, complexing proteins, and catalytic proteins in plant and animal materials and products.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Lipids: Chemistry & Nutrition
courses.desc: Chemistry of lipids as it pertains to research in food and nutrition. Relations between lipid structure and their physical properties in tissues and foods. Regulation of absorption, transport, and metabolism of lipids. Implications of dietary fats and health.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Flavor Chemistry of Foods & Beverages
courses.desc: Become familiar with basic principles of flavor chemistry, analysis, and formation in fresh and processed foods. Required to read and critically evaluate flavor chemistry literature.
courses.prereqs: CHE 008B; VEN 123; (VEN 123L or FST 103); or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: VEN 213.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Food Sensory Science
courses.desc: Advanced study of the techniques and theory of the sensory measurement of food as an analytical tool and as a measure of consumer perception and acceptance. Advanced examination of the sensory and cognitive systems associated with the perception of food.
courses.prereqs: FST 107 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Biochemistry, Microbiology & Technology of Cheeses of the World
courses.desc: Compositional and physico-chemical aspects of milk and their implications on cheesemaking; enzymatic, microbiological and physical aspects of cheesemaking; cheese as a biological composite; designing cheese quality attributes; cheese aging. Cheese from all over the world tasted and discussed.
courses.prereqs: FST 119; (BIS 103 or FST 100A); FST 123; BIS 103; CHE 107B; CHE 128B; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate level students or senior undergraduate students with appropriate background in biochemistry and microbiology.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Food Perception & the Chemical Senses
courses.desc: Examination of the anatomy and physiology of the chemical senses (taste, smell, and the trigeminal senses) and how they are involved in the perception of food and food intake.
courses.prereqs: FST 107B (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sustainable Food Systems
courses.desc: Environmental impacts of food systems. Methods for quantifying resource use and managing waste for food production and processing. Influence of policies, technologies, and consumer demand on advancing sustainable food systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Food & Gut Microbiota
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Impact of specific food structures on the structure and function of the animal gut microbiota. How food is transformed by, and modulates, the gut microbiota to provide the host with nutrients and protection.
courses.prereqs: Microbiology and molecular biology undergraduate coursework or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1.50 hour(s), Discussion 1.50 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Upper division or graduate standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Design Thinking of Food
courses.desc: Tools of design thinking as applied to high-impact, food-related challenges through a multi-disciplinary team based, experiential learning process. Application of the field of food studies to the social and cultural contexts of eating habits, food systems, and the design solutions that respond to these factors. Working with stakeholders to design innovative solutions to food system challenges.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s); Fieldwork.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.
