courses.title: White Collar Investigations & Prosecutions
courses.desc: Explore a fictional white-collar crime, learning how to establish probable cause through cooperative witnesses; search warrants, the utilization of informants, and indemnity agreements will be analyzed. Learn about indictments, complaints, laws surrounding arrests, bail hearings, evidentiary suppression motions, and grand jury indictments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Federal Jurisdiction
courses.desc: Study of subject-matter jurisdiction of federal courts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: California Civil Procedure: A Practical Approach
courses.desc: Practical, hands-on approach to California Civil Procedure through case studies, drafting of common litigation documents, and studying the application of the Code of Civil Procedure to practical case scenarios. Issues of general civil litigation emphasizing bar exam topics are included.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Taxation of Partnerships & LLCs
courses.desc: Study of the federal income tax treatment of partnerships and partners; including entities classified as partnerships.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Taxation
courses.desc: Major topics include worldwide taxation as applied to individuals (immigrants); source of income definitions in American tax law; concepts in inbound taxation, e.g., U.S. taxation of foreign persons; outbound taxation, e.g., U.S. taxation of foreign income.
courses.prereqs: LAW 220 (can be concurrent); completion or current enrollment in a course covering the domestic taxation of corporations is suggested but not required; LAW 247B can be concurrent.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Corporate Tax
courses.desc: Examination of the federal income tax relationship between corporations and their owners. Covers the transfer of funds into a corporation on formation and the re-transfer of money and property from the corporation to its shareholders.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion/Laboratory.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Taxation of Business Entities
courses.desc: Introduction to federal income taxation of business entities.
courses.prereqs: LAW 220; prerequisite will not be waived.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Law
courses.desc: Covers major topics in international and transnational law, including treaties and customary international law, international courts and tribunals, jurisdiction and immunities, use of force and law of armed conflict, and international criminal law.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Jurisdiction in Cyberspace Seminar
courses.desc: Review concepts in international law, conflicts of law, cyberlaw, and federal jurisdiction to address the growing multi-jurisdictional conflicts created by the Internet. Examine European efforts at crafting intra-Europe jurisdictional rules, as well as other international jurisdiction treaty projects such as those at the Hague.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Human Rights in Context
courses.desc: Overview of the theory and practice of human rights law. Requirements include weekly discussion responses, a seminar paper, and active class participation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: United Nations Human Rights Practicum I
courses.desc: Opportunity to work in support of the mandate of the United Nations Special Rapporteur in the field of cultural rights.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: United Nations Human Rights Practicum II
courses.desc: Build on the knowledge of the workings of the United Nations human rights system they gained in Practicum I, and gain further advanced experience working with UN documents, with individual cases in the field and with thematic reports.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Globalization & the Law
courses.desc: Globalization of people, finance, goods, services, and information puts pressure on the nation-state form. In a world of diasporas and multinational corporations, what does citizenship mean?
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Legal Spanish for U.S. Lawyers
courses.desc: Designed for law students who are native Spanish-speakers or who have achieved proficiency in Spanish through study or experiences in a Spanish-speaking country.
courses.prereqs: Must satisfy one of the following: undergraduate degree in Spanish; a minor in Spanish with experience living in a Spanish-speaking country; grew up in a Spanish-speaking household and achieved proficiency; able to pass an informal assessment by the instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Advanced International Law
courses.desc: Review books of international law; Hugo Grotius and Judge Rosalyn Higgins. Themes include peaceful resolutions of dispute, law of war and peace, and international legal process.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Law
courses.desc: Uses of comparative method, principal differences between common law and civil law and the styles of legal reasoning that prevail in these two great legal cultures. Topics include the evolution of the civil law, the phenomenon of codification, the structure of European civil codes and the interpretation of their provisions, the respective roles of counsel, judges and law teachers, civil law procedure, and the analysis of selected areas of substantive law. Knowledge of a foreign language is not required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: First Gen Experience in Scholarly & Popular Literature
courses.desc: Provides an opportunity for "first-gen" students to reflect on their own educational journeys by reading scholarly studies and commentary, as well as memoir by famous first-gen lawyers; e.g., Justice Sotomayor, Michelle Obama, and fiction.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Jurisprudence Seminar
courses.desc: Deals principally with the question of how judges should decide "hard cases," where the content of the law is in doubt and competent arguments have or could be offered for mutually inconsistent decisions in favor of either party.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Writing Workshop
courses.desc: Second- and third-year students produce a piece of academic writing that satisfies the King Hall writing requirement and is of publishable quality. Receive feedback both from the instructor and from one another in a workshop setting.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Labor Law
courses.desc: Survey of the legislative, administrative, and judicial regulation of labor relations under federal law. Historical development of labor law, the scope of national legislation, unions, strikes, picketing, and collective bargaining agreements.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Labor Law Practicum
courses.desc: Develops a theoretical and practical understanding of the labor movement, and the ways in which lawyers support and interact with the movement. Placement in labor organizations, labor-related law firms, and non-profits to gain experience with different aspects of labor organizing, labor campaigns, and collective bargaining.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Fieldwork..
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: California Labor Code
courses.desc: Topics related to California labor and employment law, especially those covered in the California Labor Code. Most meet during summer, after regular work hours; one final meeting of the course during the fall semester (week 1).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): For important scheduling information, review the expanded course description on the Law School website.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Litigation & Arbitration
courses.desc: Current developments in international law, conflict of laws, civil procedure, arbitration, and comparative law in the context of transactions and disputes that cut across national boundaries.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Criminal Litigation; Pre-Trial
courses.desc: Utilizes experiential learning techniques to teach advocacy skills during the life of a criminal case and simulates critical stages of the proceedings by conducting mock hearings throughout the semester.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Policy Advocacy
courses.desc: In-depth examination of the legislative process both within the California Legislature and from the advocates’ perspective. Train in key policy advocacy skills by legislative leaders and social justice advocates.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Community Lawyering
courses.desc: Study the need for community lawyering including the structural inequalities and privileges embedded in the legal system and society. Skills necessary for community lawyering as well as sites and models for practice will be examined.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Public Interest Law & Advocacy
courses.desc: Introduction to the applied legal and policy skills necessary to become effective lawyers and advocates in the international public interest/nongovernmental organization community.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Housing Law
courses.desc: Survey course covers legal and policy issues related to developing, protecting and preserving affordable, safe and accessible housing and sustaining viable, diverse communities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Law & Rural Livelihoods
courses.desc: This seminar considers rural manifestations of various legal, social and economic phenomena. We survey various subfields of law in relation to the rural-urban continuum, and we discuss rurality as an aspect of identity that intersects with other aspects of identity.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Credit Limitation(s): No credit if student has taken LAW 254C.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Access to Justice
courses.desc: Study of a variety of barriers that impede the access of unrepresented litigants to the courts–including poverty, racial bias, limited English proficiency and the digital divide–and critically examine existing solutions. Opportunity to develop and propose student's own solution to an access barrier.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: White Working Class & the Law
courses.desc: Considers the social, cultural, economic, and legal situation of low-income and/or low-education whites in contemporary U.S. society.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Students who have taken LAW 254A previously are not eligible for this course.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Pension & Employee Benefits Law
courses.desc: Federal regulation and taxation of private pensions and employee benefits. Covers the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) and Internal Revenue Code issues.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Land Use
courses.desc: Addresses administrative, legislative, and judicial applications of land use planning and development laws. Topics include zoning, general plans, local government regulation, and California's Environmental Quality Act.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Legislative Process & Statutory Interpretation
courses.desc: Fundamental elements of federal and state legislative process, including legislative procedure, with a focus on statutory interpretation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Legislative Intent Seminar
courses.desc: Theories and principles of statutory and constitutional interpretation. Original intent vs. living constitution; permissible kinds of evidence for determining legislative intent; canons of construction; extent to which initiatives should be interpreted similarly to legislative enactments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Statutory Interpretation
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Elective course for Environmental Law Certificate Program. Provides an introduction to the theory and practice of statutory interpretation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Applied Statutory Interpretation: California’s Housing-Framework Legislation
courses.desc: Theory and practice of statutory interpretation using case studies from the body of California law concerned with locally-erected barriers to housing supply. Grading based on a set of writing assignments derived from real-world cases.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Legislative Drafting
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Legislative Drafting provides practical experience in researching, analyzing, and drafting all legislative measures in the State of California, including bills, resolutions, and constitutional amendments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Professional Responsibility
courses.desc: The ABA's Model Rules of Professional Conduct and the Code of Judicial Conduct, which are tested on the MPRE, and the California Rules of Professional Conduct, which are tested on the California Bar Examination.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Closed to students who have taken LAW 258A.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Legal Ethics & Organizational Practice
courses.desc: Explores ethics rules governing the legal profession, including state Rules of Professional Conduct (RPCs) and the ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct. Discern how the various RPCs differ, and we apply them to real-life situations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Closed to students who have taken LAW 258 or 258H.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Mindfulness & the Law
courses.desc: Reviews the American Bar Association's Model Rules of Professional Conduct and the Code of Judicial Conduct, as tested on the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination, and  covers California Rules of Professional Conduct, which are tested on the California Bar Examination.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Conscious Lawyering
courses.desc: Introductions to the practice of conscious lawyering. Includes concepts in professional and personal identity, self-awareness, focus, emotional intelligence, cultural and personal values, mindfulness, meditation, and mind-body connection.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Practice 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Starting & Managing a Small Law Practice
courses.desc: Using real practice examples, in this discussion/simulation-based course learn how to open and successfully run a small law practice. Included topics: structure and organization, office set-up, billing, fees, time management, client handling, overseeing office staff, trust accounting, and ethical rules.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Utility of Law School & Careers in the Law
courses.desc: Despite improvements in the economy, some observers continue to question whether law school is a viable option for college graduates. Considers the controversy and expose students to the variety of careers in the legal profession.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Practice Ready Seminar
courses.desc: Includes a discussion and review of the role of the junior attorney within a law firm/legal department, professional goal-setting, strategies for effective communication and work within teams, delegation and resource management, organization and time management, an introduction to common junior-level assignments and how to complete them efficiently and effectively, building a professional network, and an introduction to business development, among other topics.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Business Fundamentals for Lawyers
courses.desc: Overview of basic concepts of accounting and finance and their application to business valuation and in business contracts..
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Professional Responsibility
courses.desc: Ethical duties of lawyers in a variety of different contexts. Examines topics such as client control over the major decisions in a case, the duty of zealous advocacy, representation of organizations, and the unique role of government attorneys. Covers the American Bar Association’s Model Rules of Professional Conduct and the California Rules of Professional Conduct, which are tested (respectively) on the MPRE and the California Bar Exam.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Students who take this course are ineligible for Law 258 and Law 258A.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Lawyers, the Rule of Law & Democracy
courses.desc: Seminar explores lawyer's roles, ethical obligations and critical choices regarding maintaining and preserving rule of law and democracy, by examining historical and contemporary scenarios. Class participation expected.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: High Performance Lawyering
courses.desc: Improve the skills most determinative of success and satisfaction: communication, judgment, leadership, rapport building, collaboration, resilience, self-awareness, ethical decision making, strategic thinking, and professionalism.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Feminist Legal Theory
courses.desc: Provides an overview of feminist legal theory and considers how its various strands inform legislative and judicial law making. Satisfies Advanced Writing Requirement.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Women, Islam & the Law
courses.desc: Study legal and religious reform movements for women's rights within Muslim communities in the context of current scholarly and political debates about fundamentalism, democracy, equality, secularism, universalism, and multiculturalism.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Women's Human Rights
courses.desc: Overview of international legal and institutional system for the protection of women’s human rights from an academic perspective and the view of the practitioner. Includes the (CEDAW), violence against women, sexual and reproductive rights, economic rights, and more.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Employment Discrimination
courses.desc: Examination of federal laws prohibiting employment discrimination.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Employment Law
courses.desc: Employment Law surveys the web of rules governing the law of work, from limits on at-will employment and privacy at work to labor law, family leave, and workplace discrimination.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Judicial Process
courses.desc: Examines a variety of issues concerning the judicial process. Focus is on judge's role in the legal process, the administration of justice, ethical issues, decision making, bias, and critical examination of the strengths and weaknesses in our current judicial system.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Judicial Process
courses.desc: Comparative law course focused on judicial institutions and judicial decision-making around the world.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Antitrust
courses.desc: Focus on the federal antitrust laws, concentrating on basic substantive areas of the Sherman and Clayton Acts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Regulated Industries
courses.desc: Examines regulation of business in sectors, traditionally described as “common carrier” and “utility” industries, where because of market failures normal competitive mechanism will not protect consumers from exercises of market power.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Criminal Trials: Theory & Practice
courses.desc: Trial advocacy centered on client relationship building, preparation for trial, and courtroom practice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Trial Practice
courses.desc: Introduction to trial. Featuring lectures, demonstrations, assigned readings, and trial drills. Formulate trial strategy, theory and theme and conduct all phases of a trial, including opening statements, direct and cross examinations, and closing arguments. Evening laboratory is 2 hours; held on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday evenings.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s), Laboratory 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Advanced Trial Practice
courses.desc: Train on the organization and presentation of a complex trial, including pretrial preparation, jury selection, strategy considerations, evidentiary issues, and effective handling of plaintiff and defense cases through verdict.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Class limited to 40 students.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Voir Dire: Theory & Practice
courses.desc: Teaches (1) the law that restricts and supports jury selection in criminal law trials, (2) the most effective methods of engaging in jury selection, (3) how to think critically and strategically about voir dire questioning and juror challenges.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Domestic Violence Trial Advocacy
courses.desc: Trial Advocacy Course designed for domestic violence cases in Family Court, for certified law students, under the supervision of an attorney, to assist with evidentiary hearings/trials.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Practice 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Parole Law & Practice
courses.desc: Parole law and practice provide knowledge and understanding of substantive and procedural law pertaining to criminal parole hearings, and include simulated client preparation and representation in a simulated parole hearing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Practice 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Water Law
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Water supply, use, infrastructure, and organizations; rights in surface waters, including riparian rights, prior appropriation, and federal reserved rights; environmental and constitutional constraints on water use; groundwater rights and management; drought and emergency water curtailment; interaction of state and federal law; contemporary case studies and challenges; water equity considerations.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ocean & Coastal Law
courses.desc: Introduction to the goals and challenges of coastal and ocean policy; the complicated web of public and private interests in coastal lands and ocean waters; regulation of coastal development; domestic and international fisheries management; and preservation of ocean resources.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Natural Resources Law Seminar
courses.desc: In-depth coverage of two foundational principles of natural resources law: public trust doctrine and private property rights protected under the Takings Clause of the U.S. and many state constitutions.
courses.prereqs: LAW 285 or LAW 256 recommended, but not required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to 15 students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Commercial Law
courses.desc: Survey of commercial transactions law under the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). Covers a number of topics under Articles 2, 3, & 9 of the UCC. Topics include attachment and perfection of security interests in personal property and general principles of negotiability. Primary goals are to provide a foundational knowledge and understanding of several articles of the UCC and improve problem-solving skills in this area.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cyber Law & Artificial Intelligence
courses.desc: Examines from a globalized perspective a broad range of internet governance issues, ranging from free speech, hate speech, defamation, copyright, intermediary liability, administrative censorship online, online anonymity, privacy, data protection, etc.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence & the Law
courses.desc: Looks at AI's seemingly infinite possibilities and discusses where should the legal boundaries begin and end. Core lecturing centers on the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the proposed EU AI Regulation requirements.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Law Practice
courses.desc: Facilitates competent and ethical integration of generative AI in legal practice through interactive use and evaluation of various AI tools. Covers technical foundations, professional responsibility issues, and policy questions related to AI in the legal profession.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Practice 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: AI & Intellectual Property
courses.desc: Learn how to represent clients facing novel issues relating to Artificial Intelligence and intellectual property. Dig deep into recent cases to see how lawyers are addressing these issues today, and prepare your own persuasive brief representing a hypothetical client.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Civil Rights Law
courses.desc: Civil remedies for civil rights violations under the primary United States civil rights statute. Specifically, covers actions for constitutional and statutory violations under 42 USC §1983, affirmative defenses, and abstention doctrines.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Basic Finance for Lawyers
courses.desc: Basic techniques of analysis that are part of the core curriculum in a good business school. Gives background necessary for understanding and advising your clients and for understanding other business-related law school courses.
courses.prereqs: Students with a non-law basic finance course will not be admitted, except with consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Consumer Protection & Financial Regulation
courses.desc: Examines laws seeking a “fair” financial marketplace, including markets for consumer credit, residential mortgages, and student lending through Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; disclosure; and prohibitions on unfair, deceptive, and abusive acts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.desc: Focus on how corporations raise money, stocks and bonds, etc.; how deals are structured and why corporations use one strategy instead of another.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Seminar on Financial Regulation
courses.desc: Introduction to the legal and regulatory issues presented by contemporary capital markets.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Public Finance
courses.desc: Introduction to the basic concepts of public finance, the underlying law governing public finance: in particular state law, federal tax law and federal securities law.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Fintech Innovation & Financial Inclusion
courses.desc: Focuses on fintech innovation and financial inclusion. Explores how fintech is transforming traditional financial services and providing new opportunities and challenges for financial inclusion.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Business Transactions
courses.desc: Survey introducing various forms of international business transactions and the regulatory environment within which international business takes place.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Life-Cycle Transactions & Drafting
courses.desc: Focuses on analysis of contract drafting design for various types of transactions and actual transactional documents typically encountered.
courses.prereqs: Business Associations and/or Trusts, Wills  Estates are recommended for enhanced comprehension.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Contract Drafting & Development
courses.desc: Complete complex contracts. Learn various approaches to completing contracts (from term sheet to final document) and complete exercises and assignments to hone contract skills. Build a “contract skills toolbox” with the tools needed for completing and drafting contracts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Transactional Lawyering Skills: Contract Drafting for Tech
courses.desc: Skills-based course applies legal concepts to client counselling and drafting of effective business documents with emphasis on the tech industry. Solve problems, analyze risk, and draft contracts in a real-world context.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nonprofit Organizations & Drafting
courses.desc: Learn special legal rules and concepts applicable to non-profit organizations; particularly IRC 501(c)(3) nonprofits. Combination skills class and lecture class.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Extensive Writing/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to 13 students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: NonProfit Organizations: State & Local Governance Issues
courses.desc: Focuses on the state and local laws applicable to nonprofit organizations; i.e., public interest, cultural, religious, educational and other not-for-profit entities.
courses.prereqs: LAW 215 (can be concurrent); or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nonprofit Organizations: Tax Exemptions & Taxation Focus
courses.desc: Focuses on the conceptual basis and substantive law criteria for the federal and state income tax exemption of nonprofit organizations.
courses.prereqs: LAW 215; or consent of instructor; LAW 220 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Family Law
courses.desc: Introduction to the legal regulation of the family.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Education Policy & the Law
courses.desc: Education law and policy, focusing in particular on efforts to use the law and policy to improve educational outcomes for disadvantaged children.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Special Education Law & Policy
courses.desc: Introduction to the law of special education including the Individuals with Disabilities in Education Act (IDEA), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, and federal regulations governing special education law.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Intellectual Property
courses.desc: Provides a broad survey of intellectual property law. Areas covered include trade secrets, patents, copyrights, and trademarks. Examines legal doctrine as well as the theories and policies animating the intellectual property system.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Intellectual Property & Development
courses.desc: Examines international trade law, national customs law, intermediary liability rules, claims for rights in traditional knowledge and genetic resources, protections for geographical indications, technology transfer, and intellectual property piracy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Trade Secrets
courses.desc: Focuses on the law of trade secrets, including the DTSA, the UTSA, current case law developments, and the overlap between trade secret laws and employment laws. No technical background required.
courses.prereqs: LAW 274; or consent or instructor; prior coursework in property, torts, evidence, and contracts recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Intellectual Property in Historical Context Seminar
courses.desc: How the legal system has adapted to earlier periods of rapid change by creating, delimiting, and expanding intellectual property rights (IPRs). Required paper satisfies advanced writing requirement.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Theory & History of Intellectual Property
courses.desc: Seminar traces development of intellectual property law in the U.S. and Europe because it is not possible to understand the logic and shape of current Intellectual Property concepts outside of their messy history.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Current Controversies in Intellectual Property Law
courses.desc: Examine controversial topics in intellectual property law and policy across a wide range of issues, from technology to the arts, to social justice, in their national and international dimensions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International & Comparative Intellectual Property
courses.desc: Examines the international regulation of intellectual property rights and explores the place of the United States in the international IP community. Discusses international treaties and legal harmonization efforts, legislation and case law from different jurisdictions, and the role of technology.
courses.prereqs: Completion or simultaneous enrollment in Copyright and/or Intellectual Property.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Complex Litigation in a Civil Rights Context
courses.desc: Study of the issues that frequently arise in large complex litigation involving multiple parties and multiple claims.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Federal Courts
courses.desc: Study of the subject-matter jurisdiction of federal courts. The constitutional and statutory grants of authority to federal courts to adjudicate actions arising under federal law or between parties of diverse citizenship are examined in contemporary detail and from the perspectives of history and the Constitution.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Juvenile Justice Process
courses.desc: Legal and philosophical bases of a separate juvenile justice process for crimes committed by minors. The role of counsel at each phase of the process is examined.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Child Welfare & the Law
courses.desc: Focus on the welfare and legal rights of children, especially the most at risk in society, including those in foster care and victims of crime and civil torts. Learn the substantive law of juvenile dependency and the special duties of lawyers representing children in dependency and civil cases, as well as child witnesses in criminal cases.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Children & the Law
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Examines the unique status of children in our legal system, and explores the fundamental question of how the law allocates decision-making power and responsibility for children among the child, the family and the State.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Federal Indian Law
courses.desc: Focuses on legal relations between Native American tribes and the federal and state governments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Tribal Justice
courses.desc: Concept of justice through a lens of responsibility, repair, and healing rather than punishment and exclusion. Learn from practitioners in the field.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Pretrial Skills
courses.desc: Sharpen pretrial lawyering skills through readings, discussion, role-playing exercises, videotaped simulations, and related projects. Emphasis on client interviewing, witness interviewing and depositions. Some simulations conducted outside class sessions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Legal Analysis
courses.desc: Focus on skills critical to law school success, and ultimately, bar exam success; skills include effective case reading, briefing, outlining, and exam writing. Receive individualized feedback on each of their written assignments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to second-year law students only.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Advanced Legal Writing: Analytical & Persuasive Writing
courses.desc: Develop essay writing skills typically employed on the bar examination. Receive feedback on written work and learn analytical and persuasive writing skills transferable to the bar exam and legal practice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to third-year Law students only.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Problem Solving & Analysis
courses.desc: Skills focused on the development of legal analytical and organizational methods essential to successful completion of the Performance Test component of the California Bar Exam (and other states), and, by extension, to success in the practice of law.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to third-year Law students only.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: State & Local Government Law
courses.desc: Introduction to the law governing the relations between local governments and states.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Energy Law
courses.desc: Explores the history, law, and public policy of energy regulation in the United States, emphasizing economic and environmental regulation. Competitive restructuring of the natural gas and electric utility industries is emphasized. Basic regulatory schemes for other energy sources—hydroelectric power, coal, oil, and nuclear power—are explored depending on class interest.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Renewable Energy Seminar
courses.desc: Provides a broad overview of renewable energy law and policy with a particular focus on the California policy context. Topics include renewable electricity, California’s renewable portfolio standard, and project development.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Remedies
courses.desc: Survey of modern American civil remedies law in both private and public law contexts. Topics include equitable remedies, equitable defenses, contempt power, injunctive relief, restitution, and money damages in torts and contracts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Law & Economics
courses.desc: Introduction to the economic analysis of law. Prior study of economics is not required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Environmental Law
courses.desc: Introduction to environmental law, focusing primarily on federal law. Includes coverage of major statutes including the National Environmental Policy Act, Endangered Species Act, Clean Air Act, and Clean Water Act.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: California Environmental Issues
courses.desc: The "Nation-state" of California has for many years been a national and global leader in environmental law and policy. Survey of key California environmental law and policy issues.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Environmental Practice
courses.desc: Examines underlying theory and practice in securing compliance with our major environmental laws.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Food Systems Law & the Environment
courses.desc: Explores the various legal structures surrounding the governance of our food system; we will cover environmental regulation (or lack thereof), food safety laws, trade laws, and labor laws.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Farmworkers & the Law
courses.desc: Provides an overview of California and federal laws impacting farmworkers and how such laws have been applied to regulate working conditions in agriculture.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Climate Change Law & Policy
courses.desc: Addresses the legal and public policy dimensions of climate change, perhaps the most important environmental issue of our time.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Environmental Justice
courses.desc: Introduction to the field of environmental justice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Environmental Law
courses.desc: Focus on Pacific Rim, examining factors, similarities/differences in countries environmental regulation and success of environmental law. Including information and market-based regulatory approaches; compliance and enforcement gaps; citizen and community mobilization; the role of legal institutions; variations in regulatory style.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Biodiversity Law
courses.desc: Covers the law of biodiversity, with a focus on the laws of the United States, including both science and federal, state, and local policies. Graded based on short response papers and participation in class discussions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Food Innovation Law & Policy Seminar
courses.desc: Introduction to the exciting world of new food discoveries and their relationship to food law and policy. Looks at food innovation, the transfer of food technology, and how new products move into the marketplace.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Craft Beer Law
courses.desc: Topics covered include the historical bases for alcohol regulation, the three-tier system, licensing and regulation, ABC enforcement procedures, various compliance requirements, and related legal issues that impact craft-breweries (including entity formation, and IP).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Environmental Law Seminar: Emerging Technologies & the Environment
courses.desc: Examines legal regimes that might apply to various emerging technologies and consider governance mechanisms and reforms that might enable more foresighted and participatory development and management of technology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Health Care Law
courses.desc: Examines law and policy issues in health care financing and access to health care. Draws from current events, case law, statutes, and regulations. The role of structural, institutional, and cultural inequalities in health care.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Topical Issues in Health Law
courses.desc: Focuses on four-six issues at the interface of law, medicine, bioethics, and health policy that are currently the subject of major litigation, legislation, and/or contentious debate in the domains of bioethics and public policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Public Health Law
courses.desc: Public health law, seen broadly, is the government's power and responsibility to ensure the conditions for the population's health.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to 15 students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Bioethics
courses.desc: Ethical, legal, and social issues that arise from biomedicine. Uses interdisciplinary and critical theory methods to consider the role of law on issues arising from biotechnology and science-based knowledge systems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Legal Psychology Seminar
courses.desc: Examines how psychological theory and research can be used to shape laws and policies to make them better reflect what we know empirically about how individuals process information, make decisions and behave.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Reproductive Rights, Law, & Policy
courses.desc: Addresses a variety of laws and practices that affect reproductive health and procreative decision making.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Neuroscience & the Law
courses.desc: Explore current topics at the crossroads of neuroscience and the law. Cover topics including neuroscience evidence at sentencing, brain-based lie detection, tort liability for brain injuries, brain based enhancement and the boundaries between life and death.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Representing Life Science Companies
courses.desc: Biotechnology and Pharmaceuticals are two of the fastest-growing industries in the U.S., and the legal issues that arise in connection with representing them are complex and evolving. Seminar focuses on the transactional, intellectual property, and regulatory legal issues that challenge lawyers working with clients in these industries.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Mental Health & The Courts
courses.desc: Explores how those with mental health needs interact with law enforcement and the justice system, including pre-arrest intervention, court diversion, serious crime prosecution, and re-entry after incarceration.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Health Justice
courses.desc: Examines health and health care through a social justice lens. Focuses on health risks disproportionately experienced by marginalized communities and individuals. Learning Activities Seminar 2 hour(s).
courses.details: Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Public Land & Natural Resources Law
courses.desc: Covers the legal aspects of managing national parks, national forests, national wildlife refuges, and other lands owned and managed by the federal government.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Poverty Law
courses.desc: Explore the theory and practice of law pertaining to the enactment and enforcement of laws regulating or aiding the poor and other disadvantaged persons.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Constitutional Law Seminar
courses.desc: Seminar explores in-depth selected topics or problems in constitutional law and theory. The current focus will include diverse topics including abortion rights, the development of Second Amendment jurisprudence, and other subject areas.
courses.prereqs: LAW 218 (can be concurrent) or LAW 218A (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Presidential Powers Seminar
courses.desc: Explores the Constitutional powers of the President in Article II and how they intersect with Congressional power. Emphasis on executive and legislative power, executive orders, appointment and removal powers, executive privilege and immunity, pardons, impeachment, Congressional investigations, independent and special counsels, and the 25th Amendment.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Supreme Court Simulation Seminar
courses.desc: Take on the role of Justices of, and advocates before, the Supreme Court of the United States.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): May satisfy the Advanced Writing Requirement or the Professional Skills Requirement; students must choose one.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: National Security Law
courses.desc: Examines the allocation of national security powers among the three branches of government, and the laws & policies that govern military operations, the collection & use of intelligence, homeland security, and other current national security issues.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: National Security Law: Crisis Simulation Seminar
courses.desc: Explore Constitutional allocation of national security powers among three branches of government, and the vital role lawyers play in national security decision-making. Conduct deep dives on national security law case studies.
courses.prereqs: Constitutional Law I; Public International Law (recommended).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Biotechnology Law & Policy
courses.desc: Coverage includes the regulation of biotechnology research, including restrictions on cloning and fetal stem cell research; regulation of the products of biotechnology to protect human health or the environment, including restrictions on use or distribution of genetically modified organisms; the availability and scope of intellectual property protection for biotechnology products, including genes and engineered organisms; and the international law governing access to the natural resources that provide the starting materials for biotechnology and trade in bioengineered organisms or their products.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Trade Law
courses.desc: China has become factory to the world, India its back office, and the US its information intermediary. Trade law affects goods, safety of foods, and conditions under which clothes are produced. Reviews trade regulation from the World Trade Organization to regional organizations such as NAFTA. Considers the implications for developing economies and analyze strengths and weaknesses of the current international trade order.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Information Privacy Law
courses.desc: Examine several topics that arise in field of information privacy law, with a special emphasis on law enforcement access to this information.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory Only.

courses.title: Comparative Privacy Law
courses.desc: Compares regulatory privacy framework. Core lecturing focuses on the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and how it compares with U.S. law. Core concepts include controller/processor, personal data/personal information, data subject/consumer, etc.
courses.prereqs: Recommended passing one of the IAPP certifications or Privacy Law Seminar.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Finance
courses.desc: Money makes the world go round. We will try to follow that money, learning how a framework of national and international laws and institutions regulates (or perhaps fails to regulate) its flow.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Investment Dispute Seminar
courses.desc: This seminar will examine the law of investor-State dispute resolution.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Immigration Law & Procedure
courses.desc: Surveys the history of U.S. immigration law and policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Immigration & Citizenship Law Seminar
courses.desc: Conducts a closer examination of various topics and subject matters that relate to immigration and citizenship law.
courses.prereqs: LAW 292; may be waived by the professor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Immigration Crimes
courses.desc: Every year, tens of thousands of people are charged with immigration-related crimes in the federal court system; almost all of the people prosecuted in these cases come from Spanish-speaking countries to the south of the United States. Examine the history of such immigration-related prosecutions, explores how they are currently conducted, and looks in particular at the streamlined proceedings that happen in districts along the southern border.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Humanizing Deportation
courses.desc: Focus on student's investigation, research, interviewing and client counseling skills. Review the stories in the UC Humanizing Deportation archive, research possible forms of immigration relief for deported individuals, and identify possible candidates for legal screening. After in-depth training, students travel to Tijuana, Mexico to provide know-your-rights and educational workshops with deported individuals.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Clinical Activity.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Immigration Federalism
courses.desc: Study local government laws and practices that seek to regulate the lives of immigrants living within their jurisdiction. Areas include housing, labor and employment, driving and professional licenses, health, public benefits, and policing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Public Interest Law
courses.desc: Examine issues and problems associated with providing civil legal services to persons and interests in American society that are typically unable to afford or otherwise obtain representation from the private bar.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Law & Popular Culture
courses.desc: Examines works of popular culture, films, and legal texts. Each session focuses on a particular film and its cultural implications, particular problem or problems of law, law practice, legal ethics, traditional ethics, or public policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Video Game Law
courses.desc: Video games are a force in entertainment, larger than film and music. Covers a variety of doctrines from IP to the First Amendment through landmark and recent cases, and includes practical experience developing arguments based on real disputes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
This course version is effective from, and including: Spring Semester 2027.

courses.title: Business of Professional Sports
courses.desc: Provides a basic understanding of how sports teams are legally structured; diversification of business lines, e.g., real estate, hospitality, non-profits, venture capital, marketing; role, structure, and importance of arena/facility as the modern community campfire; legal areas of focus, e.g., contracts, IP, finance, legislation, administrative law, risk management, construction; cutting edge legal issues, e.g., music license rights on social media, gambling, equal pay, eSports.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Trademark & Unfair Competition Law
courses.desc: Intensive look at selected issues in Trademark Law, including the concepts of trademarks & unfair competition, acquisition & loss of trademark rights, infringement, trademarks as speech, and international aspects of trademark protection.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Copyright
courses.desc: Thorough examination of the law of copyright, including its application to literature, music, films, television, art, computer programs, and the Internet.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Entertainment Law
courses.desc: Explore the foundational principles of Entertainment Law, as well as emerging developments in this area of law and practice. Study the application of intellectual property rights and rights of personhood (copyright, trademark, publicity, etc.) to artists/creators, famous individuals, and the industry at large, with surveys into the various sub-industries within the general category of Entertainment (music, TV, film, gaming, etc.) and the assorted laws that apply to each.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Fictional Characters & Real People
courses.desc: Celebrities and fictional characters both have a powerful hold on the human imagination and are important parts of our modern myths. Examines legal protection available for each.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Art Law
courses.desc: Selected issues in Art Law, including meaning of art, how to represent artists, copyright, publicity, first amendment rights, censorship, street art, government regulation, art markets, international protection of art and cultural property; and more.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Art & Cultural Heritage Law
courses.desc: Exploration of the law relevant to art and cultural heritage, including copyright, cultural property, and cultural heritage laws in international and comparative perspective. Studied issues include creativity, artists' moral rights, forgery, and repatriation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution
courses.desc: Introduction to a wide variety of alternative dispute resolution procedures, with an emphasis on negotiation, mediation, and arbitration. Discussion of skills/strategies, with a focus on laws/policies that affect how ADR procedures are conducted.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Federal Arbitration Act Seminar
courses.desc: Trace the development of commercial arbitration law, with a special emphasis on hot-button contemporary issues like consumer and employment arbitration, the separability doctrine, preemption of state law, and the arbitrability of statutory claims.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: International Arbitration
courses.desc: Introduction to the legal framework underpinning international arbitration--the preferred method for resolving international commercial disputes. Offers all essential doctrine as well as extensive skills training based on an actual arbitration.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: ADR & Social Entrepreneurship
courses.desc: Innovative, hands-on course delves into the intersection of alternative dispute resolution (ADR) and social entrepreneurship. Learn how ADR methods can be leveraged to address social challenges by creating impactful social enterprises.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Fieldwork 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Leadership & the Law
courses.desc: Prepare for responsible leadership and service in the roles that lawyers perform in legal practice, and as social change agents.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Trauma-Informed Lawyering
courses.desc: Obtain knowledge and skills to navigate the landscape of trauma. Explore the science of trauma, and develop strategies for working with trauma in clients, ourselves, and others.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Empirical Legal Studies
courses.desc: Learn about research design by reading important papers in the field of empirical legal studies. Complete empirical research project using originally collected data.
courses.prereqs: Law 228C or a previous undergraduate class in statistics is highly recommended
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Lessons in Law & Public Leadership
courses.desc: Three-week seminar brings California's great legislative, political, and leadership challenges of the last two decades into the classroom. Asks, what would you do, not if, but when confronted with your generation's defining challenges?
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Law, Economics & Empirical Legal Studies Seminar
courses.desc: Latest research in law and economics and empirical legal studies; five workshops with leading scholars' research papers.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Study Abroad: Ireland
courses.desc: Semester-away study abroad in Ireland at a partner university. Enhance knowledge of international legal regimes and gain global legal educational experience.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Independent Study.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Must apply and be accepted into the International Study Abroad Program.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

Learning Activities: Independent study.
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Community Education Seminar
courses.desc: Trains students to educate the community about basic legal rights and responsibilities. Students attend an initial four-hour orientation, followed by weekly seminars that will prepare students to teach in a local high school at least two times per week.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Clinical Activity.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Environmental Law Moot Court
courses.desc: During the first eight weeks of fall semester, students research and submit briefs as appellants, respondents, or third parties on a problem of environmental law that is prepared by the National Environmental Law Moot Court Board.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.

Advanced writing project may also be undertaken in connection with another course or seminar to satisfy the legal writing requirements. Number of units shall be approved by the faculty supervisor and will depend upon the scope of the writing effort.

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH).

courses.title: Languages of the World

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed LIN 050.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH).

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH).

courses.prereqs: LIN 001 or LIN 001Y or ANT 004; or upper division standing recommended.
courses.details:

General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.desc: Overview of key sociolinguistic concepts from a global perspective, focusing on language variation, language use and language policy. General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.desc: Investigation of real and putative (stereotyped) gender-linked differences in language structure and usage, with a consideration of some social and psychological consequences of such differences. Focus is on English, but other languages are also discussed.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Discourse Analysis
courses.desc: Methods of analyzing spoken and written chunks of language as they happen in various contexts, including doctor's offices, classrooms, sports arenas, news media, etc.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Applied Linguistics
courses.desc: Applications of linguistic principles and the analysis of language-related issues in the world. Exploration of a range of language-related problems including issues related to language learning and teaching to issues concerning language and gender, race, class and the media.
courses.details:

Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Concept selection, design, prototype manufacturing, initial testing, iteration, and product and process verification and validation activities. courses.details:

courses.desc: Manufacturing readiness strategies employed in the medical device and life science industries, including contract manufacturing. Post-market activities including complaint investigation and reporting, FMEA impacts, clinical trial support and closure, and product obsolescence.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Medical Device Development majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Latest technologies and practices in the medical devices industry. Business context within which companies operate in the medical devices industry. courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Medical Device Development majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Managing innovative enterprise in changing and uncertain environments. Technology forecasting and assessment, program selection and control, financial management, regulation, and ethics. Strategic management of organizations, including analysis of industries, firm resources and capabilities and corporate strategy. Strategy formulation, implementation and strategic decision-making. Firm and industry life cycles and change.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Medical Device Development majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Corporate financial policy and investment management. Capital budgeting and cost-of-capital determination. Valuation principles for investments with long-lived and risky cash-flows.  Theory of negotiation; application of theory to process of building teams to achieve business purposes. Integrative and distributive strategies of claiming value, recognizing bargaining tricks, uncovering hidden agendas, and brainstorming to extend Pareto frontier.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Medical Device Development majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

Application of simulation and optimization techniques integrated in CAD software to analyze physical phenomena such as fluid and solid mechanics in medical devices.
courses.prereqs: Introductory CAD course or prior equivalent industry experience required (SolidWorks preferred); engineering math recommended; one or more of the following recommended: transport phenomena, fluid dynamics, mechanics.
courses.details:

Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.prereqs: MDD 421; introductory course on engineering circuits or electronics required; introduction to coding recommended (Python preferred)
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).

Grade Mode: Letter.

Leveraging CAD and simulation skills to design for fabrication by rapid prototyping. Projects include enclosure design and assembly for electronic assembly.
courses.details:

courses.title: Capstone Project I: Introduction to Clinical Needs & Operations
courses.desc: Principles of medical device innovation, with exposure to hospital and clinical operations. Needs finding and needs screening based on real-world unmet needs. Identification of potential solutions based on needs refinement and operational constraints to secure topics for capstone projects.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Medical Device Development majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Capstone Project II: Product Concept Development
courses.desc: Teams apply product development, business leadership and engineering content to propose, implement, and verify a concept solution for their capstone project. Application of business and engineering principles and design theory to deliver initial prototypes that could meet client needs under operational constraints.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Medical Device Development majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Capstone Project III: Commercialization & Development Strategy
courses.desc: Develop a commercialization plan for their capstone product concept. Regulatory strategy, reimbursement options, and intellectual property protection integrated with technical feasibility assessment around focused clinical needs. Written and oral communication, and relevant professional and ethical responsibilities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Medical Device Development majors only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Genetics, Identity, & Religion
courses.desc: Effects of new understandings of genetics on how different religions configure belonging, identity, and ethics.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).
This course version is effective from, and including: Fall Quarter 2026.

Discussion of clinical cases, cellular pathology, cancer and emerging and reemerging human viral diseases including Coronaviruses, vaccines, antivirals, and use of viruses in medicine.
courses.prereqs: BIS 102 or BIS 102V or BIS 101 or BIS 101V or BIS 103 or BIS 104 or BIS 105.

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s), Extensive Writing 1 hour(s).

Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Detailed characterization of the mechanisms involved in cardiac excitation–contraction coupling, alterations that occur in heart disease and pharmacological interventions. Topics include cardiac contractile apparatus, action potential, Ca cycling, excitation–transcription coupling, cardiac inotropy, heart failure and arrhythmias.
courses.prereqs: An equivalent course in general pharmacology or physiology (example, BIM 204), or knowledge of basic pharmacology/physiology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students from the Pharmacology and Toxicology, Molecular, Cellular and Integrated Physiology, Biomedical Engineering and Clinical Research Graduate Groups; other students (including undergraduates) may be accepted upon consultation with the instructors.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.desc: Gene therapy from basic concepts to clinical applications. Topics include the human genome and genetic variation, genetic diseases, methods to manipulate gene expression, viral and non-viral delivery vectors, history and progress of gene therapy, case studies, and ethical issues.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).

courses.title: Intermediate Conducting

courses.details:

Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH).

courses.title: History of Film Music
courses.desc: Film music from silent films to movies of the past decade. How music supports and shapes film narrative and structure. Use of jazz, rock and classical music in film.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Film Viewing 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Introduction to the Music of The Beatles
courses.desc: Survey of music of The Beatles, focusing on the songs of Lennon and McCartney. Emphasis on understanding their evolution as musicians, composers and cultural figures. Discussion of their musical influences in wider cultural contexts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Listening 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: The Broadway Musical
courses.desc: Exploration of a variety of Broadway and film musicals from different time periods, and how musicals reflect and help create social reality, and the different aspects of the creative process as manifested through music, dance, scenery, and acting.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Music & Nature
courses.desc: Changing conceptions of music and nature from the 18th to 21st centuries. Relationships between musicians and global environments. Interactions between natural and musical sound. Ecology of instrument making.  Representation of nature in classical and popular music. Artistic integration of human and animal song. New music related to climate change.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Thinking Through Bollywood
courses.desc: Music in Bollywood cinema from the 1990s and early 2000s. How musical numbers (picturizations) shape filmic narratives, and reflect social, political, and cultural values in India and the diaspora.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s), Film Viewing 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC).

Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Listening.

General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); World Cultures (WC).
