courses.title: Orientation to Research in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Introduction to basic research resources pertinent to Native American subjects available in the region, including libraries, archives, museums, etc. Emphasis on learning to use documentary resources or other collections of data. Students will carry out individual projects.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; Native American Studies major or minor, or consent of instructor; NAS 001 or NAS 010 encouraged, but not required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Native American Religion & Philosophy
courses.desc: Religious and philosophical traditions of Native American/indigenous peoples of the Americas.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Oral Skills (OL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: California Indian Environmental Policy I
courses.desc: Contemporary California Indian environmental policy issues, with a focus on water, minerals, contamination, and alliance-building. Issues will be placed within historical and political context, drawing on theories of Native environmental ethics, environmental justice, and Federal Indian law.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: California Indian Environmental Policy II
courses.desc: Contemporary California Indian environmental policy issues, with a focus on planning, site protection, and collaborative structures. Issues will be placed within historical and political context, drawing on theories of Native environmental ethics, environmental justice, and Federal Indian law.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Indigenous Relationships with Nonhuman Animals
courses.desc: Deconstruction of anthropocentrism. How Indigenous relationships between human and nonhuman animals are created, maintained, and destroyed. Critiques of the Social Sciences, STEM, and Humanities’ approaches to human-nonhuman relations offered by Indigenous people, scholars, and knowledge holders.
courses.prereqs: NAS 001, NAS 005, NAS 010, or NAS 012 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH).

courses.title: Keepers of the Flame: Native American Cultural Burning & Land Stewardship in California
courses.desc: Use of fire by California Indian tribes to maintain ecosystems that sustain their economic, cultural, and spiritual well being. Guests include Native American cultural practitioners and prescribed fire professionals.
courses.prereqs: consent of instructor; course involves regular field days working with cultural burn practitioners.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 1.5 hour(s), Fieldwork.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); American Cultures, Governance, & History (ACGH); Domestic Diversity (DD).

courses.title: Indigenous Mesoamerica
courses.desc: Peoples, cultures and history of Mexico and Central America from pre-Columbian civilizations to the present. Resistance to colonial and neo-colonial rule. Maya movements in Mexico, Guatemala, and Belize, past and present.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Hemispheric Indigenous Connections
courses.desc: Indigenous worlds in motion in the Americas, 1491-present. Comparative Indigenous experiences of colonialism and neocolonialism, plus histories of resistance, cultural survival, and transnational grassroots organizing with an emphasis on environmental justice movements.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to UC Davis students.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Social Sciences (SS); Visual Literacy (VL); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Native American Women
courses.desc: Native American women's life experiences, cross-cultural comparisons of gender roles, and Native women's contemporary feminist thought. Utilizes texts from literature, social science, and autobiography/biography.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Oral Skills (OL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Native American Poetry
courses.desc: Contemporary Native American/Indigenous poetry, poets, and the practice of writing poetry. Understanding poetry from the perspective of Indigenous oral and ritual traditions and from the contemporary aesthetic/poetic practices of the selected poets.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Domestic Diversity (DD), World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Native American Poetry
courses.desc: Contemporary Native American/Indigenous poetry, poets, and the practice of writing poetry. Understanding poetry from the perspective of Indigenous oral and ritual traditions and from the contemporary aesthetic/poetic practices of the selected poets.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Domestic Diversity (DD), World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Native American Fiction
courses.desc: Study of literature through short stories, novels, and literary studies scholarship. Attention to the cultural/aesthetic/artistic trajectories of the writers. Primary focus on fiction from U.S. Native writers, but also some fiction from First Nations writers of Canada and Indigenous writers of Mexico.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit for students that have completed NAS 181A.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Domestic Diversity (DD); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE)

courses.title: Native American Non-Fiction
courses.desc: Works by or about Native American writers, including non-fiction novels, biographies and autobiographies, and selected literary studies scholars whose works help frame the study of literature. Attention to the cultural/aesthetic/artistic trajectories of the writers themselves. Primary focus on non-fiction from U.S. Native writers, but also some non-fiction from First Nations writers of Canada, and Indigenous writers of Mexico.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion  4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Domestic Diversity (DD); World Cultures (WC); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Contemporary Indigenous Literature of Mexico
courses.desc: Contemporary indigenous literature of Mexico, with a focus on the genres (poetry, fiction, drama, essay); analysis of cultural, historical, and spiritual themes, imagery, styles and performances; biographies of and influences on the Native writers themselves.
courses.prereqs: NAS 001 or NAS 010; NAS 181A or NAS 181C recommended; reading knowledge of Spanish required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Native American Literature in Performance
courses.desc: Performance of contemporary Native American literature onstage, through adaptations of selected literature as well as the creation of  original pieces.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Performance Instruction 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 4 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Oral Skills (OL); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Special Topics in Native American Literary Studies
courses.desc: Special topics drawn from Native American literature.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing and one of the following recommended: NAS 005, NAS 010, NAS 181A, NAS 181C.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Domestic Diversity (DD); Oral Skills (OL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Powwow Internship
courses.desc: Supervised internship for the annual UC Davis Powwow.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-12 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to upper division standing.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 12 unit(s) including course 189 and other internships taken in other departments and institutions.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Advanced Seminar on Sovereignty & Autonomy
courses.desc: Advanced course for NAS majors on contemporary theory and practice in Native American and Indigenous Studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Open to junior and senior NAS majors; NAS minors with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS).

courses.title: Topics in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Selected topics in Native American Studies related to indigenous knowledges and worldviews from a historical, cultural, hemispheric perspective.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when instructor and/or topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Oral Skills (OL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Apprenticeship & Internship
courses.desc: Supervised internships or elder-guided apprenticeships in community, educational, or other institutional settings in the U.S. or abroad that put into practice Native American and Indigenous concepts, cosmologies, and ways of knowing and being.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to upper division standing; dependent on intern position availability in Native American Studies or the CN Gorman Museum; priority to Native American Studies minors/majors.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated for credit when apprenticeship or institution differs, and/or with consent of supervising faculty that some novel experiential learning occurs.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Leadership Training in Native American & Indigenous Organizations
courses.desc: Supervised leadership training in Native American department, campus, and community settings, including the Native American Academic Student Success Center (NAASSC; aka, the Native "Nest")
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Conference 1-2 hour(s), Fieldwork, Project.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated up to 8 unit(s) total.
Grade Mode: P/NP only.

courses.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
courses.desc: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of faculty advisor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Independent Study 12 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Special Studies for Honors Students
courses.desc: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in the completion of a senior honors thesis or project under direction of faculty advisor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Independent Study 12 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Field Experience in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Field work with governmental and community groups, under supervision of faculty advisor and sponsor. Knowledge acquired in other courses to be applied in field work.
courses.prereqs: NAS 161; senior standing and major in Native American Studies, completion of lower division major requirements.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Fieldwork 36 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Senior Project in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Guided research project that enables student to apply the theory and research principles from major course work. Final product is to be a major senior project or thesis.
courses.prereqs: NAS 195 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; senior standing and major in Native American Studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s), Independent Study 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Community Tutoring in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Supervise tutoring in community.
courses.prereqs: Consent of major committee; upper division standing with major in Native American Studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Tutorial 3-15 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Directed group study.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for advanced undergraduates.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Basic Concepts in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Analysis of characteristics of the discipline of Native American Studies. Concentration of traditional and contemporary native scholarship and thought as well as theoretical and methodological consequences derived from application of these ideas.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 3 time(s) when instructor differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Native American Studies
courses.desc: Advanced study of selected topics or themes relevant to the field of Native American studies. Topics will be announced at the time of offering.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Leadership Skills & Strategies in California Language Documentation & Revitalization
courses.desc: Introduction to the indigenous languages of the Americas, with a focus on California; an examination of how contemporary Native communities document and revitalize their heritage languages. Learn to assist and administer language programs.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Study of Native American Languages
courses.desc: Advanced study of Native American languages. Development of proficiency in a particular language in order to incorporate language into Native American Studies research and argumentation. Engagement with theoretical perspectives on social, cultural, and structural dimensions of language to guide language study.
courses.prereqs: NAS 107 or equivalent background with a Native American language.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Practice, Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Community Development for Sovereignty & Autonomy
courses.desc: Examines a sample of contemporary indigenous communities from south, central and north America with the goal of understanding and evaluating the strategies adopted by Native American communities to develop and implement forms of sovereignty or autonomous self-management.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Native Criminality & Deviance
courses.desc: Examination of "deviance" in Native communities with focus on Native criminality in North America. Analysis of the concept of deviance from several different world views. Readings from a range of theories to incorporate varying theoretical perspective on criminality and deviance.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Public Law 83-280: Colonial Termination
courses.desc: Examination of the signature law of the Termination Era, Public Law 83-280. Discussions to include termination, societal conformity, political consent, jurisdiction, self-determination & decolonization, and colonial relationship between Native Peoples and the United States.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing, including school of law students.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Colonialism, Neoliberalism, & Indigenous Self-Determination
courses.desc: History, political economy and legacies of imperial/colonial systems. Continuities and discontinuities with corporate globalization and neoliberalism. Focus on resistance and self-determination of indigenous peoples, but with comparison to other groups.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Performance in the Americas
courses.desc: Ethnomusicological and anthropological approaches to study of public performance in the Americas. New ways of looking at music, dance, rituals and other forms of public expressive forms normally called "folklore" or "popular culture."
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed MUS 224. (Former MUS 224.).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Visual Sovereignty
courses.desc: Extensively examine the field of contemporary Native American and Indigenous photography, film and performance through research of artworks, writings by artists, theorists, and material in museum collections.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Film Viewing 2 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 2 time(s) when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Native American Art Collections & Museums
courses.desc: Research and examination of regional Native American art held in museums and other public institutions, as well as privately-held collections. Includes onsite viewing and research of museum collections and archives.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Native American Public Health: Topics & Issues
courses.desc: Introduction to Native American public health issues and contributing causal factors (including environmental justice and historical trauma); the dimensions of cultural competency in diagnosis and service provision; the structure of Native health care institutions; and debates in Native treatment modalities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Native American/Indigenous Research Methodologies
courses.desc: Introduction to advanced methodologies currently influencing research in Native American Studies and among Indigenous communities. Develop an original project and course assignments will guide them through the process of research design and implementation.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Indigenous Critique of Classic Maya Ethnographies
courses.desc: Construction of the Maya world through ethnographic writing during the present century. Deconstruction of ethnographies about the Mayans considering the modern theories and social/anthropological critiques of modern ethnographies.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Native American Literature
courses.desc: Introduction to the field of Native American Literature, creative works (fiction, poetry, memoir, personal essay), literary studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students only.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) when readings content is completely distinct from the course previously taken.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Indigenous Religious Traditions in the Americas
courses.desc: Religious/spiritual traditions, belief-systems, and world-views of Native American/indigenous peoples in the Americas. Land, ecological knowledge, sacred sites, the role of tricksters, language (revitalization), gender, ethics of representation, cultural revitalization, renewed ancient knowledge and practices, ceremonial (and daily) performance of the sacred, music, the arts, the worlds of the sacred, the rules of the sacred, freedom of religion.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Graduate student enrollment only.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) when readings content is completely distinct from the course previously taken.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnohistorical Theory & Method
courses.desc: Discussion of the ethnohistorical method; the utilization of diverse types of data, especially documentary sources, to reconstruct socio-cultural history. Particular attention to the applied area of ethnohistory in the solution of contemporary social problems.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Group Study for Graduate Students
courses.desc: Group study for graduate students.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Special Study for Graduate Students
courses.desc: Special study for graduate students.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.desc: Teaching assistant training.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: General Biology
courses.desc: Concepts and issues in biology. Emphasis on composition and structure of organisms; regulation and signaling; heredity, evolution and the interaction and interdependence among life forms and their environments. Designed for students not specializing in biology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed BIS 002A or BIS 002B or BIS 002C or BIS 010 or equivalent.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Introduction to Nematode Parasites
courses.desc: Introduction to the parasitic nematodes. Biology of nematode interactions and host responses.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to Entomology, Global Disease Biology, Molecular & Medical Microbiology, and Biochemistry & Molecular Biology majors.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Introduction to Nematology
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Relationship of nematodes to the human environment. Classification, morphology, ecology, distribution, and importance of nematodes occurring in water and soil as parasites of plants and animals.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for advanced undergraduates.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Molecular & Physiological Plant Nematology
courses.desc: Molecular biology and physiology of nematodes using Caenorhabditis elegans as a model, but with emphasis on plant-parasitic species. Plant responses to nematodes. Discussion of current literature emphasized.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ecology of Parasitic Nematodes
courses.desc: Major concepts in population and community ecology of animal- and plant-parasitic nematodes. Current advances in techniques, theory, and basic information about nematode-host dynamics, and application to management of nematode diseases.
courses.prereqs: (NEM 100 or NEM 110 or ENT 156); (EVE 101 or PLB 117).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Management of Plant-Parasitic Nematodes
courses.desc: Theory, foundation, principles and practices of nematode management. Techniques and equipment used to manage nematodes and methods used to analyze their effectiveness.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Insect Nematology & Biological Control
courses.desc: Biology of insect-parasitic nematodes, their effect on the host, and their potential as biological control agents of insect and other invertebrate pests. Application of ecological theory in classical and augmentative biological control.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Nematode Systematics & Evolution
courses.desc: Nematode diversity as revealed by morphological and molecular evidence. Laboratory experience focuses on structural features used in taxonomy. Phylogenetic relationships based on morphological and molecular data used to consider patterns of character change among taxa.
courses.prereqs: NEM 100 or NEM 110 or ENT 156; EVE 100 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Molecular Phylogenetic Analysis
courses.desc: Theory and practice of inferring phylogenetic trees using molecular sequence data. Practical techniques for obtaining sequence data, advantages and disadvantages of common approaches for inferring trees, statistical methods for comparing alternative hypotheses.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: EVE 210.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Field Nematology
courses.desc: Six-day demonstration and field study in applied nematology including diagnosis and prediction of nematode field problem strategies for control field plot design, and establishment in association with diverse California crops.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Fieldwork.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: Seminar.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Advanced Research Conference
courses.desc: Planning and results of research programs, proposals, and experiments. Discussion and critical evaluation of original research being conducted by the group. Discussion led by individual research instructors for research group.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Research
courses.desc: Research.

Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Internship in Nephrology
courses.desc: Supervised work experience in nephrology.
courses.prereqs: Upper division standing; approval of project by preceptor prior to internship.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-36 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 12 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Nephrology Research
courses.desc: Research topics in Nephrology.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Curriculum Design for Doctoring
courses.desc: Design of Doctoring curriculum for medical students in focused topic areas to be announced annually. Students design sessions, consider resource needs, and work with IORs to initiate the curriculum.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; second-year standing in School of Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Project 2 hour(s), Seminar 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/Fail only.

courses.title: Nephrology & Fluid Balance
courses.desc: Active participation in all inpatient/outpatient clinical activities, attendance at specific lectures and conferences at UC Davis Medical Center covering the field of nephrology and fluid-electrolyte disorders.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; completion of third-year medical school; completion of Medicine Core Clerkship.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Clinical Activity 4 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 10 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Honors/Pass/Fail.

courses.title: Research in Nephrology
courses.desc: Independent laboratory research on a specific problem related to biochemical or immunologic causes of renal disease and/or uremic disorders in humans or animals.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Honors/Pass/Fail.

courses.title: Elementary Human Physiology
courses.desc: Introduction to physiology for non-science majors. Includes basic cell physiology and survey of major organ systems and how they function in homeostasis and human health.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 101.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Exercise & Fitness: Principles & Practice
courses.desc: Human movement from physiological, psychological, sociological, and historical perspectives. Biology and psychology of exercise across the human lifespan.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken EXB 010 or an upper division EXB or NPB course.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: The Human Brain & Disease
courses.desc: Normal function and diseases of the human brain and nervous system. Diseases discussed include Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, leprosy, amnesia and schizophrenia. Intended for non-science majors.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit for students who have completed NPB 100, NPB 101, NPB 112, or PSC 121.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Extreme Animal Athletes
courses.desc: Overview of biomechanics, focusing on animal locomotion. Physical principles underlying traits such as speed, maneuverability, endurance, and precision. Comparisons of animals and human athletes performing similar feats, with animals often outperforming humans by a wide margin. Biomechanical concepts through hands-on exercises, problem sets, and readings from the scientific literature.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Illusions: Fooling the Brain
courses.desc: Introduction to perceptual processing in the human nervous system; illusions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: The Biology & Physiology of Aging
courses.desc: Broad examination of age-associated changes in body functions. Includes basic cell physiology, a survey of major organ systems and the age-induced alterations in system function. Some age-associated diseases will also be examined. Intended for non-science majors.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 015V.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Neuroendocrinology & Physiology of Animal Behavior Unleashed: Experiential Learning on the Ranch
courses.desc: Neurobiology, physiology, and behavior through direct engagement with animals at a working ranch. Experiential learning, real-time application of theoretical concepts, and bridging academic rigor with practical experience.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): No concurrent enrollment in ANS 001, ANS 002, ANS 041L, ANS 049, ANS 134, ANS 135, ANS 137, ANS 138, ANS 143, ANS 144, ANS 146.
Credit Limitation(s): Only two units of credit to students who have previously completed ANS 002 or ANS 106.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: The Path to Cyborgs: Introduction to Prostheses & Human Machine Interfaces
courses.desc: Interface of biology and technology. Mind-controlled prosthetic limbs, artificial organs, and implantable devices. Emphasis on basic physiological functions and how they can be replaced by devices. Suitable for majors and non-majors.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Biological Science for Social Justice
courses.desc: Broad survey of the many ways one can use the biological sciences to better the lives of others and break down barriers that have restricted social mobility.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE) or Social Sciences (SS); Domestic Diversity (DD); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Biology of Drug Addiction & Abuse
courses.desc: Broad examination of addictive substances and their use/abuse. Topics include historical perspective, physiological effects, etiology, neurobiology of addiction and the impact of drugs on contemporary society. Intended for non-science majors.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students having completed NPB 168.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Current Issues in Animal Behavior
courses.desc: The mechanisms and outcomes of sexual selection (mate choice and mate competition). Theory, current models and evidence that supports or refutes the models.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited enrollment.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Visual Impairment & Blindness: A World Wide Problem
courses.desc: Examination of various abnormalities of the eye and the important geographic and cultural factors that influence the epidemiology of those abnormalities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research Conference
courses.desc: Research findings and methods in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
courses.prereqs: NPB 099 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; lower division standing in Neurobiology, Physiology and Behavior or related biological science; NPB 099 required concurrently.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to lower division students.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: Work experience off and on campus in all subject areas offered in the Department of Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior. Internships supervised by a member of the faculty.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-36 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Directed group study.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Special Study for Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for undergraduates.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor. Lower division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Neurobiology
courses.desc: Brains and nervous systems, neurons and neural circuits. Coordination of movement. Development of nervous systems. Vision, hearing, and feature extraction by the central nervous system. The cell biology of learning and memory. Perception, cognition, and disorders of the brain.
courses.prereqs: BIS 002A; PHY 009A, PHY 009B or PHY 007A, PHY 007B recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 110B, NPB 112, NPB 160, NPB 161 or NPB 162, or NSC 221 or NSC 222.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: Neurobiology Laboratory
courses.desc: Experimental basis of neurobiology principles discussed in NPB 100. Topics include neurophysiology, sensory systems, motor systems, cellular neuroscience, cognitive neuroscience, and quantitative data analysis and modeling techniques.
courses.prereqs: NPB 100 (can be concurrent) or NPB 110B (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing/Discussion.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to Seniors.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Systemic Physiology
courses.desc: Systemic physiology with emphasis on aspects of human physiology. Functions of major organ systems, with the structure of those systems described as a basis for understanding the functions.
courses.prereqs: (BIO 002 or BIS 002A); (CHE 002B or CHE 002BH); or consent of instructor; PHY 001B or PHY 007C strongly recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 5 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 110C.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Systemic Physiology Discussion
courses.desc: Discussion and problem solving related to fundamental principles of systemic physiology as presented in NPB 101.
courses.prereqs: NPB 101 (can be concurrent) or NPB 101V (can be concurrent); consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1.50 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Systemic Physiology Laboratory
courses.desc: Selected experiments to illustrate functional characteristics of organ systems discussed in NPB 101.
courses.prereqs: ANS 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 3 hour(s), Discussion 2 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to seniors in BBIS, ACNU, BHUB, ANSC, and BNPB.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Systemic Physiology
courses.desc: Systemic physiology with emphasis on aspects of human physiology. Functions of major organ systems, with the structure of those systems described as a basis for understanding the functions.
courses.prereqs: (BIO 002 or BIS 002A); (CHE 002B or CHE 002BH); or consent of instructor; PHY 001B or PHY 007C strongly recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 5 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 110C.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Animal Behavior
courses.desc: Basic principles of behavioral organization in vertebrate and invertebrate animals. Underlying physiological and ethological mechanisms. The evolution of behavior, with special emphasis on behavior under natural conditions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 155. (Former NPB 155.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Quantitative Topics in Animal Behavior
courses.desc: Study of the quantitative concepts and exemplar models used in animal behavior.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Auto Tutorial 1.50 hour(s), Extensive Problem Solving 1.50 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cellular Physiology/Neurobiology
courses.desc: Cellular physiology with emphasis on membrane transport processes and neuronal physiology. Fundamental physical-chemical and biological mechanisms of membrane transport will be considered in relation to cytoplasmic homeostasis, communication between cells, and the cellular mechanisms of sensory and motor transduction.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 100B. (Former NPB 100B.)
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Experiments in Neurobiology, Physiology, & Behavior: Design & Execution
courses.desc: Design and execution of experiments in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Choose and design a project in consultation with the sponsoring faculty member.
courses.prereqs: (NPB 110A or NPB 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 102); NPB 199; and consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 7.50 hour(s), Discussion 0.50 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) to complete project; with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Oral Skills (OL); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Cell Signaling in Health & Disease
courses.desc: Basics of cell signaling pathways, their disruption in disease, and their current utility and future potential as therapeutic targets. Focus is on signaling pathways specific to nervous, endocrine and immune systems, and those fundamental to all cells.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Animal Behavior Laboratory
courses.desc: Hybrid course, consisting of limited in-person lectures and the rest laboratory exercises. Laboratory exercises are online, and require students to view and score videos of animal behavior in order to test behavioral hypotheses.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Web Electronic Discussion 12 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Kinesiology: Analysis & Control of Human Movement
courses.desc: Functional anatomy, motor control, and biomechanics of human movement understood in the context of body structures, basic principles of physics, and functional characteristics of muscle.
courses.prereqs: PHY 007A; PHY 007B; NPB 101 or NPB 110C recommended; CHA 101  CHA 101L (same as EXB 106  EXB 106L) or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Foundations 1: From Molecules to Individuals
courses.desc: Major concepts in cell biology with special emphasis on connections between cell biology and behavior. Includes: cellular metabolism, cellular sensing and signaling, membrane structure-function, molecular switches, electrical and chemical signaling, endocrine signaling, cell cycle and differentiation, cytoskeleton, and integrative examples.
courses.prereqs: ((BIS 002A, BIS 002B) or (BIO 001, BIO 002)); (CHE 002B or CHE 003A); PHY 007A and PHY 007B recommended; BIS 002C recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to majors in Neurobiology, Physiology and Behavior.
Credit Limitation(s): Credit limited to 3 units for students who have taken BIS 104.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Foundations 2: Neurobiology
courses.desc: Core concepts of neurobiology including single-neuron biophysics, synapses and transmitters, neuronal development, motor systems, central pattern generation, neuronal circuits, intracellular signal transduction, sensory processing, multisensory integration, autonomic nervous system, neuromodulation, learning and memory, and higher cognition and disease.
courses.prereqs: NPB 110A C- or better; PHY 007A and PHY 007B recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to declared NPB majors only.
Credit Limitation(s): Credit limited to 2 units for students who have taken NPB 100.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Foundations 3: Physiology
courses.desc: Focuses on the structure, function, and interactions of human and other animal organ systems in homeostasis and reproduction, and the response to perturbations of homeostasis; neural and endocrine signaling; skeletal muscle and movement; cardiovascular and respiratory systems; renal, digestive, immune, and reproductive physiology.
courses.prereqs: NPB 110A C- or better; PHY 007A; PHY 007B and PHY 007C recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to declared NPB majors only.
Credit Limitation(s): Only 2 units for students who have taken NPB 101.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Cardiovascular, Respiratory, & Renal Physiology
courses.desc: Intense and advanced presentation of concepts in cardiovascular, respiratory, and renal physiology including discussion of acid-base balance.
courses.prereqs: (NPB 110C or NPB 101 or NPB 101V); CHE 008B, PHY 007B and PHY 007C recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Gastrointestinal Physiology
courses.desc: Gastrointestinal anatomy and physiology. Digestion, secretion, absorption, motility, comparative physiology and pathology. Strong emphasis on neural and hormonal regulation and on cellular mechanisms of secretion and absorption.
courses.prereqs: (NPB 110C or NPB 101 or NPB 101V); BIS 105 or BIS 103 recommended, BIS 105 preferred.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Stress Physiology in Health & Disease
courses.desc: Adaptive and maladaptive physiological responses to acute and chronic stress in mammals, with emphasis on humans. Role of endocrine and autonomic nervous system in stress response. Prenatal and postnatal effects of stress on cognitive and affective development. Wellness interventions.
courses.prereqs: BIS 002A C- or better; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Avian Physiology
courses.desc: Physiology of the various systems of birds with emphasis on digestion, respiration, excretion, and endocrine systems.
courses.prereqs: ((BIS 002A, BIS 002B) or BIO 001 or BIO 002); CHE 002B.  NPB 101 or NPB 110C strongly recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Biomechanics
courses.desc: Comparative biomechanics, exploring how animals and other organisms interact with their physical environment. Animal locomotion, form and function of morphological traits, mechanical properties of biological materials, and rules for fluid flow and structural design. Biomechanical concepts through hands-on exercises, quantitative problem sets, and readings from the scientific literature.
courses.prereqs: (MAT 012 or MAT 016A or MAT 017A or MAT 019A or MAT 021A or MAT 021AH or MAT 021M); (PHY 001A or PHY 007A or PHY 009A); (BIS 002A or BIS 002B or BIS 002C or BIS 010); or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physiology of Aging & Senescence
courses.desc: Molecular and genetic basis of aging and senescence in various model organisms, from yeast to mammals. Organ and system level changes that take place as organisms age and their impact on their fitness and outcomes. The role of inflammation as a key contributor to aging. Mechanisms of common diseases of aging including: Alzheimer's, arthritis, atherosclerosis, osteoporosis. Theories of Aging. Ageism in modern society. Course is based on reading and evaluating primary literature.
courses.prereqs: NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C or ANS 100.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Physiology of Reproduction
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Physiological mechanisms related to reproduction, breeding efficiency and fertility, with special reference to domestic animals.
courses.prereqs: NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C or ANS 100.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Physiology of Reproduction Laboratory
courses.desc: Experiments on the reproductive systems of domestic animals including male and female gametes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Vertebrate Organology
courses.desc: Functional anatomy of major organ systems in vertebrates. Each system examined from cellular to gross level in fish, birds, and mammals. Emphasis on how differentiated cell types are integrated into tissues and organs to perform diverse physiological functions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: APC 100.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Neuroanatomy
courses.desc: Overview of the neuroanatomy in mammalian vertebrates, focusing on the cerebral cortex and experimental techniques. Examine changes or modifications to neural structures as a result of morphological or behavioral specializations.
courses.prereqs: NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 100 or NPB 110B or PSC 121.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: PSC 124.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Neuroanatomy Laboratory
courses.desc: Comparative neuroanatomy laboratory illustrating modern neuroanatomical techniques in determining neural connections within the mammalian brain. Includes experimentation and presentation of results.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Laboratory 6 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Pass One restricted to PSC and NPB majors; must be concurrently enrolled in NPB 124.
Cross Listing: PSC 124L.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Comparative Physiology: Endrocrinology
courses.desc: Comparison of physiological functions in the animal kingdom: animal hormones and their functions.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Physiology of the Endocrine Glands
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Advanced presentation of concepts in endocrinology with emphasis on the role of hormones in reproduction, metabolism, and disease.
courses.prereqs: (ANS 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Nature vs. Nurture: Physiological Interactions Among Genes, Nutrients & Health
courses.desc: Biochemical, physiological, genetic, and nutritional causes of important medical problems such as obesity, anorexia, heart disease and diabetes.
courses.prereqs: BIS 001A or BIS 002A or BIO 002; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Only 1 unit of credit allowed to students who have completed NPB 131.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Genes & the Brain
courses.desc: Genetic contributions to brain evolution, development and disorders. Topics include evolution of genomic programs of neurodevelopment and the role of genetics in autism, intellectual disability, and schizophrenia.
courses.prereqs: NPB 110B or NPB 100; or consent of instructor. BIS 101 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: General Immunology for Physiologists
courses.desc: Immunology for undergrads interested in physiology aimed at understanding the physiological role of immune responses. Illustrated with examples of human diseases including diabetes, allergies and asthma, and emerging diseases such as Ebola and Zika.
courses.prereqs: NPB 101 C- or better or NPB 101V C- or better or NPB 110C C- or better; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Neural Networks & Machine Learning in Biology
courses.desc: Neural networks as models of brain function and as powerful tools in machine learning. How neuroscience and machine learning have shaped each other. Applications of machine learning tools to biological research and health.
courses.prereqs: MAT 017C C or better or MAT 021B C or better; or consent of Instructor; some background in neuroscience, cognitive science or programming (any one of the three) is recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Frontiers in Physiology
courses.desc: Lectures by leading authorities and discussion of the latest research in newly emerging areas in physiology. Offered every fourth year.
courses.prereqs: NPB 100; (NPB 101 or NPB 101V); NPB 102 (can be concurrent).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: Principles of Environmental Physiology
courses.desc: Physiological aspects of interactions of organisms and environmental, cellular, system, and organismal levels. Emphasis on regulatory responses/mechanisms to thermal, pressure, gravity and light environmental variables.
courses.prereqs: NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C; BIS 102 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have completed NPB 148. (Former NPB 148.)
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Neurobiology & Pathophysiology of Mental Illness
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Comparison of the neurobiology and physiology of mental health to the pathophysiology of mental illness. Causative factors of mental illness (e.g., genetic, social, environmental) through a neurobiology and pathophysiology lens (e.g., neurotransmission, neuroimmunology, nervous system malfunction).
courses.prereqs: NPB 100 C- or better; or NPB 110B C- or better; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Advanced Animal Behavior
courses.desc: Advanced integrative survey of biological principles of behavioral organization, emphasizing historical roots, current research directions, conceptual issues and controversies. Laboratory exercises on the description and analysis of the behavior of captive and free-living animals.
courses.prereqs: NPB 102 or PSC 101; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: PSC 122.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Hormones & Behavior
courses.desc: Endocrine physiology with an emphasis on the principles of behavior. Fundamental relationships between hormones and various behaviors engaged in by the organism during its lifetime. Role of hormones in behavioral homeostasis, social behavior, reproductive behavior, parental behavior, adaptation to stress.
courses.prereqs: (NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110C); (NPB 102 or PSC 101).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Cross Listing: PSC 123.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Diabetes: Physiology & Management
courses.desc: Normal regulation of blood glucose contrasted with dysfunction in diabetes. Types of diabetes, physiological consequences of diabetes, as well as current and future medications and treatments.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Advanced Physiology of Animal/Human Disease
courses.desc: Centers on fundamental mechanisms and pathophysiological basis for animal and human diseases. Case-based and uses animal and human diseases to help exemplify the physiological consequences of organ dysfunction.
courses.prereqs: NPB 101 B+ or better or NPB 101V B+ or better or NPB 110C B+ or better; consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 2 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 35 students initially.
Cross Listing: HPH 157.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Frontiers in Behavior
courses.desc: Lectures by leading authorities and discussion of the latest research in newly emerging areas in behavioral biology. Offered every fourth year.
courses.prereqs: (NPB 100, NPB 102, (NPB 101 or NPB 101V)) or (NPB 110A,  NPB 110B,  NPB 110C).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: Neural Mechanisms of Behavior
courses.desc: Relationship between brain and behavior. Identification and analysis of the relevant neural circuits involved. Examples of systems to be considered are birdsong, locomotion, echolocation.
courses.prereqs: NPB 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V or NPB 110B.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Systems Neuroscience
courses.desc: Concepts and techniques in systems neuroscience: e.g., measuring and manipulating neural activity, structure of neocortex, sensory processing, motor control, storage of information, neural codes, neural mechanisms underlying cognitive functions.
courses.prereqs: NPB 100 or NPB 110B; or equivalent basic neuroscience training with consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Neurobiology of Speech Perception
courses.desc: Interdisciplinary approach to speech perception with emphasis on functional neuroanatomy and behavior. Topics include auditory processing in time and space, intelligibility in noisy environments, visual speech, evolution of vocal communication, models of speech perception, development, and hearing impairment.
courses.prereqs: NPB 110B or NPB 100 or NPB 101 or NPB 101V; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Math Tools for Neuroscience
courses.desc: Introduction to mathematics techniques used in neuroscience. Applications to neuroscience of differential equations, linear algebra, Fourier transforms, correlation and convolution, and probability theory.
courses.prereqs: (NPB 100 or NPB 110B); (MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C) or (MAT 017A, MAT 017B, MAT 017C) or (MAT 021A, MAT 021B, MAT 021C); or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Computational Neuroscience
courses.desc: Mathematical models and data analysis techniques used to describe computations performed by nervous systems. Lecture topics include single neuron biophysics, neural coding, network dynamics, memory, plasticity, and learning. Lab topics include programming mathematical models and data analysis techniques in MATLAB.
courses.prereqs: (NPB 100 or NPB 110B); (MAT 016A, MAT 016B, MAT 016C) or (MAT 017A, MAT 017B, MAT 017C) or (MAT 019A, MAT 019B, MAT 019C) or (MAT 021A, MAT 021B, MAT 021C); or consent of instructor; PHY 007A, PHY 007B or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Lecture/Lab 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Neurobiology of Addictive Drugs
courses.desc: Neurobiological basis for the effects and mechanisms of action of drugs with addictive potential, including opiates (morphine, heroin, methadone), amphetamines, cocaine, nicotine, marijuana (cannabinoids), alcohol, caffeine, and mind-altering drugs such as LSD and antidepressants.
courses.prereqs: NPB 100 or NPB 110B or NPB 110C or NPB 101 or NPB 101V; or equivalents.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Frontiers in Neurobiology
courses.desc: Lectures by leading authorities and discussion of the latest research in newly emerging areas in neurobiology. Offered every fourth year.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Quantitative Literacy (QL).

courses.title: Physiology of Neuroimmune Interactions
courses.desc: Explores the complex interactions of the nervous and immune systems, and examine how the systems function together to serve homeostasis, behavior, and disease (such as Alzheimer's, autism, and multiple sclerosis).
courses.prereqs: (BIS 002A or BIO 002); (NPB 012 (can be concurrent) or NPB 100 (can be concurrent) or NPB 110B (can be concurrent)); or consent of instructor; completion of PMI 126 or MMI 188 recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Neurobiology of Brain Disorders
courses.desc: Examination of brain disorders from a basic science perspective to gain insights into the mechanisms of their action. Genetic, molecular, cellular, circuit, and environmental basis of a variety of brain disorders. How insights about underlying mechanisms may lead to the development of improved therapies.
courses.prereqs: NPB 110B or NPB 100; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Research Conference in Animal Behavior
courses.desc: Research methods and findings on current topics in animal behavior, delivered by experts in the field and PhD students in the UC Davis Animal Behavior Graduate Group. Current research trends in the field of Animal Behavior, including both basic and applied areas of behavior.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Conference 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to undergraduate students.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: P/NP only.
This course version is effective from, and including: Winter Quarter 2027.

courses.title: Research Conference
courses.desc: Research findings and methods in neurobiology, physiology, and/or behavior. Presentation and discussion of research by faculty and students.
courses.prereqs: NPB 199 (can be concurrent); and consent of instructor; upper division standing in Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior or related biological science; NPB 199 required concurrently.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
