Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate students.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.desc: Teaching assistant training practicum.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 3-20 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Research
courses.desc: Research.
courses.prereqs: First-, second- and third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-15 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 6 time(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Professional & Clinical Skills — Y1
courses.desc: Outline expectations and skill set required to participate successfully in the DVM curriculum as well as providing learning opportunity in communication, team-building, leadership, conflict management, stress management, critical thinking, professional behaviors, history taking, physical examination skills and medical record keeping.
courses.prereqs: First-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Basic Foundations
courses.desc: Essential basic information regarding histology, general pathology, biochemistry, pharmacology and population health that is foundational to all blocks.
courses.prereqs: First-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Heme/Lymph/Coag
courses.desc: The lexicon, morphology, production, structure and function of peripheral blood cells, their bone marrow precursors and the lymphoid system, the process and regulation of hemostasis, and the laboratory evaluation of all of these in health and disease.
courses.prereqs: First-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Musculoskeletal
courses.desc: Anatomy, histology, and physiology necessary for understanding form and function of the bones, joints, muscles, and tendons in producing locomotion; and the pathologic processes that produce typical responses to injury of musculoskeletal structures in domestic animals.
courses.prereqs: First-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Neuroscience/Senses/Behavior
courses.desc: Establish a basis for clinical neurology, ophthalmology, and behavior by providing an integrated study of normal neurobiology, neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, neuropathology, neurpharmacology, neurotoxicology, ophthalmology and behavior.
courses.prereqs: First-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Gastrointestinal/Metabolism
courses.desc: Examine interrelatedness and functions of the organs associated with the gastrointestinal tract. Applied problems in pharmacology, physical examination, diagnostic testing, and imaging are used to reinforce a basic understanding of organ anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, and nutrition/metabolism.
courses.prereqs: First-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Pharmacology/Nutrition/Toxicology
courses.desc: Basic principles of nutrition and toxicology as well as pathophysiologic changes, diagnostic procedures and treatments of nutritional diseases and intoxications of domestic animals and wildlife. Incorporate case examples and directed self-learning to reinforce important concepts.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; first-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Connections — Y1
courses.desc: Integrate basic and preclinical material working with senior student in a clinical environment.
courses.prereqs: First-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Clinical Activity 15 hour(s).
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Cardiology/Respiratory
courses.desc: Normal cardiovascular and respiratory system biology and the integrated response of those systems to injury or disease.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Renal/Urinary
courses.desc: Examine and explore the normal morphology (gross and microscopic), physiology, pathology and imaging of the upper and lower urinary tract in multiple species.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Endocrinology/Reproduction
courses.desc: Anatomy and histology of endocrine glands and reproductive systems in males and females. Understand the physiology and pathology at the molecular, cellular and organismal level.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Skin
courses.desc: Structure and function of the skin and specialized keratinized structures in veterinary species. Review mechanisms by which skin responds to perturbations and discuss wound healing and skin pathology.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Oncology
courses.desc: Basic mechanisms, etiology, causes and the approach to diagnosis and treatment of cancer with emphasis on veterinary patients.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Immunology/Infectious Disease
courses.desc: Integrate immunology, microbiology, virology, parasitology of common infectious, zoonotic and foreign animal diseases.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Population Health
courses.desc: Principles of evidence-based medicine, study design and inference, and disease transmission in populations. Topics include biostatistics, outbreak investigation and response, diagnostic tests, vaccine strategies, food safety, foreign animal diseases, and impact of environmental health on animals and humans.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Clinical Foundations
courses.desc: Essential concepts that are shared across year three blocks to include foundational material in anesthesia, surgery and emergency medicine with cases that include interpretation of clinical pathology and imaging.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Connections — Y2
courses.desc: Integrate basic and preclinical material working with a senior student in a clinical environment.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Clinical Activity 15 hour(s).
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Professional & Clinical Skills — Y2
courses.desc: Continue to build on foundations from freshman year in communication, history-taking, client interactions, team-building, conflict and stress management and professional behaviors.
courses.prereqs: Second-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Core Stream
courses.desc: Longitudinal stream to include law, ethics, regulatory medicine, business, communication and disaster medicine.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Anesthesia & Surgical Stream
courses.desc: Introduction to surgical anatomy, operative and anesthetic skills.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Comparative Stream I
courses.desc: Approach commonly encountered diseases and medical problems across multiple species. Development of problem-solving skills related to the medical problems of all species from the level of individual animals to groups/herds/populations.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Comparative Stream II
courses.desc: Approach commonly encountered diseases and medical problems across multiple species. Development of problem-solving skills related to the medical problems of all species from the level of individual animals to groups/herds/populations.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Comparative Stream III
courses.desc: Approach commonly encountered diseases and medical problems across multiple species. Development of problem-solving skills related to the medical problems of all species from the level of individual animals to groups/herds/populations.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Small Animal Stream I
courses.desc: Clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, and the medical and surgical approaches to the infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic and ophthalmologic diseases of small animals.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Small Animal Stream II
courses.desc: Clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, and the medical and surgical approaches to the dermatologic, dental, and gastrointestinal diseases of small animals as well as preventative medicine and nutrition.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Small Animal Stream III
courses.desc: Clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, and the medical and surgical approaches to the cardiorespiratory, endocrine, and urinary medicine as well as diagnosis and therapy of oncologic diseases in small animals. Introduction to companion, avian, and exotic pet medicine and surgery.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Large Animal Stream I
courses.desc: Fundamentals of entry level large animal medicine and surgery to promote development of problem-solving skills for diagnosis, treatment and control of various disease conditions.
courses.prereqs: Third- and/or fourth-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Large Animal Stream II
courses.desc: Continuation of fundamentals of entry level large animal medicine and surgery to promote development of problem-solving skills for diagnosis, treatment and control of various disease conditions.
courses.prereqs: Third- and/or fourth-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Large Animal Stream—Equine Emphasis
courses.desc: Fundamental and advanced levels of equine medicine, surgery, lameness and reproduction. Focus on management of individual equids.
courses.prereqs: Third- and/or fourth-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Large Animal Stream—Livestock Emphasis
courses.desc: Fundamental and advanced levels of livestock medicine and surgery of individual animals and population health. Focus on all livestock species including cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and poultry.
courses.prereqs: Third- and/or fourth-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Large Animal Stream—Zoological Medicine Emphasis
courses.desc: Taxon- and topic-based approach to learning zoological medicine. Anatomy, physiology, nutrition, management, anesthesia, medicine, surgery and pathology on non-domestic free-ranging and captive species.
courses.prereqs: Third- and/or fourth-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Companion Small Mammals
courses.desc: Fundamental understanding of the etiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, treatment, prevention, and control of medical diseases of companion small exotic mammals.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Reptile & Avian Health
courses.desc: Organized by organ systems to present reptile and avian health issues. Overview of applied anatomy, physiology and clinical pathology of common species will be provided through laboratory opportunities and discussion of common diseases and treatments.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Poultry
courses.desc: Introduction to practical poultry medicine. Gross pathology, biosecurity and basic diagnostic tests. Visits to hatcheries, broiler, layer and turkey farms.
courses.prereqs: Third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Laboratory Animal
courses.desc: Basics of laboratory animal medicine including diseases, medicine, and surgery and comparative biology of the most common species and introduction to regulations. Combination of lecture, wet labs, and projects.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; third-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 2-18 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Business & Communication
courses.desc: Develop professional communication and business skills that are directly applicable in veterinary clinical practice by actively participating in a wide variety of interactive learning opportunities.
courses.prereqs: Third- and fourth year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1.50 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Clinical Pathology
courses.desc: Application of problem-solving and microscopy skills to laboratory data and laboratory specimens. Sections  to include hematology, immunology, body fluids, exfoliative cytology, urinalysis, microbiology and clinical chemistry data and interpretation.
courses.prereqs: Third- and fourth year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1.50 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Skills & Hospital Operations
courses.desc: Development of advanced clinical skills using skills learned in years 1–3 of the DVM curriculum as a foundation. Detailed orientation to the VMTH and VMACS, with a focus on global hospital operations that will prepare students for case management in year 4 of the DVM curriculum and for clinical practice following graduation. Some evenings and weekends required.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; third- and fourth-year standing in the School of Veterinary Medicine.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Clinical Activity 10 hour(s).
Grade Mode: S/U only.

courses.title: Internship
courses.desc: Internship experience off and on campus in the subject of veterinary science.  Internships are supervised by a member of the faculty.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3 to 36 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated for credit.

Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Methods of Quantitative Research
courses.desc: Principles of study design, examination of measurement, survey research methods and multivariate analysis. Stresses actual practice of techniques. Carry out quantitative data analysis using packaged computer programs.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 8 unit(s) with instructor approval.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Topics in Advanced Quanitative Methods in Social Science
courses.desc: Analysis of the logic and application of an advanced statistical model; the particular model chosen may vary. Emphasis on the model's assumptions, its strengths and weaknesses, its application for social science inquiry, and the relationship between methods and social theory.
courses.prereqs: SOC 206; or the equivalent and graduate standing; major graduate students.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 12 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Economy, Polity, & Society
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Introduces students to topics and selected issues in the related fields of economic and political sociology and political economy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students in sociology & related disciplines.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Deviance, Law, & Social Control
courses.desc: Report and discussions of literature on selected forms of deviance in relation to law and formal social control. Agency contacts and exploratory research projects.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sociology of Education
courses.desc: Overview of sociological theories accounting for the form, role, and evolution of educational systems. Emphasis on empirical research on education and social stratification and application to educational policy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate students or consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Cultural Sociology
courses.desc: Explores the varied ways in which culture is understood in the social sciences and the research questions that follow from contrasting viewpoints. The approach is historically informed and focused on changing cultural forms in relation to industrialization and post-modernism.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sociological Social Psychology
courses.desc: Advanced study of the varying approaches, methods, issues and topical concerns of sociological social psychology. Analysis of central and representative historical and contemporary works.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sociology of Reproduction
courses.desc: Recent social science scholarship in such areas as teenage pregnancy, family planning, abortion, adoption, AIDS, and new reproductive technologies; focus on the current situation in the United States.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ethnic (Race) Relations
courses.desc: Advanced study of the determinants of ethnic groupings and their interrelationships. Major theme will be the patterns of ethnic stratification and causes of ethnic conflict. Specific focus upon dominance and resistance to dominance. Influence of social science research.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Gender, Culture, & Local/Global Transformation
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Focus on critical approach to women and development; analyze local transformations with global connections within specific cultural contexts. Covers theory, methodological issues, and relationship between theory and practice.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Gender, Family, & Society
courses.desc: Major theoretical traditions and concerns in family sociology and sociology of gender. Analysis of selected classical and contemporary works representative of functionalist, Marxist, psychoanalytic, feminist and critical theoretical approaches to these subjects; e.g., Engels, Parsons, Freud, Horkheimer, Goode, Lasch, Mitchell. Emphasis on macro and historical questions.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Methodologies of Sociohistorical Inquires
courses.desc: Introduction to comparative and case methodological approaches to sociohistorical inquiry, theoretical and practical issues, and substantive research agendas ranging from study of large-scale social transformations to close microhistories, including research agendas being developed by students in the course.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor not required for graduate students in the Social Sciences Division or the Humanities, Arts, and Cultural Studies Division; required for undergraduates and students from other divisions or colleges.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Urban Society
courses.desc: Broad overview of the issues and concerns of the field of urban sociology. Special emphasis on the human experience of urban living in contemporary, cross-cultural or historical settings.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Developing Societies
courses.desc: Analysis of social and economic problems of developing societies from the standpoint of theory and research on modernization and underdevelopment. Nature of third world dependency and interdependence in the global political economy.
courses.prereqs: Graduate student status or familiarity with problems of developing societies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper, Project.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Social Movements
courses.desc: Analysis of current issues in and contributions to the study of collective behavior and social movements; particular focus upon the strategies and tactics of social movements.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sociology of Health & Illness
courses.desc: Sociological perspectives and methods on the study of health and illness. Select topics for supervised research. Research paper required.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate or professional students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Sociology of Law
courses.desc: Analysis of the nature of the legal process and its impact on social behavior. Will consider (1) nature and functions of law, (2) the organization and administration of law, and (3) the capacity of law to affect social behavior.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Classical Sociological Theory
courses.desc: Introduces graduate students to the work of the main classical thinkers in the tradition of social theory, such as Marx, Durkheim, Weber, Simmel, Freud, G.H. Mead, and Parsons, locating them within the historical, cultural, and philosophical milieu in which their ideas originated.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Theory in Contemporary Sociology
courses.desc: Explores the uses of theories in contemporary sociology by tracing their connections with classical sociological writings and their relations to broader theoretical concerns of contemporary social thought, with particular emphasis on relevance to the current historical, cultural and social milieu.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Social Demography
courses.desc: How social institutions affect and are affected by the level and variation of mortality, migration, and fertility. Special emphases on the determinants of fertility-related attitudes and behavior, on less-developed countries, and on contemporary empirical studies.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Organizations & Institutions
courses.desc: Theory of formal organizations and bureaucracy. Methods of research in organizational and institutional studies. Historical and comparative analysis of political, religious, educational, military, and economic structure.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 4 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Integrative Research Practicum
courses.desc: Continuing training in field, quantitative, and/or comparative-historical methods. Emphasis on students' research projects and applications of principles related to research design, concept and theory construction causality and interpretation, and data and measurement. Completion of research paper is required.
courses.prereqs: SOC 207A; SOC 242A; SOC 292A; consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 6 hour(s), Extensive Writing, Term Paper.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to Sociology graduate students only.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Seminar
courses.desc: Seminar.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Field Research
courses.desc: Introduction to the logic, methods, and practices of field research, with particular emphasis on the ethnographic tradition of participant observation. Interviewing and other qualitative techniques will also be covered. Students will develop original research projects based on their own fieldwork.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing in Sociology or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Fieldwork.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Proseminar in Sociology
courses.desc: Introduction to graduate training in sociology. A seminar designed to introduce students entering graduate work in the department to its ongoing research activities.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Special Topics Seminar
courses.desc: Research topics in Sociology. Specific topic will vary according to faculty interest and student demand.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:

Repeat Credit: May be repeated when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: The Teaching of Sociology
courses.desc: Practical instruction in teaching methods for qualitative and quantitative courses. Pedagogical issues involved in critical sociological analysis.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing; required for first-time teaching assistants.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: The Teaching of Sociology
courses.desc: Practical instruction in devising course syllabi, lectures and assignments for Associate-Instructors and others interested in college teaching. Discussion of pedagogical methods of teaching qualitative and quantitative courses.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 1 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Research Paper Workshop
courses.desc: A workshop to assist advanced graduate students in the preparation of an original research paper. Students present their research papers and discuss issues in theory, research design, data, empirical inference, and verbal and written presentation of a professional research paper.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Workshop 1.50 hour(s), Discussion 0.50 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Soils in Our Environment
courses.desc: Soils in our global ecosystem; soils as natural bodies formed by interactive environmental processes; soil response to use and management; sustainable use of soil resources; role of soils in  agricultural and environmental issues; role of soils in our daily lives.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Independent Study.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 90 students.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Soil Science Internship
courses.desc: Work experience off and on campus in soil science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; lower division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-36 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.

courses.title: Principles of Soil Science
courses.desc: Soil as part of natural and managed ecosystems and landscapes. Solid, liquid, and gas phases and their interactions in the soil. Water, gas and heat movement in soil. Soil biology. Plant nutrient acquisition and use. Soil development, management and use.
courses.prereqs: College-level courses in each of chemistry, physics, biology, and geology recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Term Paper.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Environmental Soil Chemistry
courses.desc: Soil chemistry processes related to the fate and transport of contaminants in soil. Soil minerals, natural organic matter, surface charge, soil solution chemistry, redox reactions in soil, and sorption of inorganic and organic contaminants.
courses.prereqs: General chemistry; SSC 100 or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Field Studies of Soils in California Ecosystems
courses.desc: Field-based studies of soils in California ecosystems, away from campus, throughout California. Emphasis on description and classification of soils; relationships among soils, vegetation, geology, and climate; physical, chemical, and biological processes in soils on the landscape; and the role of soils in land use.
courses.prereqs: SSC 100 and SSC 120 or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Fieldwork.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to a minimum of 10 students; maximum of 24.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Soil Physics
courses.desc: Physical properties of soil. Principles of water, gas, heat, and solute movement in soil with selected examples related to soil and water management. Influence of soil properties on transfer processes.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Sustainable Nutrient  Management
courses.desc: Availability of nutrients in organic and conventional agricultural, vineyard, orchard and plantation forest soils; management of fertilizers, cover crops, compost, sewage sludge and manures for crop production and to prevent loss to the environment is emphasized.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Soil Microbiology
courses.desc: Major groups of microorganisms in soil, their interrelationships, and their responses to environmental variables. Role of microorganisms in cycling of nutrients. Plant-microbe relationships. Transformations of organic and inorganic pollutants.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Soil Ecology
courses.desc: Overview of living constituents of soils, their interactions, importance to, and impact on biogeochemical cycles, decomposition, and soil properties. Practical applications of soil biological diversity are emphasized.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 2 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE).

courses.title: Soils in Land Use & the Environment
courses.desc: Soils are considered as elements in land use planning and environmental quality. Topics include: soil survey reports, remote sensing, land capability classification, soil erosion/conservation, waste disposal on soils and soil reclamation. One one-day field trip.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; SSC 100 or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL).

courses.title: Soil Genesis, Morphology, & Classification
courses.desc: Recognition and description of soils; chemical, biological and physical processes of soil formation. Factors of soil formation. Interactions of soils with diverse ecosystems. Introduction to soil classification. Practice using soil taxonomy. Practical experience describing soil properties in the field.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 4 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Science & Engineering (SE); Quantitative Literacy (QL); Scientific Literacy (SL); Visual Literacy (VL).

courses.title: Soil Science Internship
courses.desc: Work experience off and on campus in soil science. Internship supervised by a member of the faculty.

courses.title: Topics in Advanced Soil Chemistry
courses.desc: Reviews of current research in soil chemistry. Topics include double layer theory; clay mineral and oxide surface chemistry; adsorption on soil surfaces; speciation and modeling of solution ions; solubility and mineral stability diagrams.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; general chemistry; SSC 100 or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion 1 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to 18 students.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) when topic differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Field Studies of Soils in California Ecosystems
courses.desc: Field-based soil studies in California ecosystems. Description and classification of soils; relationships among soils, vegetation, geology, and climate; physical, chemical, and biological processes; their role in land use. Similar to SSC 105; requires additional work for graduate credit.
courses.prereqs: SSC 100 and SSC 120 or equivalent recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Fieldwork 50 hour(s), Discussion 15 hour(s), Lecture 5 hour(s).
Enrollment Restriction(s): Limited to 24 students.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s) when geographic locale differs.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Soil-Plant Interrelationships
courses.desc: Plant needs, occurrence and reactions of water and mineral nutrients in soils; root systems and their growth in soils; mass flow and diffusion mechanisms in nutrient acquisition; models relating nutrient uptake to soil and plant characteristics; nutrient assimilation and crop quality.
courses.prereqs: SSC 100; PLB 111; or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Advanced Soil Microbiology
courses.desc: Microbial metabolism of organic chemicals in soil, both natural and xenobiotic. Decomposition of organic matter. Kinetics of microbial processes in soil.
courses.prereqs: CHE 008A; CHE 008B; SSC 111; BIS 102, BIS 103 or an equivalent course recommended.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Ecosystem Biogeochemistry
courses.desc: Multidisciplinary analysis of energy and nutrient transfers within terrestrial ecosystems. Examination of processes and inter- and intra-system interactions between the atmosphere, biosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere. Laboratory section uses biogeochemical simulation models to examine case studies.
courses.prereqs: Introductory courses in ecology/biology and soils recommended; undergraduates accepted with consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s), Discussion/Laboratory 2 hour(s).
Cross Listing: ECL 219.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Pedology
courses.desc: Topics selected from studies of soil-forming processes, soil-geomorphic relations, mineral weathering, new developments in soil classification, and development of pedologic theory. Topics vary from year to year.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 1 time(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Global Carbon Cycle
courses.desc: Global carbon cycle from Phanerozoic epoch to modern times. Examination of long and short-term carbon cycles. Transfer of carbon among ocean, land and life with emphasis on humic substance formation, methods of characterization, reactions with organics and soil carbon stabilization.
courses.prereqs: MAT 016A; MAT 016B; CHE 008A; CHE 008B; SSC 100; or the equivalent of SSC 100.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Soil Minerals in the Environment
courses.desc: Describing and identifying soil minerals commonly found in the Critical Zone; Origin, occurrence, and properties of soil minerals in relation to chemical, pedologic, and environmental conditions. Research applications of mineral identification techniques including X-ray diffraction, electron microprobe analysis, and electron microscopy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Web Virtual Lecture 4 hour(s), Laboratory 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

Interactive session to review history, physical findings and case management. Perform H&P.

Grade Mode: Honors/Pass/Fail.

Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Science & Engineering (SE); Scientific Literacy (SL); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Digital Rhetorics
courses.desc: Rhetorical concepts and processes applied to digital environments with an emphasis on user experience, universal design, and writing for networked publics. Application of rhetorical theory as both an analytic method and as a heuristic for the production of digital texts and performances.
courses.prereqs: UWP 010 C- or better; UWP 015 C- or better.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 1 hour(s), Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Rhetorics & Culture
courses.desc: Relationship between written communication and cultural practices, epistemologies, and genres. Producing texts for different professional and community writing scenarios that leverage cultural rhetoric strategies.
courses.prereqs: UWP 010 C- or better; UWP 015 C- or better.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s); Discussion 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Capstone Portfolio Seminar
courses.desc: Capstone course for majors. Synthesis and application of  rhetorical concepts learned in the major. Development of professional digital and print portfolio for graduate school and career applications.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to majors who have completed 135 units.
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Internship in Writing
courses.desc: Internships in fields where students can practice their skills.
courses.prereqs: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or ENL 003 or ENL 003V or equivalent course; consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Internship 3-36 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 12 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH).

courses.title: Tutoring in Writing
courses.desc: Tutoring one-on-one or leading small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with a writing course.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Tutorial 1-5 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 10 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH).

courses.title: Community Tutoring in Writing
courses.desc: Field experience, with individuals or in K-12 classroom instruction, focusing on reading- and writing-to-learn strategies in any subject area.
courses.prereqs: Consent of instructor; upper division standing.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Tutorial 1-4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 10 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH).

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Directed group study. May be taught abroad.
courses.prereqs: UWP 001 or UWP 001V or UWP 001Y or ENL 003 or ENL 003V or equivalent course; consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-5 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated 10 unit(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Special Study for Advanced Undergraduates
courses.desc: Special study for advanced undergraduates. May be taught abroad.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-5 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Pass/No Pass only.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH); Writing Experience (WE).

courses.title: Rhetorical Approaches to Genre Study
courses.desc: Using genre theory and methods of analysis to understand and prepare to do research on different types of writing in varying academic and professional contexts. Emphasis on problems in organizational, professional, and/or interdisciplinary communication.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: English for International/ESL Graduate Students
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Multi-skills ESL course designed to help international/ESL students improve their English language skills for successful academic study. Emphasis on writing, speaking, listening, reading, and academic culture.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken LIN 025.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Writing for International Graduate Students
courses.desc: This version has ended; see updated course, below.Focuses on writing needed for academic work, including summaries, critiques, research & grant proposals, memos, resumes, and research papers. Includes a review of grammar needed for writing and some focus on reading skills and American vocabulary and idioms.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken LIN 026.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Writing Assessment
courses.desc: Examines key testing and measurement concepts; the history of writing assessment; and relationships among writing tests and methods of teaching writing; the impacts of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), and how educational policies both drive and respond to writing assessments.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Writing Program Administration
courses.desc: Theories, models, and procedures of writing programs, primarily in higher education. Developmental, first-year, and advanced writing programs, writing centers, writing-across-the-curriculum programs, writing minors and majors, and graduate programs in rhetoric and composition.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Theory & Research in Response to Student Writing
courses.desc: Intensive focus on the critical topic of response or feedback to student writers. Coverage of philosophy, theory, and empirical research on teacher written feedback, teacher-student writing conferences, peer response, and error correction.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing, Extensive Writing/Discussion, Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Literacy & Technology
courses.desc: Examines how the physical qualities of texts offer different affordances during production and reception; grounds these discussions in the development of literacy practices and writing technologies from ancient to contemporary; creates frameworks for research into literacy, teaching, and textual technologies.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Second Language Writing
courses.desc: Traces the history of second language writing theory and research on second language writers in a variety of academic and professional contexts. Emphasis on writer characteristics, texts, and contexts.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing, Project.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Restricted to graduate standing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Introduction to Rhetorical Traditions: Histories, Theories, & Practices
courses.desc: Rhetorical traditions from around the world--surveys of classical Western rhetoric as well as rhetoric before and beyond them--with an emphasis on the rhetorical histories, theories and practices developed as a result.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Journal Editing Workshop: Writing on the Edge
courses.desc: Reading and critiquing manuscript submissions. Discussing relevant work in the field of writing studies. Applying principles of professional editing. Developmental editing, copy-editing, and typesetting of accepted manuscripts. Soliciting articles and communicating with contributors. Students encouraged to enroll both quarters.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 2 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Teaching Writing in Community Colleges
courses.desc: Key findings and practices from developmental writing research to inform curriculum design and pedagogical practices. History of U.S. higher education general education writing instruction to prepare students as community college professionals (researchers, administrators, faculty, etc.).
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.desc: Directed group study.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-5 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Individual Study
courses.desc: Individual study.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Workshop 1-12 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Theory & Practice of Teaching University-Level Composition
courses.desc: Examination of current theories and practices in teaching of writing. Practical application to undergraduate writing courses. Emphasis on designing assignments and class sequences, and responding to student writing. Examination of impact of cultural, technological and theoretical changes on composition pedagogy.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s), Extensive Writing.
Enrollment Restriction(s): Open to graduate students teaching UWP 001 in the fall quarter following this course.
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Oral English for ESL Students
courses.desc: Intensive work in oral English for non-native English-speaking students, particularly international student teaching assistants, to increase fluency, accuracy, and use of appropriate discourse strategies in academic settings; e.g., seminar, discussion, laboratory.
courses.prereqs: Open only to non-native speakers of English with priority enrollment to international student teaching assistants; completion of any required ESL courses or consent of instructor.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated with consent of instructor.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Teaching Expository Writing
courses.desc: Discussion of problems related to teaching expository writing at the university level, with special emphasis on teaching reading and writing skills and responding to student papers.
courses.prereqs: UWP 390; graduate standing; appointment as Teaching Assistant in the Composition Program; or the equivalent of UWP 390.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Discussion 2 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Theory & Practice of Teaching Writing Across the Curriculum
courses.desc: Professional development in the teaching of writing for TAs across disciplines, including theories of writing, assignment design, responding and grading, and supporting multilingual writers. Supports TAs in their current contexts and prepares them to teach writing as future faculty.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 3 hour(s), Conference 1 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory Only.

courses.title: Teaching Multilingual Writers
courses.desc: Preparing teachers of university-level second language writers, whether in composition courses or courses in other disciplines with a substantial writing component. Suitable for graduate students and advanced undergraduates.
courses.prereqs: Graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing; recommended: UWP 390, LIN 1, ENL 106/LIN 106/UWP 106.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Seminar 3 hour(s).
Grade Mode: Letter.

courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training Practicum
courses.desc: Teaching assistant training practicum.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Variable 1-4 hour(s).
Repeat Credit: May be repeated.
Grade Mode: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

courses.title: Elementary Urdu
courses.desc: Introduction to conversation, word structure, and literacy in the Urdu form of Hindi/Urdu using the Nastaʿliq script in the context of the shared culture of Hindi/Urdu.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 5 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken HIN 001.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Elementary Urdu
courses.desc: Introduction to conversation, vocabulary, and sentence structure in the Urdu form of Hindi/Urdu using the Nastaʿliq script in the context of the shared culture of Hindi/Urdu. Emphasis on conversation, vocabulary, and sentence structure.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 5 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken HIN 002.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.title: Elementary Urdu
courses.desc: Introduction to making presentations and writing compositions in the Urdu form of Hindi/Urdu using the Nasta’liq script in the context of the shared culture of Hindi/Urdu. Emphasis on short student presentations and compositions in Urdu. Includes an introduction to the Hindi form of Hindi/Urdu using the Devanagari script at the elementary level.
courses.details:
Learning Activities: Lecture/Discussion 5 hour(s).
Credit Limitation(s): Not open for credit to students who have taken HIN 003.
Grade Mode: Letter.
General Education: Arts & Humanities (AH) or Social Sciences (SS); World Cultures (WC).

courses.desc: Tutoring in undergraduate courses, including leadership in small voluntary discussion groups affiliated with departmental courses.
